diagnostics.finding: Damaged tire, loose/missing wheel nuts, wobble, severe grinding or impaired control
diagnostics.meaning: There is a condition that can make further driving unsafe.
diagnostics.next: Keep the car parked; arrange inspection and suitable transport. Do not continue a road test.

diagnostics.finding: Hum changes with pavement; tire has uneven tread
diagnostics.meaning: Tire/road interaction is a credible source. More than one fault can coexist.
diagnostics.next: Record pressure, wear and conditions; follow tire/wheel diagnosis before condemning a hub.

diagnostics.finding: Noise changes on ordinary curves
diagnostics.meaning: Wheel loading changes; tire wear and hub/bearing concerns remain possible.
diagnostics.next: Compare supported checks and use professional localization if needed. Do not select a side from turn direction alone.

diagnostics.finding: Wheel moves relative to its mounting face
diagnostics.meaning: Wheel attachment must be investigated.
diagnostics.next: Check the wheel, studs, nuts and mating surfaces for damage; do not drive on unexplained looseness.

diagnostics.finding: Wheel/hub moves relative to knuckle
diagnostics.meaning: Bearing condition or hub attachment/clamping needs assessment.
diagnostics.next: Keep the central fastener undisturbed for diagnosis. Use the correct front/rear repair after confirming the cause.

diagnostics.finding: Knuckle and wheel move together; movement is visible at a joint
diagnostics.meaning: Suspension or steering movement may be responsible.
diagnostics.next: Identify the exact joint and apply its inspection method; hand position alone is not a diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: One wheel binds after the brake is released
diagnostics.meaning: A local brake or parking-brake issue is possible.
diagnostics.next: Follow brake diagnosis. Several dragging wheels require a different system-level investigation.

diagnostics.finding: Hand checks are quiet but road noise persists
diagnostics.meaning: The unloaded test has not reproduced the operating condition.
diagnostics.next: Use chassis listening, tire/wheel diagnosis or specified measurements. Do not declare the bearing good solely because it has no detectable hand play.

verification.title: Before any road observation
verification.body: No unresolved dangerous tire/wheel condition, abnormal brake or steering control, severe grinding, binding or unexplained mechanical looseness. If present, transport the car for assessment.

verification.title: After a wheel or brake was removed
verification.body: Correct parts and required new bolts installed; specified torque applied; hoses/cables unstressed; normal firm brake pedal and brake release verified; wheel seated flush; dry-thread wheel nuts tightened in a star pattern; tools and supports cleared.

verification.title: A diagnosis you can explain
verification.body: You can identify the observed fault and the evidence linking it to the symptom. If you cannot, record the uncertainty and the next specific test. A replacement part is not evidence by itself.

verification.title: After repair
verification.body: Original symptom checked under comparable safe conditions; no remaining looseness, drag, leak or rubbing; wheel nuts rechecked within 100 mi / 160 km if a wheel was reinstalled.

references.title: Timken · Checking a hub bearing assembly
references.description: Two-position hand check and exposed-hub inspection; general technique, not Mustang fastener specifications.

references.title: Timken · Symptoms of a worn wheel hub bearing
references.description: Explains overlapping symptoms and why noise, wobble or brake effects need diagnosis.

references.title: MOOG · Diagnosis of worn wheel-end bearings
references.description: Notes that a wheel-bearing noise may only be noticeable while driving. Its generic replacement mileage is not used here.

notes: Keep oil and grease off friction surfaces. Never leave a removed caliper hanging from its flexible hose.
guides.title: Brake inspection: pads, discs and hoses
guides.summary: Measure wear, look for damage and keep the fitted brake package straight before selecting parts.
guides.introduction: Brakes use friction to turn motion into heat. Pads are expected to wear, but an inspection also needs to consider the disc surface, hose condition and how the system is behaving. A change in noise is useful information; it does not automatically identify which part should be replaced.
guides.why: Uneven pad wear, damaged hoses and disc problems require different repairs. Treating every brake concern as “needs pads” can leave the cause in place.

when.summary: Inspect pads, discs, hoses and parking-brake condition at each oil-change service.
notes: A change in stopping performance, a fluid leak or a brake warning needs attention before the next scheduled service.

prepare.title: Identify the front brake package
prepare.detail: Use the 2-, 4- or 6-piston procedure that matches the car. Do not mix limits or hardware instructions.

prepare.title: Plan safe access
prepare.detail: Let hot components cool and arrange the correct lifting/support equipment before wheel-off inspection.

steps.title: Record how the concern behaves
steps.body: Note noise, pull, pulsation or dragging and when it happens.

steps.title: Inspect and measure
steps.body: Check the pads, discs and hoses using the applicable inspection limits. Compare inner and outer wear where the procedure requires it.

steps.title: Choose the matching repair
steps.body: Replace or service only what the inspection calls for, then complete the verification steps in the selected brake procedure.

watchFor.title: Fluid leakage or reduced braking
watchFor.body: Stop treating the issue as routine wear and have the braking system assessed.

watchFor.title: Uneven wear
watchFor.body: Investigate how the caliper and pads are moving instead of replacing the worn friction material alone.

procedures.purpose: Start brake diagnosis from the symptom.
Front pad work for the 2-piston package.
Front pad work for the 4-piston package.
Front pad work for the 6-piston package.
Standard rear pad procedure.

notes: Do not use an uncontrolled roll test or rely on the parking brake as the sole means of supporting a raised vehicle.
guides.title: Parking brake: holding and releasing both matter
guides.summary: Check for a reliable hold, a full release and changes in control feel before reaching for an adjustment.
guides.introduction: The parking brake has two jobs: keep the parked car from moving and release cleanly when you are ready to drive. A change in lever feel, poor holding or drag after release can point to a concern. Simply taking up more cable adjustment does not establish that the mechanism is healthy.
guides.why: Dragging brakes generate heat and wear. A system that releases well but cannot hold the vehicle also needs attention, so the inspection must consider both directions of operation.

when.summary: Check operation every six months and during oil-service brake inspections.

prepare.title: Choose controlled conditions
prepare.detail: Use a safe location for an owner operation check. Raised-wheel and cable inspections belong in the dedicated procedure.

prepare.title: Note the change
prepare.detail: Describe new travel, stiffness, poor holding or failure to release rather than just asking for the cable to be tightened.

steps.title: Check normal application and release
steps.body: Observe the control’s feel and whether the system releases normally.

steps.title: Investigate a fault
steps.body: Use the symptom chart to inspect for damage or a mechanical cause. A warning lamp also needs the correct diagnosis.

steps.title: Adjust only as instructed
steps.body: If adjustment is called for, use the procedure for the fitted brake arrangement and verify both holding and release afterward.

watchFor.title: Drag after release
watchFor.body: Do not assume that the brake has released just because the lever is down.

watchFor.title: A brake warning that stays on
watchFor.body: The cause can include incomplete release or another brake-system problem; confirm it.

procedures.purpose: Diagnose parking-brake operation.
Use the standard cable-adjustment procedure when needed.
Understand and service the control mechanism.

notes: Keep coolant replacement on its separate schedule. This inspection does not reset the coolant-change due date or create a timed replacement requirement for the pump, radiator, thermostat or fan. [Ford maintenance schedule](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)
guides.title: Cooling-system checks between coolant changes
guides.summary: Check coolant level, freeze protection, visible hoses and leaks on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine, then decide what needs attention.
guides.introduction: I start with the coolant and the plumbing before blaming an expensive component. The pump circulates coolant, the thermostat controls its route, and the radiator transfers heat to outside air. Trouble anywhere in that loop can upset cooling; the temperature gauge does not conveniently name the guilty damn part. [2.3L cooling](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L cooling](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L cooling](#/document/G1694609)
guides.why: Low coolant, contamination, an unsuitable mixture or restricted airflow can compromise cooling. This inspection helps separate a healthy system from one needing diagnosis, without turning a routine check into speculative pump, thermostat or radiator replacement. [2.3L inspection](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L inspection](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L inspection](#/document/G1694609)

when.summary: Inspect coolant strength and hoses at oil service. Check coolant level and strength every six months.
notes: Follow the coolant replacement schedule separately.

prepare.title: A cold engine and controlled starting
prepare.detail: Allow the engine and cooling system to cool completely. Switch the ignition off, remove the key from the vehicle and disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Unexpected starting can cause serious injury. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189), [Cooling-system safety](#/document/G1693187)

prepare.title: Inspection and sampling supplies
prepare.detail: Have eye protection, a thick cloth for the reservoir cap and a coolant/battery refractometer, Ford 300-ROB75240 or equivalent, with its sampling supplies and operating instructions. Wear protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. A refractometer measures the coolant's freeze protection; the optional nitrite test kit serves a different purpose. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189), [2.3L tools](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L tools](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L tools](#/document/G1694609)

prepare.title: Correct coolant if a top-up is needed
prepare.detail: All three engine sections specify Motorcraft Orange prediluted coolant VC-3DIL-B, WSS-M97B44-D2, or concentrate VC-3-B, WSS-M97B44-D mixed with distilled water to the required concentration. Match the specification, not just the color. Mixing coolant types can reduce corrosion protection and damage the cooling system. [2.3L fluid requirements](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L fluid requirements](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L fluid requirements](#/document/G1694583)

prepare.title: Keep access appropriate to an inspection
prepare.detail: Work through the open hood at the reservoir and visible portions of the cooling circuit. Leave hoses and components connected. Keep hands and tools clear of cooling fans, which can operate with the ignition off; fans must be disabled before work nearby. This guide uses visual checks without reaching into the fan area. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189), [2.3L inspection](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L inspection](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L inspection](#/document/G1694609)

steps.title: Make the first look a safety check
steps.body:
With the ignition off, visually check the cooling fan for cracks, damage or separation before proceeding with underhood work. If it is damaged, stop: Ford requires replacement before working under the hood because a damaged fan can come apart during operation. Stay clear of the blades even with the ignition off. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

Do not loosen the coolant pressure cap while the engine is running or the system is hot. Even a small opening can release pressurized steam and coolant forcefully enough to cause serious burns. [Cooling-system safety](#/document/G1693187)

steps.title: Find the coolant reservoir
steps.body:
Locate the coolant expansion reservoir, called the degas bottle in the workshop manual. Its pressure-relief cap is the cooling-system cap; these vehicles do not have a separate radiator cap. Identify the reservoir markings before opening anything. [2.3L reservoir](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L reservoir](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L reservoir](#/document/G1694609)

On the 3.7L layout, item 10 is the degas bottle, item 8 the radiator, and items 4 and 7 the upper and lower radiator hoses. Use that layout only for the 3.7L. [3.7L component locations](#/document/G1694572)

steps.title: Read and record the cold level
steps.body:
Look through the reservoir and record the coolant level before adding anything. Ford's filling instructions identify the top of the MIN FILL LEVEL line as the cold filling reference; the warm reference is different, so compare readings taken under the same cold conditions. [2.3L level reference](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L level reference](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L level reference](#/document/G1694583)

Note whether the cap appears correctly installed and whether there is leakage around it or the bottle. A low reading starts an investigation; repeated topping up should not become the maintenance plan. [2.3L inspection](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L inspection](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L inspection](#/document/G1694609)

steps.title: Follow the visible hoses and joints
steps.body:
Visually follow the accessible radiator, heater and reservoir hoses and tubes. Look for cracks, damage, incorrect routing, apparent blockage, damaged clamps, and leakage or weeping where hoses join components. Check visible areas around the thermostat housing, radiator, coolant pump, reservoir and cap. Observe accessible gasket and seal joints, engine core plugs and the block heater if fitted. Do not disconnect parts to complete this check. [2.3L inspection](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L inspection](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L inspection](#/document/G1694609)

For the 3.7L, also inspect visible areas around the lower intake manifold and transmission-fluid cooler where fitted. [3.7L inspection](#/document/G1694576)

For the 5.0L, include the visible lower intake manifold and oil cooler. [5.0L inspection](#/document/G1694609)

Note coolant odor or evidence of steam. Inside the cabin, a wet floor or coolant odor can point toward the heater core. Record the location rather than immediately ordering a component. [2.3L leak checks](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L leak checks](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L leak checks](#/document/G1694609)

steps.title: Look for cooling problems outside the plumbing
steps.body: From outside the fan area, inspect the visible radiator and air-conditioning condenser for airflow obstructions such as leaves or cardboard. Note missing air deflectors or front-end damage. Visually check for a loose, worn or incorrectly positioned drive belt, an obviously damaged tensioner, and damaged fan wiring or connectors. Arrange correction of anything abnormal; do not reach into the fan or belt area during this inspection. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189), [2.3L visual checks](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L visual checks](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L visual checks](#/document/G1694609)

steps.title: Open the cold reservoir and inspect the coolant
steps.body:
Once the system is cold, cover the pressure cap with a thick cloth and remove it. Inspect the cap and bottle sealing areas for damaged threads, burrs or a damaged sealing O-ring. Sealing damage calls for replacement of the affected cap or bottle. [Cooling-system safety](#/document/G1693187), [2.3L cap handling](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L cap handling](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L cap handling](#/document/G1694583), [2.3L sealing checks](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L sealing checks](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L sealing checks](#/document/G1694609)

On the 2.3L and 5.0L, there is another replacement trigger even if the sealing parts look intact: evidence that coolant was expelled through the cap and may have contaminated its gasket calls for replacement of the affected cap and/or bottle as appropriate. Establish whether coolant came through the cap; leakage from a nearby hose joint alone does not establish this condition. Arrange the required replacement rather than judging the cap serviceable by appearance alone. [2.3L cap replacement criteria](#/document/G1673122), [5.0L cap replacement criteria](#/document/G1694609)

Look for clarity, sediment, brown discoloration, an oily sheen or a milky appearance. Orange coolant can become pink or light red during normal use; clear, uncontaminated coolant does not need replacement solely because of that color shift. Use the diagnostic decisions below if the appearance is abnormal. [2.3L coolant condition](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L coolant condition](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L coolant condition](#/document/G1694609)

steps.title: Measure coolant strength
steps.body:
If the coolant appearance is acceptable, use the coolant/battery refractometer to measure freeze protection. Follow the instrument's instructions for preparing it, collecting the sample, reading the appropriate scale and cleaning it afterward. Record the result. Ford specifies a refractometer for this check. [2.3L strength test](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L strength test](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L strength test](#/document/G1694609)

For ordinary year-round conditions, the target is 48–50% coolant: a coolant-to-distilled-water ratio of 48/52 to 50/50, corresponding to freeze protection from -34°C to -37°C (-30°F to -34°F). All three engine sections give this range. [2.3L concentration](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L concentration](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L concentration](#/document/G1694609)

Below -37°C (-34°F), a higher concentration may be necessary, but never exceed 60% coolant, or 60/40; that concentration provides freeze protection to -50°C (-58°F). Excess concentrate reduces overheat protection. For extreme heat, never go below 40% coolant, or 40/60, because freeze and corrosion protection suffer. Both extremes can damage the engine. These are climate limits, not an invitation to improve the mixture by eyeballing it. [2.3L climate limits](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L climate limits](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L climate limits](#/document/G1694583)

steps.title: Top up only when the fluid and mixture are suitable
steps.body:
If the cold level needs raising and the coolant is clean, correctly specified and already within the normal 48–50% range, add the specified Orange prediluted coolant to the cold reference at the top of the MIN FILL LEVEL line. Record what you added. [2.3L top-up](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L top-up](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L top-up](#/document/G1694583)

If concentration is wrong, plan a measured correction rather than adding random amounts. Ford's direction is to remove some coolant and replace it with specified concentrate when the mixture is too weak, or distilled water when it is too strong, then verify the result. Coolant removal and any required filling or bleeding belong to the separate coolant-service task. Contamination needs diagnosis and the appropriate flushing/refilling service. [2.3L correction decisions](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L correction decisions](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L correction decisions](#/document/G1694609)

Do not add alcohol, methanol, brine or coolant containing alcohol or methanol; these can cause overheating or freezing damage. Ford also advises against recycled coolant for systems originally filled with Orange coolant. [2.3L filling precautions](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L filling precautions](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L filling precautions](#/document/G1694583)

steps.title: Refit the cap and close out the check
steps.body:
If the cap and bottle passed the sealing checks, refit the reservoir cap and tighten it until it reaches its hard stop. Confirm that it is seated correctly. If step 6 identified sealing damage—or, on the 2.3L or 5.0L, coolant expelled through the cap that may have contaminated its gasket—arrange replacement of the affected cap and/or bottle before returning the car to service. Reinstalling a cap does not resolve a replacement finding. [2.3L cap criteria and installation](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L cap criteria and installation](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L cap criteria and installation](#/document/G1694609)

Remove the cloth, sampling equipment and other inspection supplies from the engine compartment. I would keep a short record of the cold level, freeze-protection reading, coolant appearance, any additions and the locations of suspicious marks or damage. That gives the next inspection something useful to compare. If you found leakage, contamination or abnormal temperature behavior, use the decisions below to arrange the next action.

watchFor.title: Steam, leakage or overheating
watchFor.body: Stop the routine check and arrange diagnosis; do not run the engine merely to reproduce an overheating concern. Leave a hot pressure cap closed. [Cooling-system safety](#/document/G1693187), [2.3L diagnosis](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L diagnosis](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L diagnosis](#/document/G1694609)

watchFor.title: A good freeze reading with suspicious coolant
watchFor.body: Freeze protection does not clear contamination. Ford checks appearance before measuring strength, and suspected Gold coolant contamination requires a separate nitrite test. [2.3L condition checks](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L condition checks](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L condition checks](#/document/G1694609)

procedures.purpose: Identify the 3.7L cooling-system components.
2.3L inspection criteria and follow-up cooling diagnosis.
3.7L inspection criteria and follow-up cooling diagnosis.
5.0L inspection criteria and follow-up cooling diagnosis.

stepGroups.title: Prepare safely and establish the level
stepGroups.summary: Make the car safe to inspect and identify the cold coolant reference.

stepGroups.title: Inspect the visible system
stepGroups.summary: Check hoses, joints, airflow, cap sealing and coolant appearance.

stepGroups.title: Measure strength and finish
stepGroups.summary: Interpret the mixture, make a supported top-up if appropriate and secure a serviceable cap.

diagnostics.finding: Clear coolant has shifted from orange to pink or light red.
diagnostics.meaning: This can be a normal color change rather than deterioration.
diagnostics.next: Continue the strength check; color alone does not justify draining or flushing. [2.3L color guidance](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L color guidance](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L color guidance](#/document/G1694609)

diagnostics.finding: Coolant is murky green-brown, or an incorrect coolant is known or suspected to have been added.
diagnostics.meaning: Mixed coolant may have reduced corrosion protection. Gold coolant contamination may leave the orange appearance largely unchanged.
diagnostics.next: For suspected Gold contamination, use the 3-Way HD Antifreeze Coolant Test Kit 328-2050-62291 or equivalent, following its nitrite-test instructions. A positive nitrite result calls for flushing and refilling with the correct coolant mixture. Known non-specified coolant requires chemical flushing. [2.3L contamination checks](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L contamination checks](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L contamination checks](#/document/G1694609)

diagnostics.finding: Dark orange coolant contains debris, or coolant is light/reddish brown.
diagnostics.meaning: Debris may indicate stop-leak material that can restrict coolant flow; brown discoloration may indicate rust.
diagnostics.next: Arrange the engine-specific flushing and correct refill service. A top-up does not remove sediment or rust. [2.3L condition decisions](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L condition decisions](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L condition decisions](#/document/G1694609)

diagnostics.finding: An iridescent oil-like sheen or milky brown coolant is present.
diagnostics.meaning: Oil may be entering the cooling system; a milky appearance can indicate an internal engine leak.
diagnostics.next: Arrange diagnosis of the contamination source and subsequent flushing/refilling. Ford calls for pressure testing with milky brown coolant and engine diagnosis when oil contamination is suspected. [2.3L contamination diagnosis](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L contamination diagnosis](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L contamination diagnosis](#/document/G1694609)

diagnostics.finding: The cold level keeps falling, with or without a visible leak.
diagnostics.meaning: Coolant loss may be external or internal. An apparently dry engine compartment does not settle the question.
diagnostics.next: Arrange the separate cooling pressure/leak test using the correct engine branch. If external leakage is absent, Ford's diagnosis continues with checks for fluid cross-contamination and combustion gases. [2.3L loss diagnosis](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L loss diagnosis](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L loss diagnosis](#/document/G1694609)

diagnostics.finding: Coolant strength is outside the intended range.
diagnostics.meaning: The mixture needs correction for the vehicle's operating climate.
diagnostics.next: Use the correction direction in step 8, then have the final mixed coolant retested. Do not treat the 40–60% outer limits as the ordinary target range. [2.3L concentration decisions](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L concentration decisions](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L concentration decisions](#/document/G1694609)

diagnostics.finding: Temperature behavior changes despite an acceptable level and mixture.
diagnostics.meaning: Airflow, circulation, thermostat, sensor or gauge concerns remain possible; the inspection has not identified a failed component.
diagnostics.next: Arrange engine-specific overheating or slow-warm-up diagnosis. Use [2.3L diagnosis](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L diagnosis](#/document/G1694576) or [5.0L diagnosis](#/document/G1694609) as applicable.

verification.title: Level and cap are accounted for
verification.body:
The cold level has been recorded and any appropriate top-up reaches the cold reference. A serviceable pressure cap is installed to its hard stop. [2.3L level and closure](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L level and closure](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L level and closure](#/document/G1694583)

Any cap or bottle replacement finding must be resolved before returning the car to service. For the 2.3L and 5.0L, that includes coolant expelled through the cap that may have contaminated its gasket, even when visible sealing damage is absent. [2.3L replacement criteria](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L sealing criteria](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L replacement criteria](#/document/G1694609)

verification.title: Strength was measured
verification.body: Record the refractometer result and compare it with the normal 48–50% target or the justified climate-specific concentration. An unmeasured mixture remains an unfinished strength check. [2.3L strength inspection](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L strength inspection](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L strength inspection](#/document/G1694609)

verification.title: Findings have a next action
verification.body: Visible hose damage, leakage, sealing faults, airflow restrictions and contamination have been identified for correction or diagnosis. A visual inspection alone does not prove that the system is leak-free or that the pump, thermostat and fan function correctly. [2.3L inspection and testing](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L inspection and testing](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L inspection and testing](#/document/G1694609)

notes: Scope: 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine.
This is an inspection and diagnosis guide. Exhaust cutting, component replacement and connection reassembly are separate repairs.
guides.title: Exhaust and heat shields: track down the damn rattle
guides.summary: Inspect the exhaust pipes, silencers, supports and heat shields on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. Separate harmless surface rust and cooling noises from leaks, broken supports and unwanted body contact.
guides.introduction: An underbody rattle can make a perfectly respectable Mustang sound like a drawer full of cutlery. I start by separating the suspects: the exhaust itself, the supports holding it in position, and the shields around it. Ford lists faults in all three areas as possible noise sources, so the loudest-looking part does not automatically deserve replacement. [2.3L diagnosis](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L diagnosis](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L diagnosis](#/document/G1688102)
guides.why: This inspection answers three useful questions: is anything damaged or leaking, is the exhaust supported without touching the body, and are its heat shields present and secure? Those findings lead to different repairs. A loose shield, a broken hanger and a perforated pipe are separate problems, even when they all announce themselves with an irritating buzz. [2.3L diagnosis](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L diagnosis](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L diagnosis](#/document/G1688102)

when.summary: Inspect the exhaust and heat shields at every oil-change service. Monthly, check that any designed holes or slots in the tailpipe remain clear of debris.
notes: Only clear existing openings; do not drill new holes or change the exhaust design.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a suitably rated hoist, or a service jack and stands with adequate capacity for the vehicle, cargo and modifications. Identify the lifting locations by the stamped triangles and the lifting-point diagram. The emergency tire jack is not suitable for this inspection. [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631), [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Have inspection equipment ready
prepare.detail: Have a rubber mallet for the light tapping checks, eye and ear protection, and protective gloves for sharp edges. No exhaust disconnection, cutting or replacement materials are needed to perform the inspection. [2.3L noise checks](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L noise checks](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L noise checks](#/document/G1688102), [Personal protection](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Identify the engine
prepare.detail: Use the diagnosis for the engine actually fitted: 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L. The shared inspection below applies to those three engines, but replacement layouts, connections and tightening specifications must come from the matching repair procedure. [2.3L diagnosis](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L diagnosis](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L diagnosis](#/document/G1688102)

steps.title: Describe the concern before chasing it
steps.body: Write down what you have already noticed: rattle, buzz, clunk, hiss, tick, sputter or low drumming. Note whether it happens cold, after warm-up, at idle, with changing engine speed, during acceleration, over bumps or after shutdown. Also record odors, smoke or reduced power. Ford uses these distinctions to direct the inspection and narrow down the possible causes. [2.3L symptom chart](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L symptom chart](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L symptom chart](#/document/G1688102)

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start and let the exhaust cool
steps.body: Before working around or beneath the car, disable remote start if equipped through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Switch the ignition off and remove the key so another person cannot start the engine during the inspection. Exhaust components become hot in use; allow them to cool before handling or tapping them. Wear eye and ear protection, and gloves when handling sharp edges. Unexpected starting and sharp components can cause serious injury. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189), [Exhaust heating and cooling](#/document/G1688088)

steps.title: Raise and support the car without creating another problem
steps.body:
For jack-and-stand access, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block wheels remaining on the ground. Lift at the designated locations identified by the stamped triangles, then support the vehicle on stands before going underneath. Never work beneath a car held only by a jack: it can lower or shift unexpectedly. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189), [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631)

For a hoist, use the designated support locations and adequate equipment capacity. Check that its adapters and arms clear the exhaust, suspension, steering linkage, brackets and rear axle cover. Check underbody clearance before driving onto a drive-on lift. Do not lift against either bumper. [Hoist positioning](#/document/G1663631), [Hoist safety](#/document/G1693189)

Inspect with the exhaust assembled. The convertible brace removal and exhaust separation shown in the 3.7L muffler-replacement procedure are removal operations, not routine inspection prerequisites. [3.7L replacement context](#/document/G1688092)

steps.title: Inspect the pipes and exhaust housings
steps.body: Work along the accessible exhaust from the engine end toward the outlets. Look for pinched or crushed pipes, damaged mufflers, damage to the catalytic converter housings, and damaged tailpipe sections. Examine rusty areas for actual holes rather than judging by color alone. Ford considers surface rust normal when there are no perforations; a hole is a different finding and needs repair assessment. Record any section you cannot inspect rather than calling it good. [2.3L visual inspection](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L visual inspection](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L visual inspection](#/document/G1688102)

steps.title: Check the shields and the spaces around them
steps.body: Look for loose, damaged or missing heat shields, and for foreign material trapped between a shield and an exhaust component. Pay particular attention to these areas if the concern is a metallic rattle or a burning smell at idle. A missing shield and debris caught against the exhaust both need correction; removing a rattling shield permanently is not the prescribed fix. Ford calls for securing a loose shield or replacing a missing or persistently noisy shield or component. [2.3L shield checks](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L shield checks](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L shield checks](#/document/G1688102)

steps.title: Inspect the hangers and check for body contact
steps.body:
The isolators are the rubber supports between the exhaust hangers and their mounting points. Check that they are correctly installed and inspect them for wear or damage. Look for broken hangers, damaged brackets, loose fasteners and signs that the exhaust has been touching the body or chassis. In Ford's charts, an exhaust that is 'grounded' means it is making unwanted physical contact—not an electrical fault. [2.3L mounting checks](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L mounting checks](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L mounting checks](#/document/G1688102)

With the exhaust cool, move the assembled system to simulate its movement over bumps while watching for contact. Contact or a reproduced clunk points toward support, alignment or clearance trouble; it does not by itself prove the muffler is bad. [2.3L movement check](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L movement check](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L movement check](#/document/G1688102)

On the 3.7L, avoid excessive bending or twisting and never let the exhaust hang from its flexible joint; that can damage the assembly. Do not apply oil- or grease-based lubricant to its rubber isolators, because it can deteriorate them. [3.7L handling precautions](#/document/G1688092)

steps.title: Use light taps to locate a rattle
steps.body: If a rattle, buzz, hiss or similar noise remains unexplained, use the rubber mallet to tap the exhaust components lightly. Check the muffler, then the catalytic converter or converters, listening for the original noise and locating its source. A reproduced internal rattle can indicate loose or broken muffler baffles—the internal partitions—or a loose or broken converter element. Have the identified component assessed for repair or replacement. [2.3L tapping checks](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L tapping checks](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L tapping checks](#/document/G1688102)

steps.title: Look for evidence of an exhaust leak
steps.body:
Inspect the accessible system for punctures, broken welds, loose or damaged clamps and fasteners, and damage around gaskets and exhaust sensors. Look on nearby chassis surfaces for grayish-white or black soot: Ford identifies those deposits as evidence of leakage at that location. Check clamp position as well as condition; a clamp merely being present does not establish that the joint is correctly assembled. [2.3L leak checks](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L leak checks](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L leak checks](#/document/G1688102)

Whistling, booming, humming or ticking that changes as the engine warms, especially with fumes, directs attention toward leaks. A sputter that is worse cold and improves warm also calls for leak and damage checks. If the visual inspection does not locate a suspected leak, arrange further leak diagnosis before declaring the system sound. Do not tighten an unidentified connection using a torque borrowed from another engine or component. [2.3L symptom chart](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L symptom chart](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L symptom chart](#/document/G1688102)

steps.title: Check existing drain openings when restriction is suspected
steps.body:
If the exhaust seems restricted and frozen condensate is a possibility, inspect the existing drain holes for foreign material. Ford directs moving the vehicle indoors to thaw, then checking whether normal operation returns. If the concern persists, it needs powertrain and emissions diagnosis. A drain hole enlarged by corrosion can itself cause noise; confirm that it is the source before condemning the component. [2.3L restriction checks](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L restriction checks](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L restriction checks](#/document/G1688102)

Check openings as they exist. This inspection does not call for drilling new holes or enlarging old ones.

steps.title: Turn each finding into a specific next action
steps.body:
Record the location and type of each defect: loose shield, worn isolator, broken bracket, body contact, damaged pipe, perforation, leaking connection or internal rattle. Damaged isolators, hangers and exhaust components need the corresponding repair or replacement; loose bracket fasteners need their component-specific tightening specification. Keep those repairs separate from this inspection. [2.3L repair decisions](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L repair decisions](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L repair decisions](#/document/G1688102)

For a confirmed loose heat shield, all three diagnosis charts specify worm gear clamp 7L5Z-5A231-AA tightened to 7 Nm. Give that detail to whoever performs the correction. A missing shield, or noise that remains after securing it, requires assessment for a replacement shield or affected component. The 7 Nm value belongs to that specified shield clamp, not every clamp under the car. [2.3L shield correction](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L shield correction](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L shield correction](#/document/G1688102)

steps.title: Finish with a clear inspection result
steps.body:
Recheck that shields, hangers and connections remain installed and that nothing introduced during the inspection is left underneath. This inspection requires no exhaust disassembly, so there are no muffler clamps or brace bolts to reinstall. Clear the work area and lower the vehicle using the lifting equipment's operating instructions. [Lifting safety](#/document/G1663631), [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

After any necessary repair, repeat the relevant visual, mounting, contact and noise checks. Confirm that the original concern has been resolved under the conditions recorded at the start. If it remains, use the symptom to continue diagnosis rather than replacing another part on a hunch. [2.3L diagnosis](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L diagnosis](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L diagnosis](#/document/G1688102)

watchFor.title: Unexpected starting
watchFor.body: Disable remote start before working around the car, switch off the ignition and remove the key. An unexpected engine start during service can cause serious injury. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

watchFor.title: A jack is not an underbody support
watchFor.body: Use designated lifting points and stands or a correctly positioned hoist. A jack alone can lower unexpectedly, trapping someone beneath the vehicle. [Lifting safety](#/document/G1663631)

watchFor.title: Fumes or burning smells
watchFor.body: If exhaust fumes enter the cabin, stop using the car and arrange immediate assessment. Burning smells or smoke also need investigation for foreign material or missing shields. [Leak and burning-smell diagnosis](#/document/G1688088)

watchFor.title: A rattle does not justify deleting a shield
watchFor.body: Secure or replace the affected shield as appropriate. Ford's correction retains the shielding rather than removing it as a permanent noise cure. [Heat-shield correction](#/document/G1688077)

Engine-specific exhaust inspection and symptom diagnosis for the 3.7L.
Applicable exhaust inspection and symptom diagnosis for the 5.0L.
3.7L handling precautions and a separate repair reference if muffler-and-tailpipe replacement is confirmed.

stepGroups.title: Describe the concern and gain safe access
stepGroups.summary: Identify the symptom, prevent starting and support the vehicle correctly.

stepGroups.title: Inspect condition, shields and supports
stepGroups.summary: Find damage, loose shielding, failed mountings and unwanted contact.

stepGroups.title: Narrow down the source
stepGroups.summary: Use light tapping, leak evidence and drain-hole checks where relevant.

stepGroups.title: Choose the next action and finish
stepGroups.summary: Record specific faults and verify the result after correction.

diagnostics.finding: Rusty surface, but no perforation
diagnostics.meaning: Surface rust alone is normal for these exhaust materials; heat and road salt can contribute.
diagnostics.next: Record the condition. Actual holes require repair assessment. [2.3L rust guidance](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L rust guidance](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L rust guidance](#/document/G1688102)

diagnostics.finding: Pinging only while the hot exhaust cools after shutdown
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies this as normal expansion and contraction during heating and cooling.
diagnostics.next: Do not replace components solely for that cooling sound. Investigate separately if there is also damage, leakage or a different noise. [2.3L cooling noise](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L cooling noise](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L cooling noise](#/document/G1688102)

diagnostics.finding: Rattle, squeak or buzz from underneath
diagnostics.meaning: Possible sources include loose shields, trapped material, worn isolators, damaged hangers, internal component damage or body contact.
diagnostics.next: Use the shield, movement and light-tapping checks to identify the source before selecting a repair. [2.3L noise diagnosis](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L noise diagnosis](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L noise diagnosis](#/document/G1688102)

diagnostics.finding: Drone, clunk, acceleration thump or vibration
diagnostics.meaning: Support damage, misalignment, strained isolators or exhaust-to-body contact may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Check isolator condition and installation, brackets, fasteners and clearance. Persistent engine-speed-dependent drumming needs further diagnosis if those checks do not identify the cause. [2.3L vibration diagnosis](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L vibration diagnosis](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L vibration diagnosis](#/document/G1688102)

diagnostics.finding: Soot near a connection, a broken weld or a perforation
diagnostics.meaning: These are leak findings; noises that change with warm-up can support the same diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Identify the affected joint or component and arrange the matching repair, followed by a leak check. [2.3L leak diagnosis](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L leak diagnosis](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L leak diagnosis](#/document/G1688102)

diagnostics.finding: Hissing or rushing noise without reduced performance
diagnostics.meaning: Possible sources include exhaust flow, a leak or loose internal muffler or converter parts.
diagnostics.next: Check for leaks and use the light rubber-mallet check to locate an internal rattle. Do not assume unchanged performance proves there is no fault. [2.3L hissing diagnosis](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L hissing diagnosis](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L hissing diagnosis](#/document/G1688102)

diagnostics.finding: Low power or suspected exhaust restriction
diagnostics.meaning: A crushed pipe, damaged converter, internal obstruction or frozen condensate may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Inspect visible damage and existing drains. If thawing does not restore normal operation, or freezing is not the explanation, obtain powertrain and emissions diagnosis. [2.3L restriction diagnosis](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L restriction diagnosis](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L restriction diagnosis](#/document/G1688102)

diagnostics.finding: Sulfur or rotten-egg odor
diagnostics.meaning: A slight occasional sulfur smell can result from sulfur in the fuel. Rich running and misfires are separate possible causes.
diagnostics.next: Do not condemn a converter from odor alone. Suspected rich running or misfire requires powertrain and emissions diagnosis. [2.3L odor diagnosis](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L odor diagnosis](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L odor diagnosis](#/document/G1688102)

verification.title: Account for every inspected area
verification.body: Confirm that accessible pipes, mufflers, converter housings, shields, isolators and hanger brackets were checked. Record inaccessible areas and unresolved findings explicitly. [2.3L inspection](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L inspection](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L inspection](#/document/G1688102)

verification.title: Confirm support and clearance after correction
verification.body: Repeat the movement check after a mounting or alignment repair. The original contact or clunk should no longer occur, and the affected supports and shields should be secure. [2.3L contact check](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L contact check](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L contact check](#/document/G1688102)

verification.title: Verify the original symptom and any repaired leak
verification.body: Reassess the conditions that originally produced the noise. An unresolved symptom remains open even if the system looks tidy. After 3.7L muffler-and-tailpipe service, Ford specifically requires an exhaust leak check. [2.3L diagnosis](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L diagnosis](#/document/G1688088), [5.0L diagnosis](#/document/G1688102), [3.7L post-service check](#/document/G1688092)

notes: The supported scope remains 2015 Mustang models with 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines.

Gear-oil substitution and friction modifier are specification decisions. The documented standalone level check specifies WSS-M2C942-A gear lubricant; the additive instructions appear in the separate drain-and-fill procedure. [Level check](#/document/G2214894) · [Draining and filling](#/document/G2214742)
guides.title: Rear axle inspection: find where the leak starts
guides.summary: Inspect the rear differential for damage and leakage, check its lubricant level when needed, and recognize findings that require further diagnosis.
guides.introduction: For a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine, I start with a simple question: where does the wetness actually begin? Buying a seal before answering that is an expensive way to play parts roulette. A wet housing is a clue, not a conviction. This guide covers the exterior inspection and the documented fluid-level check; draining the axle and repairing it are separate jobs. [Axle diagnosis](#/document/G2214741) · [Fluid-level check](#/document/G2214894)
guides.why: The rear differential houses gears and bearings that depend on the correct lubricant level. Its seals contain that lubricant, while the housing vent prevents pressure buildup. A blocked vent can damage sealing lips, so replacing a leaking seal without investigating the vent can leave the underlying problem alive and well. [Leak analysis](#/document/G2214741)

when.summary: Inspect the rear axle at oil-change service. Have suspected leakage or axle submersion assessed promptly.
notes: Routine fluid replacement is addressed separately because Ford’s online normal schedule and axle exception use different wording.

prepare.title: Record what prompted the inspection
prepare.detail: Note where you noticed wetness, any recent axle work, and when a noise occurs: during turning, acceleration, deceleration or a shift from Reverse to Drive. These details help distinguish the possible causes listed in Ford’s diagnostic chart. [Axle diagnosis](#/document/G2214741)

prepare.title: Arrange safe access
prepare.detail: The documented level check uses a vehicle hoist with the transmission in Neutral. Use a hoist rated for the vehicle’s actual weight, including cargo and modifications, with its supports at the specified lifting points identified by stamped triangles. If you cannot provide that setup, have the underside inspection and level check performed where it is available. [Fluid-level setup](#/document/G2214894) · [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) · [Hoist precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Gather inspection supplies and protection
prepare.detail: Useful inspection aids are a light, clean wiping cloths and a way to record findings. Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. If using a cleaning chemical, read its safety information; keep flammable solvents away from ignition sources. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Have the level-check equipment ready if needed
prepare.detail: Use a tool that properly matches the actual fill-plug recess and a torque wrench capable of 25 lb.ft (34 Nm). For topping up, the specified lubricant is Motorcraft SAE 75W-85 Premium Synthetic Hypoid Gear Lubricant, XY-75W85-QL, meeting WSS-M2C942-A. The level check calls for clean gear lubricant; do not add friction modifier by habit or use a complete-refill quantity as a top-up amount. [Level-check materials and torque](#/document/G2214894) · [Separate drain-and-fill procedure](#/document/G2214742)

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: Before working around or beneath the car, disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Keep the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle so another person cannot start it during the inspection. Unexpected starting can cause serious injury. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Raise the car using the documented access
steps.body:
With the transmission in Neutral, position the Mustang on the correctly rated hoist. Locate the stamped triangles marking the lifting points and position the supports as shown in Ford’s lifting diagram. Check that the adapters and arms will not damage the suspension, exhaust, steering components, axle or rear cover. For a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it. [Level-check setup](#/document/G2214894) · [Lifting locations and clearance](#/document/G1663631) · [Hoist capacity](#/document/G1693189)

Never get beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, and do not use the emergency tire-changing jack for this service. Incorrect support can let the car shift or fall. [Lifting safety](#/document/G1663631)

steps.title: Inspect the housing, seals and pinion flange
steps.body:
Look over the differential housing for obvious mechanical damage, then inspect the seals and pinion flange. The pinion flange is the connection where the driveshaft meets the differential. Look around the housing-cover joint and plugs as well, recording where wetness appears rather than immediately assigning blame to the nearest seal. Ford’s preliminary inspection specifically calls for checking the housing, seals and pinion flange for damage. [Preliminary inspection and leakage analysis](#/document/G2214741)

If the axle has cooler lines, include their visible connections in your observations. Leave them connected: disconnecting a cooler line and removing its fitting are operations in the draining procedure. [Cooler-equipped axle branch](#/document/G2214742)

steps.title: Clean enough to trace the leak
steps.body:
Clean the affected exterior area enough to identify the exact source, then inspect it again. Distinguish fresh fluid emerging at a joint or seal from fluid merely coating a nearby surface. If the source remains unclear, record that uncertainty. [Leak-source analysis](#/document/G2214741)

Do not call the leak repaired simply because the area now looks clean. The inspection needs either an identified source or a clear next step for further diagnosis. [Diagnostic sequence](#/document/G2214741)

steps.title: Include the vent in a confirmed leak investigation
steps.body:
When leakage is present, include the axle housing vent in the diagnosis. A blocked vent allows pressure to build inside the housing and can cause excessive seal-lip wear. Ford directs checking the vent, clearing it if possible and replacing it if it cannot be cleared. Have that check completed as part of the leak assessment; a seal-only repair can miss the cause. [Axle vent diagnosis](#/document/G2214741)

For leakage originating at the pinion seal, arrange inspection of the seal and flange sealing surface as well as the vent. Seal damage, a worn sealing surface, installation damage and trapped metal debris are among Ford’s listed causes. This exterior inspection does not establish which internal sealing defect is present. [Pinion seal leakage](#/document/G2214741)

steps.title: Decide whether to open the fill plug
steps.body:
Suspected leakage warrants a lubricant-level check. Howling or whining, and a loud clunk when shifting from Reverse to Drive, also lead Ford’s diagnostic chart to a level check as an initial action; neither symptom proves low lubricant is the only cause. [Symptom chart and leak analysis](#/document/G2214741)

For an otherwise uneventful exterior inspection, do not automatically turn the job into a fluid change. Ford’s axle-maintenance exception says level checks or changes are not required unless leakage is suspected or the axle has been submerged. After submersion, have the axle checked as soon as possible, even if its exterior is dry. [Ford axle-maintenance exception](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649140&Uid=G1634877&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

If no level check is needed, continue to step 10.

steps.title: Identify and remove the fill plug
steps.body: Match the actual housing to the level-check illustration and remove the differential fluid fill plug using a tool that fits its recess correctly. On the illustrated housing, the fill plug is the higher plug, offset to one side. The lower plug identified in the draining illustration is the drain plug; leave it installed for this check. [Fill-plug identification](#/document/G2214894) · [Drain-plug identification](#/document/G2214742)

steps.title: Check the level and top up only if needed
steps.body:
Check the lubricant surface relative to the fill opening. The specified level is within 9 mm (0.354 in.) below that opening. If the level is farther below it, add clean Motorcraft SAE 75W-85 Premium Synthetic Hypoid Gear Lubricant, XY-75W85-QL, meeting WSS-M2C942-A, and recheck until the level meets the requirement. The measurement determines the top-up amount. [Fluid level and lubricant specification](#/document/G2214894)

Use the standalone level-check instructions for this job. Friction modifier quantities and the cooler-pump operation belong to the separate drain-and-fill procedure; they are not additional steps in Ford’s level-check procedure. [Level check](#/document/G2214894) · [Drain-and-fill instructions](#/document/G2214742)

steps.title: Reinstall and tighten the fill plug
steps.body: Install the differential fluid fill plug and tighten it to 25 lb.ft (34 Nm). Wipe away fluid spilled during the check so it will not obscure your final inspection. [Fill-plug installation](#/document/G2214894) · [Leak-source visibility](#/document/G2214741)

steps.title: Close the inspection with a finding and a next action
steps.body:
Reinspect the cleaned area and, if opened, the fill plug. Record the leak location or remaining uncertainty, visible damage, the measured level and any lubricant added. Cleaning and topping up do not resolve a leaking seal, damaged housing or blocked vent; those findings need the appropriate repair and subsequent verification. If the source is not visually evident or a noise remains unexplained, continue with diagnosis. [Inspection and diagnostic sequence](#/document/G2214741)

Before lowering the hoist, clear your equipment and make sure everyone is clear of the vehicle. Keep any water-exposure finding open for prompt assessment: a correct level alone does not settle that concern. [Ford submersion guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649140&Uid=G1634877&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

watchFor.title: Water exposure without a visible leak
watchFor.body: An axle that has been submerged needs checking as soon as possible. A dry housing does not cancel that requirement. [Ford axle-maintenance exception](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649140&Uid=G1634877&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

watchFor.title: A seal leak with an overlooked vent
watchFor.body: Pressure from a plugged vent can wear sealing lips. Include the vent in the diagnosis so a replacement seal does not inherit the same damn problem. [Vent and seal diagnosis](#/document/G2214741)

watchFor.title: Noise despite a correct level
watchFor.body: Correct lubricant level does not rule out housing, gear or bearing damage. Persistent noise needs diagnosis matched to when and how it occurs. [Axle symptom chart](#/document/G2214741)

procedures.purpose: Inspect the axle exterior, trace leakage, consider vent problems and interpret noise findings.
Perform the conditional lubricant-level check and reinstall the fill plug.
Identify lifting points and prevent support or underbody damage.
Prevent unexpected starting and apply relevant service and hoist precautions.
Distinguish drain-and-fill operations from an exterior inspection and standalone level check.

stepGroups.title: Prepare and gain safe access
stepGroups.summary: Prevent starting and support the car correctly.

stepGroups.title: Inspect and trace the source
stepGroups.summary: Check the housing and sealing areas, then include the vent in leak diagnosis.

stepGroups.title: Check the lubricant level when indicated
stepGroups.summary: Use the correct opening, level specification, lubricant and plug torque.

stepGroups.title: Verify and choose the next action
stepGroups.summary: Separate completed checks from concerns still requiring diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Fresh leakage has a clearly identified origin.
diagnostics.meaning: The exterior inspection has located the source, but the underlying cause still needs assessment.
diagnostics.next: Verify lubricant level, include the vent check and arrange the repair appropriate to the identified source. [Leak analysis](#/document/G2214741)

diagnostics.finding: The level is more than 9 mm (0.354 in.) below the fill opening.
diagnostics.meaning: The lubricant is below the specified level.
diagnostics.next: Top up with the specified WSS-M2C942-A lubricant, reinstall the plug at 25 lb.ft (34 Nm), and continue investigating any leakage. [Level check](#/document/G2214894) · [Leak diagnosis](#/document/G2214741)

diagnostics.finding: Howling, whining or a loud Reverse-to-Drive clunk.
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect lubricant level is one possible cause. Gear contact, damage or excessive backlash may also be involved, depending on the symptom.
diagnostics.next: Check the level first. If correct or the concern persists after correction, arrange further axle diagnosis; backlash is the free play between meshing gears, not something to adjust by ear. [Axle symptom chart](#/document/G2214741)

diagnostics.finding: Grinding, popping or chattering during turns.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies worn or damaged differential gears as possible sources.
diagnostics.next: Arrange differential-carrier diagnosis rather than assuming an additive will fix it. [Turning-noise diagnosis](#/document/G2214741)

diagnostics.finding: Grunting with takeoff shudder, or shudder during acceleration.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include loose mounts or fasteners, damaged mounting or suspension components, and incorrect driveline angles.
diagnostics.next: Arrange the relevant mounting, suspension and driveline checks. Do not guess a tightening torque from this inspection. [Shudder diagnosis](#/document/G2214741)

diagnostics.finding: Continuous low-pitched scraping beginning at low speed.
diagnostics.meaning: Worn or damaged pinion bearings are a listed possible cause.
diagnostics.next: Arrange bearing diagnosis; an exterior inspection cannot confirm bearing condition. [Scraping-noise diagnosis](#/document/G2214741)

diagnostics.finding: The axle was submerged, whether or not leakage is visible.
diagnostics.meaning: The water-exposure exception applies independently of the exterior findings.
diagnostics.next: Have the axle assessed as soon as possible. [Ford submersion guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649140&Uid=G1634877&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

verification.title: The exterior findings are specific
verification.body: Record whether the housing, seals and pinion flange show damage, and whether leakage has been traced to an exact source or remains unresolved. [Preliminary inspection and leak analysis](#/document/G2214741)

verification.title: Any level check is fully closed
verification.body: Confirm the lubricant is within 9 mm (0.354 in.) of the fill opening and the fill plug is installed at 25 lb.ft (34 Nm). Reinspect the wiped plug area for fresh leakage. [Level check](#/document/G2214894) · [Leak analysis](#/document/G2214741)

verification.title: Unresolved concerns have a next action
verification.body: A confirmed leak, visible damage or unexplained noise needs the corresponding diagnosis or repair. Submersion needs prompt assessment even if the level is correct. [Axle diagnosis](#/document/G2214741) · [Ford water-exposure guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649140&Uid=G1634877&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

notes: Scope remains the 2015 Mustang with 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. Connection and support checks follow the equipment actually fitted.
Shaft removal, exhaust removal, U-joint replacement, runout correction and balancing are follow-up jobs, not routine inspection prerequisites.
guides.title: Driveshaft and U-joints: check movement, noise and mounting
guides.summary: Inspect the installed driveshaft, joints and supports on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. Check for damage, binding, unwanted movement and mounting problems, then choose the right diagnostic next step.
guides.introduction: A clunk is a clue, not a parts order. I start by checking what the driveshaft is actually doing before condemning an expensive length of metal. Ford’s diagnosis separates joint wear, support trouble, imbalance and incorrect angles because several different problems can deliver the same damn soundtrack. [Driveshaft diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
guides.why: The driveshaft runs lengthwise between the transmission and rear differential; it is separate from the two rear halfshafts leading toward the wheels. Its joints accommodate changes in alignment along that path. This inspection looks for physical trouble and connects it to the conditions that produce the noise or vibration. A clean-looking shaft alone does not rule out imbalance, excessive runout—wobble as it turns—or an angle problem. [Shaft layout and inspection](#/document/G2214730) [Diagnostic branches](#/document/G2214728)

when.summary: Inspect at each oil-change service. Predominantly towing or car-top-carrier use calls for more frequent inspection and service as needed.
notes: Lubricate only if the fitted joint has the specified grease fitting.

prepare.title: Record the symptom
prepare.detail: Note road speed, acceleration, steady cruise or coast, whether the noise occurs when selecting a gear, and any recent repairs. Keep the original tire pressures and vehicle load unchanged before the baseline vibration road test. [Initial vibration check](#/document/G2214730) [Repair history](#/document/G1693185)

prepare.title: Arrange proper underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a suitably rated twin-post hoist, with an operator who can position and secure the car correctly for inspection and manual shaft rotation. Ford also permits a frame hoist with jackstands and requires the driveshaft angle to remain close to its normal, vehicle-at-rest position. The emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this job. [Inspection support](#/document/G2214730) [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) [Hoist safety](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Confirm the applicable hoist setup
prepare.detail: Ford specifies NEUTRAL for hoist positioning in each applicable engine’s underbody service procedure: [2.3L setup](#/document/G1688079), [3.7L setup](#/document/G1688092), [5.0L setup](#/document/G1688106). Have the lift operator establish a secure setup that permits hand rotation before anyone works underneath. These setup references do not make exhaust removal part of this inspection.

prepare.title: Gather inspection equipment
prepare.detail: Have a light and a way to record findings; those are practical inspection aids. Wear eye and ear protection, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. No joint press, replacement bolts or dial indicator is needed for the installed visual and hand-rotation checks described here. [Protective equipment](#/document/G1693189) [Inspection method](#/document/G2214730)

steps.title: Describe the concern before changing anything
steps.body: Write down exactly when the clunk, shudder or vibration occurs. Include whether it began after other work. Ford calls for verifying the concern and checking obvious causes before pursuing deeper diagnosis; previous repairs can contribute to a new problem. An intermittent noise that is absent during testing is not sufficient grounds to order parts. [Inspection and verification](#/document/G2214728) [Diagnostic approach](#/document/G1693185)

steps.title: Establish a baseline when investigating vibration
steps.body: First look for obvious damage. If no finding requires correction before driving, reproduce the reported vibration during a road test and record the road speed and driving condition. Do this before making adjustments or changing tire pressure or vehicle load. Note whether the vibration follows road speed or changes with acceleration and deceleration; that distinction helps select the next test. Skip this road test when you are simply performing an inspection without a reported symptom. [Baseline vibration inspection](#/document/G2214730) [Correct obvious causes first](#/document/G2214728)

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working underneath. An unexpected start can seriously injure someone working around the driveline. Keep the engine off throughout the underbody inspection and hand-rotation checks. [Unexpected-start precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Lift the car and establish safe working access
steps.body:
Have the hoist operator use the lifting locations identified by the stamped triangles and position the adapters clear of suspension, exhaust, brackets and the rear axle cover. Confirm the hoist has adequate capacity for the car and its contents. Keep the driveshaft close to its normal vehicle-at-rest angle for inspection. Never get underneath a car supported only by a jack. [Lifting locations and clearance](#/document/G1663631) [Capacity and support safety](#/document/G1693189) [Inspection position](#/document/G2214730)

Use the NEUTRAL hoist setup applicable to the engine: [2.3L](#/document/G1688079), [3.7L](#/document/G1688092), [5.0L](#/document/G1688106). If the shaft cannot be turned by hand with the car securely supported, stop the rotation check and have the operator resolve the setup. Do not force the shaft or change the vehicle’s restraint arrangement while underneath.

steps.title: Follow the shaft from front to rear
steps.body: Locate the lengthwise shaft between the transmission and rear differential. Identify its end connections, the joints present, and the center bearing support if fitted. A U-joint has a cross carried in bearing cups between two fork-shaped yokes; other connections may use a constant-velocity joint or flexible coupling. Inspect the arrangement actually fitted rather than assuming every car has the same connections. Leave the shaft and its fasteners installed for these checks. [Shaft layout](#/document/G2214730) [Connection variants](#/document/G2214904) [U-joint construction](#/document/G2214732)

steps.title: Inspect the shaft tube and joint seating
steps.body: Use the light to examine the accessible shaft surfaces for damage, missing balance weights and undercoating on the shaft. Look at the U-joint bearing cups for visibly incorrect seating. Record the location of anything suspicious so it can be checked during rotation. Ford treats these findings as relevant to vibration; a damaged shaft calls for replacement rather than a balancing experiment. [Visual shaft inspection](#/document/G2214730) [Balance-related symptoms](#/document/G2214728)

steps.title: Check the mounting connections and center support
steps.body:
Look at the rear connection where the shaft meets the differential’s pinion flange—the bolted mating face at the differential input. Check for visibly loose or missing fasteners and an obviously disturbed connection. Inspect the front connection as well for obvious damage or incorrect attachment. Ford identifies loose rear pinion-flange bolts as a possible cause of cruising vibration. Do not loosen fasteners merely to inspect them. [Connection inspection](#/document/G1693185) [Cruising-vibration diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)

If a center bearing is fitted, examine its insulating support for wear or damage. Record a damaged support separately from a damaged shaft tube; they lead to different observations even when both produce vibration. [Center support check](#/document/G2214728)

steps.title: Inspect the flexible coupling if fitted
steps.body: Examine the visible flexible coupling for cracks. Ford’s replacement decision is direct: a cracked coupling needs replacement. Record the finding and arrange that repair; this inspection does not require disconnecting the coupling to inspect its exposed surfaces. [Flexible coupling inspection](#/document/G2214904)

steps.title: Rotate slowly and feel for joint trouble
steps.body:
With the engine off and the car securely configured for hand rotation, turn the driveshaft slowly by hand. Examine the surfaces that were previously hidden. Feel for binding and end play at the U-joint trunnions—the short bearing journals on the joint’s cross. End play means movement along those journals; binding means the joint resists movement instead of moving smoothly. Note where either occurs. Ford supplies an observational check here, not a numerical play allowance. [Hand-rotation inspection](#/document/G2214730)

Also check for rough operation at the center bearing, if fitted, and inspect the CV joints and U-joints for wear or damage. A smooth hand check does not, by itself, clear every possible cause of vibration. [Bearing and joint checks](#/document/G2214728)

steps.title: Choose the next action from the findings
steps.body:
Match the observations to the diagnostic decisions below. Correct a confirmed visible cause before moving into more testing. If the installed inspection does not explain a persistent vibration, the next branch may be measured runout, balance or driveline angles—not automatically a replacement shaft. Runout is the amount the shaft wanders as it rotates; angle diagnosis checks the relationship between the transmission, shaft and axle. [Diagnostic sequence](#/document/G2214728) [Runout escalation](#/document/G2214730) [Angle diagnosis](#/document/G2214729)

A grease fitting creates a separate lubrication requirement. Ford’s owner instructions call for lubrication where fittings exist; do not assume a joint without a fitting needs a homemade lubrication point. Record any fitted lubrication points for service using the correct lubricant and method. This article covers inspection, not an unspecified grease procedure. [Ford owner maintenance instructions](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Close the inspection and verify the outcome
steps.body:
Record which connections, shaft sections, joints and supports you checked, including any area you could not examine. This inspection leaves the assembly installed, so there is no removal sequence to reverse. Collect the light and other inspection items, clear everyone from underneath, and have the lift operator return the car to the ground.

After any corrective work, recheck the original concern at the road-test speed and driving condition that produced it. If the symptom remains, continue diagnosis. [Post-correction verification](#/document/G2214730) [Symptom verification](#/document/G2214728)

watchFor.title: A vibration that began after other work
watchFor.body: Include that work in the investigation. Incorrectly completed repairs can contribute to the current concern; timing is useful evidence, although it does not establish the cause by itself. [Repair history checks](#/document/G1693185)

watchFor.title: Disassembly creeping into an inspection
watchFor.body: Shaft removal, slip-yoke spline inspection and U-joint replacement are separate repair work. Ford requires replacement of removed driveshaft attachment bolts and, during U-joint repair, discarded snap rings. Do not undo them as an exploratory play check. [Shaft removal requirements](#/document/G2214904) [Joint repair requirements](#/document/G2214732)

watchFor.title: A vise offered as a convenient shaft holder
watchFor.body: Never grip the driveshaft assembly in vise jaws or a similar fixture. Local dents or fractures can lead to shaft failure while driving. [Driveshaft handling warning](#/document/G2214732)

watchFor.title: A persistent symptom with no visible damage
watchFor.body: That result calls for a more specific test. It does not prove the assembly is healthy, and it does not prove the shaft needs replacement. [Vibration diagnostic branches](#/document/G2214728)

procedures.purpose: Match the observed noise or vibration to the appropriate diagnostic branch.
Support the installed inspection and provide subsequent runout and balancing procedures when indicated.
Provide the separate angle-measurement procedure when symptoms and joint checks point there.
Provide connection details, coupling inspection and separate shaft removal and installation requirements.
Provide handling precautions and the separate U-joint repair procedure.

stepGroups.title: Establish the concern
stepGroups.summary: Capture the symptom and preserve a useful baseline.

stepGroups.title: Secure underbody access
stepGroups.summary: Prevent starting and establish the correct supported inspection position.

stepGroups.title: Inspect the installed assembly
stepGroups.summary: Check the shaft, connections, coupling, joints and center support.

stepGroups.title: Decide and finish
stepGroups.summary: Select further diagnosis where needed and verify completion.

diagnostics.finding: A loud clunk when shifting from REVERSE to DRIVE, or a clunk as the car starts moving after a stop.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies worn or damaged CV joints or U-joints; excessive joint play is specifically associated with the moving-off clunk. [Clunk diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
diagnostics.next: Use the joint inspection findings to confirm wear or damage. Arrange the indicated repair or shaft replacement when necessary; the noise alone is not confirmation. [Joint inspection and repair decision](#/document/G2214728)

diagnostics.finding: Binding or end play during slow hand rotation.
diagnostics.meaning: These are abnormal joint observations called out in Ford’s inspection. [Joint movement check](#/document/G2214730)
diagnostics.next: Record the affected joint and arrange component-specific repair assessment. Do not invent a numerical clearance or try to free the joint by force. [Inspection and corrective actions](#/document/G2214730)

diagnostics.finding: Damaged center-bearing insulation or rough bearing operation.
diagnostics.meaning: A worn or damaged center support is a listed cause of cruising vibration. [Center-bearing diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
diagnostics.next: Arrange the repair assessment Ford calls for, including shaft replacement where necessary. [Center support action](#/document/G2214728)

diagnostics.finding: Visibly loose rear flange bolts.
diagnostics.meaning: Loose pinion-flange attachment bolts can cause cruising vibration. [Flange diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
diagnostics.next: Have the attachment corrected to specification before further vibration diagnosis. If bolts are removed, Ford requires new bolts and its seating and tightening procedure. [Attachment repair requirements](#/document/G2214904)

diagnostics.finding: Cracks in a fitted flexible coupling.
diagnostics.meaning: The coupling fails Ford’s inspection criterion. [Coupling inspection](#/document/G2214904)
diagnostics.next: Arrange coupling replacement. [Replacement decision](#/document/G2214904)

diagnostics.finding: Coasting rumble or boom, or shaft damage, missing weights or undercoating.
