diagnostics.meaning: Ford associates the noise with possible imbalance and directs inspection for these physical conditions. [Rumble and balance diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
diagnostics.next: Address confirmed damage first. For unresolved vibration, proceed through measured runout and the applicable balancing diagnosis rather than attaching guessed weights. [Runout and balancing sequence](#/document/G2214730)

diagnostics.finding: A similar buzz during cruise and coast, or shudder during acceleration from a stop or low speed.
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect driveline angles are possible. Acceleration shudder can also involve binding or damaged joints. [Buzz and shudder diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
diagnostics.next: Check joint condition first, then arrange angle measurement when indicated. Angle testing requires its own level-surface, unloaded ride-height and tire-pressure setup. [Angle measurement prerequisites](#/document/G2214729)

diagnostics.finding: Cruising vibration remains after the installed inspection.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include shaft or pinion-flange runout, imbalance, incorrect angles and joint or support problems. [Cruising-vibration diagnosis](#/document/G2214728)
diagnostics.next: Select the appropriate measurement branch. Shaft runout uses a dial indicator at the front, center and rear of each shaft section; a numerical verdict requires the applicable specifications. [Runout measurement](#/document/G2214730)

verification.title: Document the physical checks
verification.body: Record shaft condition, balance-weight observations, joint seating, joint movement, visible attachments, coupling cracks and center-support condition. Distinguish a completed check from an inaccessible or incomplete one. [Inspection items](#/document/G2214730) [Support checks](#/document/G2214728) [Coupling criterion](#/document/G2214904)

verification.title: Confirm the original symptom after correction
verification.body: Repeat the relevant road-test condition after repairs. A continuing vibration requires further diagnosis even when the visual inspection is satisfactory. [Repair verification](#/document/G2214730)

verification.title: Give the result an honest conclusion
verification.body: For an inspection without a reported symptom, record the observed condition. For a noise or vibration complaint, record whether it was reproduced, whether a cause was confirmed, and what remains to be tested. [Verification sequence](#/document/G2214728)

notes: These inspection steps cover the original 2015 Mustang 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L scope; they do not extend applicability to other years.
Joint grease and differential lubricant serve different locations. A boot finding is not a differential-fluid filling instruction.
guides.title: Halfshaft boots: catch damage before the joint pays for it
guides.summary: Inspect the inner and outer rear halfshaft boots on both sides of your 2015 Mustang, covering the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. Look for damaged covers, displaced attachments and escaping grease, then separate boot concerns from differential-seal leaks.
guides.introduction: I start with the humble flexible covers around the rear halfshaft joints. They’re easy to overlook beside all that suspension hardware, but Ford specifically includes the constant-velocity (CV) joint boots in its visual inspection. A little careful looking beats the hell out of guessing which expensive part deserves replacing. [Halfshaft inspection](#/document/G2214769)
guides.why: The useful result is a clear finding: which boot is damaged, where a leak begins, or which surfaces still need a better view. Ford checks boots, joints, shafts and loose hardware together, then uses the actual symptom to guide further diagnosis. A boot inspection helps narrow the problem; it does not certify the joint’s internal condition. [Inspection and diagnosis](#/document/G2214769)

when.summary: Inspect the halfshaft boots at every oil-change service; investigate visible grease loss sooner.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail:
Arrange secure underside access with a hoist rated for the vehicle's weight, including cargo and modifications. Locate the triangles stamped into the body structure and position the lift adapters at the corresponding lifting points. Keep the arms clear of suspension parts, stabilizer brackets, steering and exhaust components; incorrect placement can damage parts or let the car shift or fall. [Marked lifting points and restrictions](#/document/G1663631) [Hoist precautions](#/document/G1693189)

If using a jack for access, work on a hard, level surface, use adequate lifting capacity, set the parking brake and block the wheels remaining on the ground. Support the car on proper stands before going underneath. Never rely on a jack alone, and do not use the emergency tire-changing jack for this inspection. [Jack and stand safety](#/document/G1693189) [Lifting restrictions](#/document/G1663631)

prepare.title: Prevent an unexpected start
prepare.detail: Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around or underneath the car. An unexpected start can seriously injure someone inspecting it. [Start prevention](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Bring viewing aids and protection
prepare.detail: A flashlight and inspection mirror are useful viewing aids; a phone can help record locations and findings. Wear eye and ear protection for service work, and protective gloves where you could contact sharp edges. No replacement parts or disassembly tools are needed for the visual inspection described here. [Personal protection](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Keep the job to inspection
prepare.detail: You are examining the installed halfshafts. The knuckle removal, pry bar and seal tools shown in the repair material belong to component replacement; they are not instructions for gaining inspection access. Keep the boots away from sharp edges and hot exhaust parts, which can damage them. [Halfshaft arrangement and handling](#/document/G2214772)

steps.title: Confirm the car is ready to inspect
steps.body: Before reaching underneath, confirm that secure support is already established, the ignition is off, the key is removed and remote start is disabled if equipped. Keep clear of hot exhaust components. If safe access is unavailable, have the inspection performed where the car can be properly supported. [Inspection safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Find both ends of each rear halfshaft
steps.body: Locate the differential between the rear wheels, then follow each halfshaft outward toward its wheel. Identify the flexible boot at the inner joint near the differential and the boot at the outer joint near the wheel. Make a four-location checklist: left inner, left outer, right inner and right outer. The installed arrangement is shown in Ford’s halfshaft illustrations. [Rear halfshaft layout](#/document/G2214772)

steps.title: Inspect the first boot’s folds and attachments
steps.body:
Use your light to examine the visible folds, the spaces between them and both ends where the boot attaches. Look for splits, holes, visibly damaged material, an end that has moved out of place or an attachment that appears displaced. Ford’s visual check includes the boots and surrounding hardware. Use the mirror to improve your view without levering against the shaft or pushing tools into the boot. [Visual inspection](#/document/G2214769)

Work around the visible circumference from different viewing angles. Do not call the boot sound if you have only seen its easiest face; record any area you cannot inspect.

steps.title: Look beyond the boot for escaping grease
steps.body: Examine the boot ends, joint housing and nearby surfaces for greasy deposits or a thrown pattern. Treat these as clues and trace them toward their apparent origin before wiping anything away. Record whether the material leads to a visible opening in the boot, an attachment area or somewhere else. This is a practical way to document Ford’s visual check for boot and joint damage; deposits alone do not establish which component has failed. [Boot and joint inspection](#/document/G2214769)

steps.title: Repeat at the other three locations
steps.body:
Give the other boot on that halfshaft and both boots on the opposite side the same examination. Check the folds, attachment areas and surrounding deposits at each location. Also note obvious shaft damage or visibly loose hardware without disturbing fasteners. Ford includes all of these in the initial inspection. [Inspection checklist](#/document/G2214769)

If a surface remains hidden, record the specific location and arrange a better supported viewing position. Do not remove suspension components for this visual inspection. [Halfshaft repair scope](#/document/G2214772)

steps.title: Separate the differential seal from the joint boot
steps.body:
At each inner joint, distinguish the flexible boot from the separate seal where the halfshaft enters the differential housing. Ford’s seal illustration identifies that housing opening. If wetness appears to begin there rather than at the boot, record a suspected halfshaft-seal leak. If the origin is obscured or uncertain, record that uncertainty instead of naming a failed part from appearance alone. [Halfshaft seal location](#/document/G2214752)

A housing-seal concern needs a different repair assessment from a damaged boot. Neither observation is an instruction to put lubricant into the boot.

steps.title: Choose the next action from the finding
steps.body:
For a damaged boot, displaced attachment or apparent grease escape, arrange assessment of the boot and CV joint rather than assuming a new cover alone settles the matter. Ford’s diagnostic path calls for inspecting joint wear or damage and replacing the rear halfshaft when necessary. [Joint assessment](#/document/G2214769)

Include any existing clunk, acceleration shudder or cruising-speed vibration in the report. Ford assigns different possible causes to those symptoms. Report them without assuming the boot finding explains them, and use the diagnostic decisions below to describe the concern accurately. [Symptom chart](#/document/G2214769)

steps.title: Finish with a complete inspection record
steps.body:
Record each of the four boot locations as either no visible defect found, a specific defect found or incompletely viewed. For a concern, note the exact location, apparent leak origin and any reported driving symptom; photographs are useful for comparison. Remove your viewing aids and confirm that nothing was disturbed or left beneath the vehicle before the lift operator returns the car to the ground.

This inspection removes no components, so there are no boot clamps, suspension fasteners or halfshaft retainers to reinstall. Any repair is a separate job. [Inspection scope](#/document/G2214769)

watchFor.title: Inspection tools becoming damage tools
watchFor.body: Keep sharp tools away from the flexible covers and avoid contact with hot exhaust parts. Ford warns that either can damage the boots. [Boot protection](#/document/G2214772)

watchFor.title: A clean-looking boot beside a driving complaint
watchFor.body: No visible defect does not resolve a clunk, shudder or vibration. Ford directs diagnosis by symptom when the cause is not visually evident. [Diagnostic sequence](#/document/G2214769)

watchFor.title: Inspection turning into lubrication
watchFor.body: Ford lists halfshaft-boot inspection separately from lubrication of components equipped with grease fittings. Do not interpret that schedule as an instruction to open or fill a boot. [Ford maintenance schedule](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

procedures.purpose: Identify the installed rear halfshaft arrangement and understand the separate component-replacement procedure.
Assess visible halfshaft concerns and route reported clunks, shudder or vibration.
Identify the differential-side halfshaft seal and route a confirmed seal leak to the appropriate repair.
Locate the marked lifting points and establish safe support for underside inspection.

stepGroups.title: Prepare and locate
stepGroups.summary: Establish safe access and identify the four boot locations.

stepGroups.title: Inspect both sides
stepGroups.summary: Examine the boots and trace suspicious deposits.

stepGroups.title: Decide and finish
stepGroups.summary: Choose the appropriate assessment and record what was actually checked.

diagnostics.finding: Split boot, displaced attachment or grease apparently escaping from a boot
diagnostics.meaning: There is a visible boot-area concern; the inspection does not establish the joint’s internal condition.
diagnostics.next: Arrange boot and joint assessment. Ford calls for joint inspection and rear halfshaft replacement when necessary, rather than automatic replacement based on a symptom alone. [Boot and joint diagnosis](#/document/G2214769)

diagnostics.finding: Wetness appears to begin where the halfshaft enters the differential
diagnostics.meaning: The separate halfshaft seal may be the source.
diagnostics.next: Have the leak origin confirmed and use the seal repair path if appropriate. [Rear halfshaft seal](#/document/G2214752)

diagnostics.finding: Loud clunk when shifting from reverse to drive
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies worn or damaged CV joints as a possible cause.
diagnostics.next: Have the CV joints inspected for wear or damage; replacement of the rear halfshaft depends on that assessment. [Clunk diagnosis](#/document/G2214769)

diagnostics.finding: Clunk as the vehicle starts moving forward after a stop
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies a loose hub nut as a possible cause.
diagnostics.next: Have the hub-nut torque checked against the correct specification. Ford requires a new hub nut if the torque is outside specification; this guide does not provide that repair specification. [Start-off clunk diagnosis](#/document/G2214769)

diagnostics.finding: Grunting with acceleration shudder from a stop, or vibration at cruising speed
diagnostics.meaning: Ford associates these symptoms with possible CV-joint binding; cruising vibration can also involve joint damage.
diagnostics.next: Have the outer CV joint’s seating in the hub checked and the concern diagnosed before selecting a repair. [Shudder and vibration diagnosis](#/document/G2214769)

diagnostics.finding: No visible damage or leakage
diagnostics.meaning: The inspected surfaces show no obvious defect; hidden surfaces and internal joint condition remain unverified.
diagnostics.next: Record the result. If a driving concern remains, continue symptom-based diagnosis. [Inspection and verification](#/document/G2214769)

verification.title: All four locations accounted for
verification.body: The record includes the left and right inner and outer boots, with any obscured areas explicitly identified. [Halfshaft arrangement](#/document/G2214772)

verification.title: Findings identify a location and next action
verification.body: Every concern distinguishes a boot-area finding, suspected differential-seal leak or unresolved source. Reported symptoms accompany the finding rather than being treated as proof of one failed part. [Diagnostic approach](#/document/G2214769) [Seal location](#/document/G2214752)

verification.title: The inspection ends without creating a repair
verification.body: Viewing aids are removed, nothing has been left underneath and no boot attachments or driveline fasteners have been disturbed. A visual pass is recorded as no visible defect, not a guarantee that the joint is healthy.

notes: Lubricate only a specified grease fitting where one is fitted. Do not generalize that instruction to boots or dry rubber bushings.
guides.title: Steering linkage: inspect the mechanical connection
guides.summary: Check the linkage and joints; the electric steering system has no hydraulic reservoir to top up.
guides.introduction: The steering gear moves the tie rods, which change the direction of the front wheels. Electric assistance reduces the effort at the steering wheel, but the mechanical joints still need to hold their geometry. A useful check considers looseness, damage and changing steering behavior rather than looking for a power-steering fluid service.
guides.why: A worn joint can allow wheel movement that was not requested at the steering wheel. Tire and suspension concerns can also affect steering feel, so diagnosis needs to consider the whole front end.

when.summary: Inspect steering linkage, ball joints and tie-rod ends at each oil-change service.
notes: The electric-assist system has no power-steering-fluid reservoir, top-up or flush interval.

prepare.title: Describe the feel
prepare.detail: Record a new pull, looseness, stiffness or knock and the conditions in which it occurs.

prepare.title: Confirm the exact component
prepare.detail: The steering column, steering gear and tie rods are related parts with different procedures.

steps.title: Inspect the mechanical system
steps.body: Check the linkage and joints according to the steering and suspension diagnostic instructions.

steps.title: Separate mechanical and assist concerns
steps.body: A warning or a change in electric assistance needs the power-steering diagnostic path; a suspected worn joint needs mechanical assessment.

steps.title: Verify the repair
steps.body: Use the correct replacement and alignment-related instructions, then confirm the original concern is resolved.

watchFor.title: A steering warning or marked change in effort
watchFor.body: Have the system assessed rather than looking for fluid to add.

watchFor.title: Play or damaged joint protection
watchFor.body: Identify the affected joint before ordering a gear assembly.

procedures.purpose: Service a tie-rod end.
Service the inner tie rod.
Follow power-steering diagnosis.
Understand electric steering operation.

notes: Suspension inspection is not permission to grease all bushings. Stabilizer-bar bushing care has a specific dry-installation rule.
guides.title: Suspension checks: follow wear, leaks and ride changes
guides.summary: Inspect arms, joints, springs, dampers and mountings as a connected system.
guides.introduction: The suspension keeps the tire controlled as the road and vehicle loads change. Arms locate the wheel, springs carry load and dampers control movement. Bushings and joints let the system move without losing its intended geometry. That is why a single clunk or uneven tire-wear pattern can have several possible causes.
guides.why: A worn mounting can make a good damper or arm seem faulty. Looking across the system helps connect a symptom to an actual finding.

when.summary: Inspect at each oil-change service. Investigate a new knock, unstable feeling, ride-height change or visible damage sooner.

prepare.title: Start with the basics
prepare.detail: Check tire pressure, approved tire size and loading before treating the suspension as the cause.

prepare.title: Record modifications
prepare.detail: Aftermarket springs, arms, wheels or other changes can affect which specifications apply.

steps.title: Describe and reproduce the concern safely
steps.body: Note road surface, speed and loading. Use the diagnostic path for the symptom rather than a guessed replacement list.

steps.title: Inspect component condition
steps.body: Check the arms, joints, bushings, dampers and fasteners for the wear, damage or leakage called out by diagnosis.

steps.title: Repair and verify
steps.body: Complete the correct component procedure and any required alignment checks. Confirm the car behaves as expected afterward.

watchFor.title: A recurring alignment complaint
watchFor.body: Worn or damaged parts need attention before an alignment can be relied on.

watchFor.title: Oil around a damper or visible damage
watchFor.body: Have the condition assessed; do not assign a universal replacement mileage to every shock or strut.

procedures.purpose: Identify the rear suspension arms, links and dampers.
Follow suspension inspection and symptom diagnosis.
Diagnose front suspension concerns.
Diagnose rear suspension concerns.

notes: The front performance-package restriction changes the repair choice; this article does not expand into a front bar-assembly replacement tutorial. [Front service restriction](#/document/G1692534)

The owner schedule includes suspension inspection at oil-change service. It does not list an automatic mileage-based stabilizer-bushing replacement. [Ford maintenance schedule](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)
guides.title: Stabilizer bushings: find the fault, skip the grease
guides.summary: Inspect the front and rear stabilizer bushings, separate noise from actual damage, and use the correct dry-installation procedure when replacement is needed.
guides.introduction: I start a suspension-noise hunt with a look underneath, not a shopping cart. A stabilizer bar helps control sway and body roll, but its bushings, links and mounting hardware are only some of the possible noise sources. A damn convincing clunk still needs evidence before it gets new parts. Parts roulette gets expensive fast. [Suspension diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)
guides.why: The bushings support the stabilizer bar inside its mounting brackets. Ford specifically prohibits lubricant on the bar and bushings because it can damage the bushings. The rear procedure allows water on the bracket during installation; that narrow exception does not authorize greasing the assembly. [Front bushings](#/document/G1692534) [Rear bushings](#/document/G1686652)

when.summary: Inspect with the suspension at oil service, or sooner when a clunk, loose handling or visible damage appears. Replace after inspection confirms a defect.
notes: There is no automatic mileage-based bushing replacement in this schedule.

prepare.title: Identify the car and the branch
prepare.detail: This guide covers the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. Identify the affected axle and confirm the front performance-package equipment before ordering parts: performance-package front bushings require replacement of the front stabilizer bar assembly. Aftermarket steering, suspension or wheel equipment requires its own applicable specifications. [Front service restriction](#/document/G1692534) [Equipment checks](#/document/G1686610)

prepare.title: Inspection equipment and safe access
prepare.detail: Have a tire-pressure gauge, eye and ear protection, and protective gloves for sharp-edged parts. Plan access with a suitably rated hoist and the marked lifting points. Inspection does not automatically require removing the air cleaner, coolant bottle or a wheel; those operations below belong to front bushing replacement. [Preliminary checks](#/document/G1686610) [Service safety](#/document/G1693189) [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631)

prepare.title: Replacement tools and parts
prepare.detail: Use hand tools that match the actual fasteners and torque wrenches covering the chosen branch. Front bracket bolts require 76 lb.ft (103 Nm); rear bracket bolts require 52 lb.ft (70 Nm). Front access also involves smaller fasteners specified below. Obtain vehicle-correct bushings and new bracket bolts before dismantling; removed bracket bolts are discarded. [Front replacement](#/document/G1692534) [Rear replacement](#/document/G1686652)

prepare.title: Materials for the chosen branch
prepare.detail: Keep lubricant away from the bar and bushings. Water is optional on rear brackets only. For 5.0L front replacement, have Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 for the wheel-pilot interface only, plus a torque wrench capable of 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) for the wheel nuts. [Rear installation](#/document/G1686652) [Wheel installation](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Confirm the symptom before choosing parts
steps.body: If the car is safe to drive, verify the concern on a smooth road. Note whether it occurs over bumps, while turning, braking or entering a driveway. Those conditions lead to different diagnostic possibilities; a noise alone does not identify a failed bushing. If an obvious loose or damaged component is already apparent, address that concern before a road test. [Suspension diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Check the easy impostors
steps.body: With the tires cold and the usual vehicle load aboard, check pressures and tire sizes against the vehicle certification label. Look for abnormal wear or damage and note uneven loading or aftermarket modifications. These checks matter particularly when the complaint includes sway, wandering or unusual handling. [Preliminary inspection](#/document/G1686610)

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around or underneath the car; an unexpected start can cause serious injury. Wear eye and ear protection, with gloves when handling sharp edges. For front underhood work, inspect the cooling fans with the ignition off: do not work beneath the hood with a damaged fan, and disable the fans before working near them because they can operate with the ignition off. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Establish safe underside access
steps.body:
For the hoist route, place the transmission in Neutral and use a hoist rated for the vehicle's weight, including cargo and modifications. Locate the triangles stamped into the body structure and position the lift adapters at the corresponding lifting points. Keep the arms clear of suspension parts, stabilizer brackets, steering and exhaust components; incorrect placement can damage parts or let the car shift or fall. [Hoist setup](#/document/G1686652) [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) [Hoist precautions](#/document/G1693189)

If using a jack for access, work on a hard, level surface, use adequate lifting capacity, set the parking brake and block the wheels remaining on the ground. Support the car on proper stands before going underneath. Never rely on a jack alone, and do not use the emergency tire-changing jack for this service. [Jack and stand safety](#/document/G1693189) [Lifting restrictions](#/document/G1663631)

steps.title: Inspect both supports and the neighboring links
steps.body: Remove excessive mud or road deposits that obscure the inspection. Follow the stabilizer bar across the affected axle and find the bushings held inside its mounting brackets. Examine both sides for visibly worn, damaged or displaced bushings, out-of-position isolators or locating features, and loose or damaged brackets and fasteners. Inspect the bar for damage or breakage and the links for visible wear, damage or displacement. The links are separate components; a link fault does not establish a bushing fault. [Inspection and noise checks](#/document/G1686610) [Front support arrangement](#/document/G1692534) [Rear support arrangement](#/document/G1686652)

steps.title: Choose the next action
steps.body: If the bushings and surrounding parts show no evident fault, leave them assembled and continue diagnosis of the reported symptom. Do not spray lubricant on them as a test or a cure. Replace confirmed worn or damaged components through the appropriate repair branch. For performance-package front bushings, stop at the bar-assembly service decision: the separate-bushing steps below do not apply. For serviceable front bushings, continue with steps 7–13; for rear bushings, use steps 14–16. Then complete steps 17–19. [Diagnostic decisions](#/document/G1686610) [Front restriction and lubrication rule](#/document/G1692534) [Rear lubrication rule](#/document/G1686652)

steps.title: Front replacement: remove the correct air cleaner
steps.body:
Use only the instructions for your engine.

**2.3L:** Keep debris out of every opened intake connection; even small particles can damage the turbocharger compressor. Loosen the outlet-pipe clamp and move the pipe aside. Detach the wiring-harness retainers, disconnect the intake-air-temperature (IAT) sensor connectors, remove the mounting bolt and lift out the air-cleaner assembly. [2.3L air cleaner](#/document/G1675705)

**3.7L:** Loosen the outlet-pipe clamp and move the pipe aside. Remove the mounting bolt and lift out the air-cleaner assembly. [3.7L air cleaner](#/document/G1675694)

**5.0L:** Loosen the outlet-pipe clamp and separate the pipe from the air cleaner. Disconnect the mass-airflow (MAF) sensor connector, detach the wiring harness from the cleaner and move it aside. Detach and move aside the sound symposer connection, then remove the mounting bolt and air cleaner. [5.0L air cleaner](#/document/G1675683)

steps.title: Front replacement: move the coolant reservoir aside
steps.body: Remove the degas-bottle mounting bolts and position the bottle aside. The degas bottle is the coolant reservoir shown at the front of the engine compartment. Move it carefully without straining its attached hoses; the bushing procedure calls for repositioning the bottle. [Front access](#/document/G1692534)

steps.title: 5.0L front replacement: open the left wheel access
steps.body:
On the 5.0L only, remove the left-hand wheel nuts and wheel with the car safely supported. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut: it can damage the wheel and bearing. Ford places the rearward front-bushing bracket bolt beneath the alternator and requires access through the wheel opening. [5.0L bolt access](#/document/G1692534) [Wheel removal](#/document/G1686507)

If fitted, move the left-side splash shield upward out of the way to reach that rearward bracket bolt. This is access to the same fastener, as described in the bar procedure. [Splash-shield access](#/document/G1692533)

steps.title: Front replacement: remove the brackets and bushings
steps.body: On both sides, remove and discard the front bushing bracket bolts. On the 5.0L, use the wheel-opening access for the rearward bolt as specified. Remove each bracket, then remove its bushing from the bar. Keep the removed bolts separate from reusable hardware so they cannot accidentally go back in. [Front bushing removal](#/document/G1692534)

steps.title: Front replacement: fit dry bushings with the slits rearward
steps.body: Install the vehicle-correct front bushings with their slits facing the rear of the car. Apply no lubricant to either the bushings or the bar; lubricant can damage the bushings. Fit the brackets and install new bracket bolts on both sides. Tighten the bolts to **76 lb.ft (103 Nm)**. On the 5.0L, install the rearward bolt through the wheel opening. [Front installation](#/document/G1692534)

steps.title: 5.0L front replacement: refit the left wheel
steps.body:
Return any repositioned splash shield to its fitted position and make sure its retainers are secure. [Shield access](#/document/G1692533)

Clean corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel and hub/brake-disc mounting faces, and ensure rotor-retaining fasteners cannot interfere with wheel seating. Contamination can allow the wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to detach. Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft XL-2 anti-seize **only between the wheel's center pilot bore and the hub pilot**. Keep it off mounting faces, studs, nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. Refit the wheel and install its nuts finger-tight. Final tightening comes in step 18 with the car resting on its tires. [Wheel installation](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Front replacement: restore the reservoir and intake
steps.body:
Return the degas bottle to its mounting position and tighten its bolts to **80 lb.in (9 Nm)**. [Reservoir installation](#/document/G1692534)

**2.3L:** Inspect the intake components and clean them if necessary while keeping debris out of the system. Refit the air cleaner and tighten its mounting bolt to **71 lb.in (8 Nm)**. Reconnect the IAT connectors and attach the harness retainers. Refit the outlet pipe and tighten its clamp to **48 lb.in (5.4 Nm)**. [2.3L installation](#/document/G1675705)

**3.7L:** Refit the air cleaner and tighten its mounting bolt to **71 lb.in (8 Nm)**. Refit the outlet pipe and tighten its clamp to **48 lb.in (5.4 Nm)**. [3.7L installation](#/document/G1675694)

**5.0L:** Refit the air cleaner and tighten its mounting bolt to **71 lb.in (8 Nm)**. Reattach the sound symposer and wiring harness, reconnect the MAF connector, and refit the outlet pipe. Tighten its clamp to **44 lb.in (5 Nm)**. [5.0L installation](#/document/G1675683)

steps.title: Rear replacement: remove the brackets and bushings
steps.body: With the vehicle in Neutral and safely positioned on the hoist, remove and discard the rear bushing bracket bolts on both sides. Remove the brackets, then remove both bushings from the bar. [Rear removal](#/document/G1686652)

steps.title: Rear replacement: face the slits forward
steps.body: Install the vehicle-correct rear bushings on both sides with their slits facing the **front** of the car. Keep the bar and bushings free of applied lubricant; lubrication can damage them. Confirm the direction before fitting the brackets, because the front and rear bushings use opposite slit orientations. [Rear bushing installation](#/document/G1686652) [Front orientation](#/document/G1692534)

steps.title: Rear replacement: install the brackets and new bolts
steps.body: Fit both rear brackets. Water may be applied to the brackets to help installation; keep that exception confined to the brackets. Install new bracket bolts and tighten them to **52 lb.ft (70 Nm)**. [Rear bracket installation](#/document/G1686652)

steps.title: Check the work and restore cooling-fan operation
steps.body:
Inspect both serviced supports: bushings seated inside the brackets, slits facing rearward at the front or forward at the rear, and new bracket bolts tightened to the correct axle-specific value. Confirm that no lubricant was applied to the bar or bushings. [Front assembly checks](#/document/G1692534) [Rear assembly checks](#/document/G1686652)

After front work, also check the reservoir mounting, outlet-pipe connection and every connector, harness attachment or sound-symposer connection disturbed in your engine branch. [Reservoir installation](#/document/G1692534) [2.3L intake](#/document/G1675705) [3.7L intake](#/document/G1675694) [5.0L intake](#/document/G1675683)

Before starting the engine, clear hands and tools from the fans and restore any cooling-fan connections or controls disabled for access. Confirm that the action used to disable the fans has been reversed so their operation is restored. Fans can run with the ignition off; keep clear once they are enabled. [Cooling-fan safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Lower the car and finish any wheel installation
steps.body: Clear people, tools and loose parts from the lifting area before lowering the car. For the 5.0L front branch, perform final wheel-nut tightening with the vehicle resting on its tires: tighten in a **star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm)**, with clean, dry stud and nut threads. The pattern helps prevent brake-disc runout and resulting vibration. Retighten the wheel nuts within **100 mi (160 km)** after refitting the wheel because they can loosen after initial installation. [Wheel tightening and follow-up](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Recheck the original concern
steps.body: Once assembly and fastener checks are complete, cooling-fan operation has been restored and no unresolved safety defect remains, repeat the smooth-road check and compare the original symptom. If the noise or handling concern persists, continue symptom-based diagnosis of the links, fasteners and other possible sources. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189) [Suspension diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)

watchFor.title: The grease-fitting instruction has limits
watchFor.body: The owner schedule calls for lubrication where grease fittings exist. It does not override the explicit prohibition on lubricating these stabilizer bars and bushings. [Ford maintenance schedule](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) [Front rule](#/document/G1692534) [Rear rule](#/document/G1686652)

watchFor.title: A slit is not automatically a tear
watchFor.body: These bushings have an intentional installation slit. Assess its location and surrounding condition rather than condemning the part simply because a split is visible. Front slits face rearward; rear slits face forward. [Front orientation](#/document/G1692534) [Rear orientation](#/document/G1686652)

watchFor.title: Inch-pounds and foot-pounds are different settings
watchFor.body: Reservoir, air-cleaner and intake-clamp specifications use lb.in; bracket and wheel specifications use lb.ft. Check the wrench's units before tightening. [Front fasteners](#/document/G1692534) [2.3L intake](#/document/G1675705) [3.7L intake](#/document/G1675694) [5.0L intake](#/document/G1675683) [Wheel nuts](#/document/G1686507)

procedures.purpose: Front bushing serviceability, access, dry installation, slit direction and bracket torque.
Rear bushing removal, slit direction, water-on-bracket exception and bracket torque.
Preliminary inspection and decisions separating bushing faults from other noise sources.
Correct lifting points and lifting restrictions.
Unexpected-start prevention, personal protection, lifting safety and cooling-fan precautions.
2.3L air-cleaner removal and explicit reinstallation.
3.7L air-cleaner removal and explicit reinstallation.
5.0L air-cleaner removal and explicit reinstallation.
5.0L left-wheel removal, installation, tightening and follow-up.
Conditional splash-shield access to the rearward front bracket bolt.

stepGroups.title: Inspect and choose the repair
stepGroups.summary: Establish safe access, inspect the actual parts and avoid diagnosing by noise alone.

stepGroups.title: Serviceable front bushings
stepGroups.summary: Use the correct engine access branch, then restore everything disturbed.

stepGroups.title: Rear bushings
stepGroups.summary: Install dry bushings facing forward and secure the brackets with new bolts.

stepGroups.title: Finish and verify
stepGroups.summary: Check assembly, restore cooling-fan operation, complete wheel tightening if applicable and reassess the symptom.

diagnostics.finding: A bushing is visibly worn, damaged or displaced.
diagnostics.meaning: There is an identifiable condition to address, rather than noise alone.
diagnostics.next: Use the appropriate axle procedure; a performance-package front bushing requires bar-assembly replacement. [Bushing diagnosis](#/document/G1686610) [Front restriction](#/document/G1692534)

diagnostics.finding: A bracket or fastener is loose.
diagnostics.meaning: Loose hardware is a possible source of rattle, clunk or excessive sway.
diagnostics.next: Correct the fastening concern to its applicable specification. If bushing bracket bolts are removed during this service, discard them and install new bolts using the axle-specific procedure. [Loose-hardware diagnosis](#/document/G1686610) [Front bolts](#/document/G1692534) [Rear bolts](#/document/G1686652)

diagnostics.finding: The bar is damaged or broken, or a link is worn or damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: Replacing only the support bushings will not repair the identified component.
diagnostics.next: Arrange the corresponding bar or link repair; those repairs are outside this bushing guide. [Component decisions](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: The bushings look correctly positioned and intact, but the noise remains.
diagnostics.meaning: The visual inspection has not established the cause. Several suspension and neighboring systems can produce similar symptoms.
diagnostics.next: Continue symptom-based diagnosis, including links and other relevant components. Do not replace bushings solely because the noise sounds plausible. [Noise diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)

diagnostics.finding: The suspension or stabilizer equipment is aftermarket.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford's stated specifications do not establish the requirements for modified equipment.
diagnostics.next: Identify the fitted components and obtain their applicable installation and inspection instructions before servicing them. [Aftermarket equipment](#/document/G1686610)

verification.title: The inspection produces a clear decision
verification.body: Record which axle and side showed damage, displacement or loose hardware—or that no visible bushing fault was found. Match the next repair to that finding. [Inspection decisions](#/document/G1686610)

verification.title: Bushing assembly is correct
verification.body: Confirm correct slit direction, no applied bar/bushing lubricant, and new bracket bolts tightened to 76 lb.ft (103 Nm) at the front or 52 lb.ft (70 Nm) at the rear. [Front installation](#/document/G1692534) [Rear installation](#/document/G1686652)

verification.title: Access components are restored
verification.body: After front replacement, confirm the reservoir and engine-specific intake assembly are secured and all disturbed connections are restored. If the left wheel was removed, complete its star-pattern tightening and arrange the required retightening within 100 mi (160 km). [Front reassembly](#/document/G1692534) [2.3L intake](#/document/G1675705) [3.7L intake](#/document/G1675694) [5.0L intake](#/document/G1675683) [Wheel follow-up](#/document/G1686507)

verification.title: Cooling-fan operation is restored before engine start
verification.body: Confirm that any cooling-fan connections or controls disabled for access have been restored and that the disabling action has been reversed. Keep hands and tools clear of the fans once enabled, including with the ignition off. Complete this check before starting the engine or road-testing. [Cooling-fan safety](#/document/G1693189)

verification.title: The symptom is reassessed
verification.body: Compare the post-service road check with the original concern. Persistent noise requires further diagnosis, even when the new bushings are installed correctly. [Suspension diagnosis](#/document/G1686610)

notes: This is a fluid-level inspection and correction guide, not a transmission fluid-and-filter replacement procedure.
The cold indicator area used during a repair refill serves a different purpose from the dotted B target used for the final hot check. [Refill versus final check](#/document/G1692052)
guides.title: Check and correct the 6R80 automatic transmission fluid level
guides.summary: Use a scan tool, the transmission’s short level indicator and the correct temperature window to check the level, adjust it and tighten the fill plug.
guides.introduction: I like a simple dipstick check. The 6R80 makes you earn it: the indicator lives at the transmission, and a useful reading depends on fluid temperature and the correct markings. Guessing by how many bottles went in is a damn expensive measuring system. This guide covers the 6R80 automatic in 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine; it does not cover the MT82 or 3160 manual transmission. [Level-check procedure](#/document/G1692053)
guides.why: Ford specifies an engine-running check at 96.7–102°C (206–215°F), with the fluid reaching the upper end of the indicator’s dotted B area. A low level can cause internal transmission failure, and overfilling is also prohibited. The temperature and the mark belong together: neither tells the whole story alone. [Level and temperature requirements](#/document/G1692053)

when.summary: The normal oil-service checklist includes transmission level inspection where applicable; use the 6R80-specific procedure to determine and perform the correct check.
notes: Investigate suspected leakage or a shift concern separately. This does not replace the fluid-and-filter replacement interval.

prepare.title: Scan tool and hoist
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool that displays transmission fluid temperature and a suitably rated hoist that provides safe access while keeping the vehicle level. Locate the triangle-marked lifting points before positioning the lift arms. Check adapter clearance around the suspension, exhaust, steering components and axle housing. [Check setup](#/document/G1692053) · [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) · [Hoist safety](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Plug tools and level indicator
prepare.detail: Use a tool that matches the actual fill plug and a torque wrench capable of 35 Nm (26 lb-ft). The level indicator is removed from the fill plug; identify the dotted B area and the separate crosshatched A area before measuring. [Plug and indicator](#/document/G1692053)

prepare.title: Equipment for correcting the level
prepare.detail: If adjustment is needed, have a universal fluid dispenser for adding fluid and a fluid suction gun for removing excess. Use Motorcraft MERCON LV automatic transmission fluid, XT-10-QLVC, specification WSS-M2C938-A. An incorrect fluid can cause abnormal operation or transmission failure. Ford recommends a pressurized dispenser with an 8–12 qt capacity; that is equipment capacity, not an instruction to add that amount. [Fluid and adjustment equipment](#/document/G1692052)

prepare.title: Personal protection and controlled access
prepare.detail: Have eye and ear protection, and protective gloves for handling sharp-edged parts. Review the fluid’s safety information. Plan access around a running engine and fluid at the specified hot checking temperature; avoid contact with hot fluid and components. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189) · [Checking temperature](#/document/G1692053)

steps.title: Confirm this is a level check
steps.body: Use this sequence for checking and correcting an assembled transmission. If its pan or filter has been removed, its main control replaced, or the transmission overhauled, complete the applicable refill procedure first. The refill procedure’s initial quantities and cold indicator position are not routine top-up targets. Its full air-purge sequence is expressly separate from an ordinary level check. [Refill distinctions](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Disable remote start and set up the hoist
steps.body: Before working around or underneath the car, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup, if equipped. An unexpected remote start can seriously injure someone servicing the vehicle. Connect the scan tool and position the car on the hoist. Confirm adequate lift capacity and place the arms at the triangle-marked lifting points; incorrect support can let the car shift or fall. All drive wheels must be clear of the ground before the running engine is allowed to power them during selector cycling. Never work underneath a car supported only by a jack, and do not use the emergency tire jack for this job. [Remote-start and hoist precautions](#/document/G1693189) · [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) · [Check setup](#/document/G1692053)

steps.title: Run through the selector positions
steps.body: With the engine running, move the selector through every gear position, holding each position for approximately five seconds. Return it to PARK and keep the engine running for the check. Keep everyone clear beneath the vehicle while changing selector positions. [Selector sequence](#/document/G1692053)

steps.title: Watch the transmission temperature
steps.body: Monitor transmission fluid temperature on the scan tool. The valid checking window is 96.7–102°C (206–215°F). After extended high-speed driving, city traffic, hot-weather use or towing, the fluid may need to cool before a valid reading is possible. Do not substitute engine coolant temperature or accept an out-of-window reading as the final result. Do not drive the car if its transmission fluid level is confirmed low. [Temperature and low-level precautions](#/document/G1692053)

steps.title: Remove the fill plug and use its indicator
steps.body: Locate the fill plug on the side of the transmission case, just above the pan, as shown in Ford’s illustration. Remove the plug, then remove the short level indicator from it. Insert the indicator into the fill opening in the checking position shown, then withdraw it to read the fluid trace. Keep clear of hot fluid and nearby components while reaching the opening. [Plug location and indicator use](#/document/G1692053)

steps.title: Read the dotted B area
steps.body: With the engine still running in PARK, confirm the scan tool shows 96.7–102°C (206–215°F). Read the dotted B area, not the crosshatched A area. The correct level reaches the upper end of the dotted B markings. Below that target requires adding fluid; above it requires removing fluid. If the temperature has left the window, restore the checking conditions before deciding how much correction is needed. [Correct markings and reading conditions](#/document/G1692053)

steps.title: Correct a low reading
steps.body: If the reading is low, use the fluid dispenser to add Motorcraft MERCON LV, XT-10-QLVC, meeting WSS-M2C938-A, through the fill opening. Recheck with the level indicator and scan tool, continuing until the fluid reaches the upper end of dotted B within the specified temperature window. There is no fixed top-up quantity: the measured result determines when to stop. Do not drive with a confirmed low level; internal failure can result. [Adding fluid](#/document/G1692052) · [Final level target](#/document/G1692053)

steps.title: Correct an overfilled reading
steps.body: If the reading is above the target, use a fluid suction gun through the fill opening to remove excess fluid. Recheck the indicator and transmission fluid temperature, repeating the correction until the level reaches the upper end of dotted B at 96.7–102°C (206–215°F). Removing excess does not require dropping the transmission pan. [Removing excess fluid](#/document/G1692052) · [Final reading](#/document/G1692053)

steps.title: Reassemble and finish
steps.body: Return the level indicator to the fill plug and install the plug assembly. Tighten the fill plug to 35 Nm (26 lb-ft). Check the closed opening for fresh leakage, then shut down the engine and lower the vehicle using the hoist’s operating instructions. As a useful completion note, record the final fluid temperature, the level reached and whether fluid was added or removed. [Indicator assembly and plug tightening](#/document/G1692053)

watchFor.title: New cooler or cooler tubes
watchFor.body: If a new transmission fluid cooler or cooler tubes have been installed, Ford requires driving until transmission fluid reaches 96.7–102°C (206–215°F) to purge cooling-system air before accepting the final level. Establish the safe pre-drive level through the applicable refill procedure first; never road-drive a confirmed low transmission. [Cooler replacement requirement](#/document/G1692053) · [Refill and pre-drive level](#/document/G1692052)

watchFor.title: A refill quantity masquerading as a level check
watchFor.body: Initial refill quantities apply to particular repair states. They do not establish the correct final level and must not be added wholesale during this check. Finish by temperature and dotted B, not bottle arithmetic. [Refill quantities and final check](#/document/G1692052)

watchFor.title: Slip, slow shifts or leakage
watchFor.body: These are reasons to check the fluid level. Correcting a low reading does not establish why fluid was lost or prove a shift problem has been repaired. Arrange diagnosis if leakage or symptoms remain. [Reasons to check](#/document/G1692052)

procedures.purpose: Check the 6R80 fluid level at the specified temperature and secure the fill plug.
Use the specified fluid and equipment to add fluid or extract excess; distinguish correction from a repair refill.
Identify lifting points and protect the vehicle during access.
Apply remote-start, personal-protection and hoist safety requirements.

stepGroups.title: Establish safe checking conditions
stepGroups.summary: Confirm the service state, support the car and prepare the running transmission.

stepGroups.title: Measure the fluid level
stepGroups.summary: Use the case-mounted indicator and the correct hot-level markings.

stepGroups.title: Adjust and close
stepGroups.summary: Correct the measured level, repeat the check and secure the fill plug.

diagnostics.finding: Fluid reaches the upper end of dotted B at 96.7–102°C (206–215°F), with the engine running in PARK.
diagnostics.meaning: The level meets the specified checking target.
diagnostics.next: Reassemble the indicator and fill plug, and tighten the plug to 35 Nm (26 lb-ft). [Level and closure](#/document/G1692053)

diagnostics.finding: Fluid is below the dotted B target at the correct temperature.
diagnostics.meaning: The transmission fluid level is low.
diagnostics.next: Add the specified MERCON LV fluid with the dispenser and repeat the check. Do not drive until corrected; investigate suspected leakage separately. [Level warning](#/document/G1692053) · [Fluid correction](#/document/G1692052)

diagnostics.finding: Fluid is above the dotted B target at the correct temperature.
diagnostics.meaning: The transmission is overfilled.
diagnostics.next: Remove excess with a fluid suction gun and repeat the temperature-controlled check. [Overfill correction](#/document/G1692052)

diagnostics.finding: The scan tool shows a temperature outside the checking window, or the reading was taken from crosshatched A.
diagnostics.meaning: That result does not establish the specified final level.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the reading at 96.7–102°C (206–215°F), using dotted B. Allow overheated fluid to cool first. [Valid reading conditions](#/document/G1692053)

verification.title: Final reading confirmed
verification.body: Before closing the opening, confirm the engine is running in PARK, transmission fluid temperature is 96.7–102°C (206–215°F), and fluid reaches the upper end of dotted B. Repeat this check after any addition or extraction. [Final level check](#/document/G1692053)

verification.title: Indicator and plug restored
verification.body: Confirm the indicator is back in its plug and the fill plug is tightened to 35 Nm (26 lb-ft). Visually check for fresh fluid at the closed opening. [Closure specification](#/document/G1692053)

verification.title: Unresolved symptoms recorded
verification.body: Note any remaining leakage, slipping or slow shifts so they receive diagnosis rather than another hopeful splash of fluid. Ford identifies these symptoms as reasons to check the level. [Symptom guidance](#/document/G1692052)

notes: Keep the cabin filter and engine air filter distinct when buying parts and recording maintenance. Ford lists them as separate service items. [Ford maintenance schedule](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)
guides.title: Cabin air filter: replace the element and button up the passenger footwell
guides.summary: Replace the cabin filter through the right lower dashboard, then refit its cover and insulating panel and check ventilation.
guides.introduction: I like to keep this job focused: one filter, its cover, and the panel underneath the passenger-side dashboard. No parts-cannon bullshit if the original airflow complaint survives. This guide covers the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine, using the same cabin-filter access and replacement sequence. [Cabin-filter procedure](#/document/G1676759)
guides.why: The cabin filter is the replaceable element in the climate-control housing. Changing it gives you a chance to inspect the old element and fit a fresh replacement behind its cover. [Filter location and replacement](#/document/G1676759) Ford lists the cabin filter separately from the engine air filter, so confirm you have the cabin part before opening anything. [Ford maintenance schedule](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

when.summary: Replace every 20,000 mi (32,000 km) in normal use.
notes: Dusty conditions can require earlier inspection and replacement. Frequent inspection is also called for with extensive low-speed commercial use.

prepare.title: Have the replacement and suitable retainer tools ready
prepare.detail: Get a cabin filter confirmed for your specific vehicle. Follow its markings and installation instructions for orientation. Match any tool to the retainers actually fitted; do not assume a screwdriver size or fastener type. The job removes two lower-panel retainers and one filter-cover retainer. [Access illustrations and procedure](#/document/G1676759)

prepare.title: Make room under the passenger-side dashboard
prepare.detail: RH means right-hand side. Locate the lower instrument-panel insulator—the panel beneath the dashboard—and clear enough footwell space to reach it and keep the removed panel and retainers together. The filter cover is behind this panel. [Passenger-side access](#/document/G1676759)

prepare.title: Make access safe before reaching underneath
prepare.detail: Disable remote start through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup, turn the ignition off, and remove the key from the vehicle. An unexpected start during service can cause serious injury or death. Wear eye protection, and use protective gloves when handling parts with sharp or pointed edges. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Remove the right lower dashboard insulator
steps.body: Support the lower insulator while removing its two retainers, then remove the panel. Keep the retainers with it so both are ready for reassembly. The first illustration identifies the panel and marks the retainer count as ×2. [Lower-panel removal](#/document/G1676759)

steps.title: Remove the cabin-filter cover
steps.body: Locate the long, narrow cover with the honeycomb-patterned face shown in the second illustration. Remove its single retainer, then remove the cover to expose the filter. Keep the cover and its retainer together. [Filter-cover removal](#/document/G1676759)

steps.title: Withdraw the old element and look it over
steps.body: Remove the cabin filter from the exposed opening shown in the third illustration. [Filter removal](#/document/G1676759) As a practical condition check, look for collected dirt, torn material or a distorted frame. Note what you find, but do not use the amount of visible dirt alone to declare an airflow complaint solved.

steps.title: Fit the correct replacement
steps.body: Compare the replacement’s dimensions and frame shape with the removed element and confirm its vehicle application. Follow the replacement component’s markings and instructions for orientation; do not guess an airflow-arrow direction from the illustration. Install the replacement in the filter opening. Before closing it, check that the element sits in place without a folded edge or crushed frame. [Filter installation](#/document/G1676759)

steps.title: Refit the filter cover and its retainer
steps.body: Return the filter cover to its original position over the opening, making sure the element is not caught between the cover and housing. Reinstall the single cover retainer and secure the cover. Check that it sits properly without being forced into place. [Reverse-order cover installation](#/document/G1676759)

steps.title: Reinstall the lower insulator
steps.body: Return the right lower instrument-panel insulator to its original position. Align its attachment points and reinstall both retainers. Check that the panel is supported at both locations and that neither retainer is left over. [Lower-panel installation](#/document/G1676759)

steps.title: Check the assembled result
steps.body: Remove your tools and the old filter from the footwell. As a practical completion check, switch on the ventilation and try your usual fan settings. Check for airflow and any new rattle or flutter. If something changed unexpectedly, switch the ventilation off and repeat the safe setup before reopening the access area. Recheck the filter, cover and panel using the same removal and installation sequence. [Access and reassembly sequence](#/document/G1676759) [Safe setup](#/document/G1693189)

watchFor.title: A replacement that needs force to fit
watchFor.body: Pause and check the application, dimensions and component instructions. A folded edge or crushed frame is a reason to correct the fit before reinstalling the cover. [Filter installation](#/document/G1676759)

watchFor.title: Damaged attachment points
watchFor.body: While handling the cover and insulator, look for broken retainers or damaged mounting points. Resolve a damaged attachment before calling the reassembly complete; these parts must be secured again. [Cover and insulator installation](#/document/G1676759)

watchFor.title: A symptom that survives the service
watchFor.body: Treat unchanged airflow, odor or temperature as an unresolved complaint. Recheck your installation first; further diagnosis belongs to the remaining symptom, rather than another round of filter guessing.

procedures.purpose: Cabin-filter access, removal and reverse-order installation.
Task-relevant unexpected-start and personal-protection precautions.

stepGroups.title: Open the access
stepGroups.summary: With the safe setup complete, remove the lower panel and filter cover.

stepGroups.title: Inspect and replace the element
stepGroups.summary: Look over the removed filter and fit the correct replacement.

stepGroups.title: Close up and check
stepGroups.summary: Secure the cover and lower panel, then check ventilation.

diagnostics.finding: The removed filter has visible dirt or damaged material.
diagnostics.meaning: You have a useful record of its condition, but that observation alone does not establish the cause of a ventilation complaint.
diagnostics.next: Install the correct replacement, finish reassembly and compare ventilation afterward. [Replacement sequence](#/document/G1676759)

diagnostics.finding: The replacement will not sit properly or the cover will not return to position.
diagnostics.meaning: Part fit or seating remains unresolved.
diagnostics.next: Remove the replacement and recheck its application and markings. Correct the fit before securing the cover. [Filter and cover installation](#/document/G1676759)

diagnostics.finding: A new rattle or flutter appears after replacement.
diagnostics.meaning: The assembly needs another check; the sound alone does not identify the cause.
diagnostics.next: Switch the ventilation off, repeat the safe setup, and inspect the element seating, cover retainer and both insulator retainers. [Safe setup](#/document/G1693189) [Access and installation](#/document/G1676759)

diagnostics.finding: The filter, cover and panel are correctly fitted, but the original complaint remains.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement has not resolved that complaint.
diagnostics.next: Continue diagnosis of the remaining airflow, odor or temperature symptom instead of assuming another filter will fix it.

verification.title: Element and cover are fitted
verification.body: Before fitting the lower panel, confirm the replacement is seated without a folded edge and the filter cover is back in position with its single retainer secured. [Filter installation](#/document/G1676759)

verification.title: Lower panel is secured
verification.body: Confirm the right lower insulator is installed with both retainers, and account for the removed parts and tools. [Insulator installation](#/document/G1676759)

verification.title: Ventilation has been checked
verification.body: Run the ventilation at your usual settings and note whether the original symptom improved, remained unchanged or was joined by a new noise. Record any remaining complaint for follow-up.

notes: The linked air-cleaner procedures cover complete assembly access. Routine element service does not automatically require every full-assembly removal operation.
guides.title: Engine air filter: change the element, protect the intake
guides.summary: Keep incoming dirt out while preserving the correct seal and duct connections for your engine.
guides.introduction: The engine needs air, but abrasive dirt should stay on the dirty side of the air-filter element. The housing, element and connected ducting form one path. A fresh element helps only if it sits correctly and the housing is closed as intended.
guides.why: A damaged, poorly seated or heavily loaded element changes how the intake is protected. The air-cleaner housing is normally a reusable assembly; the scheduled replacement item is the filter element.

when.summary: Replace the element every 30,000 mi (48,000 km) in normal use.
notes: Predominantly dusty or sandy use: inspect at 15,000 mi (24,000 km) and replace as needed.

prepare.title: Identify the engine and element
prepare.detail: The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L air-cleaner arrangements differ.

prepare.title: Keep the clean side clean
prepare.detail: Prepare a clean work area so debris is not introduced while the housing is open.

steps.title: Access the correct housing
steps.body: Use the engine-specific air-cleaner instructions to understand the clips, connections and cover arrangement.

steps.title: Inspect and replace the element
steps.body: Check the removed element and its seating area; install the correct new element securely.

steps.title: Restore the intake path
steps.body: Close the housing and verify any connections disturbed during access. Avoid leaving an opening or poorly seated duct.

watchFor.title: An element that does not sit naturally
watchFor.body: Recheck the part and orientation rather than forcing the cover closed.

watchFor.title: An ongoing performance concern
watchFor.body: Replacing a dirty filter is maintenance; a remaining symptom still needs diagnosis.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L air-cleaner arrangement and access.
3.7L air-cleaner arrangement and access.
5.0L air-cleaner arrangement and access.

notes: These time and mileage intervals are for the stated 2015 base engines. They do not establish a 5.2L schedule.
guides.title: Coolant replacement: fluid choice and trapped air matter
guides.summary: Refresh the coolant at its time-or-distance deadline and use the correct filling and bleeding process.
guides.introduction: Coolant carries heat and helps protect the cooling system’s internal surfaces. A replacement renews the fluid, but the job is not finished merely because the reservoir looks full. The system also needs the specified concentration and a filling method that removes trapped air.
guides.why: Air pockets and incorrect coolant can undermine an otherwise sound cooling system. The correct procedure is as important as choosing the bottle with the right specification.

when.summary: First replacement: six years or 100,000 mi (160,000 km). Afterward: every three years or 50,000 mi (80,000 km), whichever comes first.
notes: Use elapsed time from the actual replacement when planning the next service.

prepare.title: Let the engine cool
prepare.detail: Opening a hot pressurized cooling system can cause serious burns.

prepare.title: Gather the specified fluid and equipment
prepare.detail: Read the engine-specific draining, vacuum-filling and bleeding instructions before starting. Arrange collection and proper disposal of old coolant.

steps.title: Confirm the service history and fluid
steps.body: Identify what is due and use the required coolant for the engine.

steps.title: Drain and refill by the correct procedure
steps.body: Follow its access, draining, filling-equipment and bleeding requirements in order.

steps.title: Complete the final checks
steps.body: Verify the final level and absence of leaks as directed, then record the date, mileage and coolant used.

watchFor.title: Repeated coolant loss
watchFor.body: Find and repair the cause; a scheduled fluid replacement is not a leak repair.

watchFor.title: Unstable temperature after service
watchFor.body: Stop and assess the filling/bleeding result rather than assuming the new coolant solved the issue.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.
3.7L draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.
5.0L draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.

notes: Scope: 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L EcoBoost, 3.7L V6 or 5.0L V8. Follow only the matching engine branch.
The existing maintenance schedule remains separate from this procedure. Scheduled plug renewal and diagnosis of a running problem are different decisions.
guides.title: Spark plugs: fresh sparks without the parts-cannon bullshit
guides.summary: Replace the spark plugs on a 2015 Mustang using the separate 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L procedure, including coil access, plug gaps, tightening and reassembly.
guides.introduction: I treat scheduled plug replacement and misfire diagnosis as two different jobs. This guide handles renewal: get access, keep dirt out, fit the correct plugs and put everything back properly. A shopping cart full of ignition parts is a damn expensive diagnostic tool.
guides.why: The plug’s electrode gap and installation torque are engine-specific. So is access: the 3.7L requires upper intake manifold removal to reach the right-hand coils, while the other engines have different cover and tube arrangements. Choose one engine branch and stay with it. [2.3L plugs](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L coil access](#/document/G1675558), [5.0L coil access](#/document/G1675574)

when.summary: Replace every 100,000 mi (160,000 km) in normal use.
notes: Predominantly towing/car-top-carrier use or extensive idling/low-speed commercial use: 60,000 mi (96,000 km).

prepare.title: Get the correct plugs
prepare.detail: Ford’s 2015 owner information lists four SP-537 / CYFS-12Y-2 plugs for the 2.3L, six SP-520 / CYFS-12F-5 plugs for the 3.7L and eight SP-519 / CYFS-12Y plugs for the 5.0L. Match the replacement to the actual vehicle and follow its handling instructions. The workshop specification’s shared number 12405 does not distinguish these engine-specific choices. [Ford Motorcraft parts](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?variantid=3259&languageCode=en&countryCode=USA&moidRef=G1517147&Uid=G1634835&ProcUid=G1642992&userMarket=usa&div=f&vFilteringEnabled=False&buildtype=web), [2.3L quantity](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L quantity](#/document/G1675559), [5.0L quantity](#/document/G1675575)

prepare.title: Prepare hand tools and measuring equipment
prepare.detail: Have hand tools that fit the actual plugs and fasteners, a suitable plug-gap measuring tool, compressed air, and a torque wrench covering the specified low tightening values. The plug illustrations prohibit an impact wrench. The 3.7L and 5.0L also require a way to measure the additional tightening angles. Match socket and fastener sizes on the vehicle rather than guessing. [2.3L plugs](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L plugs](#/document/G1675559), [5.0L plugs](#/document/G1675575), [3.7L coil tightening](#/document/G1675558), [5.0L coil tightening](#/document/G1675574)

prepare.title: Know the plug gaps before opening the boxes
prepare.detail: 2.3L: 0.0295 in (0.75 mm). 3.7L: 0.049–0.053 in (1.25–1.35 mm). 5.0L: 0.049–0.053 in (1.25–1.35 mm). Check the replacement plugs against the appropriate specification; follow the replacement manufacturer’s handling instructions rather than bending electrodes by guesswork. [2.3L specifications](#/document/G1673181), [3.7L specifications](#/document/G1675554), [5.0L specifications](#/document/G1675570)

prepare.title: Add the 3.7L access supplies
prepare.detail: For the 3.7L, obtain new upper intake manifold gaskets, a hose clamp remover/installer, and clean blanking plugs for the opened vapor connection. The removed manifold gaskets must be discarded. Have suitable supplies ready to clean the upper and lower manifold sealing surfaces. [Upper intake manifold](#/document/G1681529), [Coupling cleanliness](#/document/G1671536)

prepare.title: Prepare for vapor-tube connections
prepare.detail: The 3.7L manifold access involves an EVAP purge connection; EVAP handles fuel vapor. The 5.0L involves PCV and crankcase ventilation connections. Have clean blanking plugs ready for open connections. These procedures require battery ground disconnection, clean coupling retainers and hand-operated releases. Tools can distort the clips and cause leaks. Fuel-pressure release is specified for liquid-fuel connections; these plug-access steps do not instruct you to open a liquid-fuel line. [3.7L manifold connections](#/document/G1681529), [3.7L couplings](#/document/G1671536), [5.0L coil access](#/document/G1675574), [5.0L couplings](#/document/G1671557)

prepare.title: Recognize the coupling before releasing it
prepare.detail: Keep the release styles separate. On the illustrated side-tab style, release both side tabs first, raise the retainer next, then separate the coupling; reconnect it straight onto the tube and press the retainer fully home. On the lower-release style, press the lower release point before lifting the retainer; reconnect straight onto the tube, then press the retainer down. A single locking-tab style releases by finger pressure; hold that tab released during connection and return it to its locking position afterward. Other illustrated styles use two release points before moving their retainer: complete that sequence before separating them, and restore their retainer after connection. A fitting with separate primary and secondary locks requires the secondary lock released first, the primary tab depressed second, and separation third; reconnect, pull-check it, then secure the secondary lock. Never borrow one style’s latch movement for another. [3.7L coupling actions](#/document/G1671536), [5.0L coupling actions](#/document/G1671557)

steps.title: Make the underhood area safe
steps.body: Switch the ignition off and remove the key. If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup so the engine cannot be started remotely during the job. Wear eye and ear protection, particularly when using compressed air, and protective gloves around sharp edges. Inspect the cooling fan with the ignition off; do not work under the hood with a damaged fan. Fans can operate with the ignition off, so disable them before working nearby. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Wait for the correct engine temperature
steps.body: Remove plugs only when the engine is warm to hand touch after cooling down. Do not remove them from a hot engine or one that is cold soaked: either condition can damage the plug threads or cylinder head. Recheck this immediately before loosening the plugs, especially after the longer 3.7L access work. [2.3L removal precautions](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L removal precautions](#/document/G1675559), [5.0L removal precautions](#/document/G1675575)

steps.title: Disconnect battery power, then choose your branch
steps.body: Remove the battery-cover retainers and cover. Loosen the negative cable clamp nut, remove the negative cable from its terminal and position it aside so it cannot reconnect accidentally. Leave the positive cable connected; negative disconnection is sufficient to interrupt vehicle power. This is required directly by the 2.3L coil procedure and by the coupling procedures used for 3.7L and 5.0L access. Continue with steps 4–9 for the 2.3L, 10–21 for the 3.7L, or 22–27 for the 5.0L. All branches finish at step 28. [Battery disconnection](#/document/G1692356), [2.3L coils](#/document/G1673188), [3.7L couplings](#/document/G1671536), [5.0L couplings](#/document/G1671557)

steps.title: 2.3L: remove the appearance cover and release the wiring
steps.body: Remove the engine appearance cover’s retaining nuts, then its retaining bolts, and lift off the cover. Release the wiring harness retainers. If a coil connector has a sliding cover over its locking tab, slide the cover back to expose the tab. Depress the connector locking tab and disconnect each of the four coil connectors. [2.3L coil access](#/document/G1673188)

steps.title: 2.3L: clean around and remove the coils
steps.body: Use compressed air to clear foreign material from the coils and surrounding area before removing them. Remove the coil mounting bolts. Give each coil a slight twist to release its seal, then remove it. Keep the coils organized by their original positions as a practical way to avoid mixing up observations. [2.3L coil removal](#/document/G1673188)

steps.title: 2.3L: clear the wells and remove four plugs
steps.body: Confirm the engine is still warm to hand touch. With the plugs still installed, blow foreign material out of each plug well—the recess surrounding the plug—before loosening anything. Remove the four plugs with hand tools. Keep dirt out of the open holes. If any plug is dropped, discard it: hidden internal damage can cause a misfire and subsequent engine damage. [2.3L plug removal](#/document/G1673189)

steps.title: 2.3L: check and install the replacement plugs
steps.body: Confirm a gap of 0.0295 in (0.75 mm). Guide each correct replacement plug into its hole and start its threads by hand; if it will not turn freely, stop and resolve the alignment or thread problem rather than forcing it. Tighten each plug to 106 lb.in (12 Nm). Use hand tools, and follow the replacement plug’s instructions about handling or compounds rather than adding something by habit. [2.3L gap](#/document/G1673181), [2.3L installation and torque](#/document/G1673189)

steps.title: 2.3L: inspect and refit the coils
steps.body: Inspect each coil assembly for cracks, rips or tears, and replace any damaged assembly. Install the coils and their mounting bolts. Tighten the bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). [2.3L coil inspection and installation](#/document/G1673188)

steps.title: 2.3L: restore the wiring and appearance cover
steps.body: Reconnect all four coil electrical connectors and secure their locking tabs. Reattach the wiring harness retainers. Install the engine appearance cover, then its retaining nuts and bolts; tighten those fasteners to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Continue at step 28. [2.3L reassembly](#/document/G1673188)

steps.title: 3.7L: remove the air cleaner outlet pipe
steps.body: The upper intake manifold must come off to reach the right-hand coils; this is established plug access, not optional extra disassembly. Start by disconnecting and positioning aside the brake booster tube and crankcase ventilation tube at the air cleaner outlet pipe. Loosen both pipe clamps and remove the pipe. [Right-hand coil access](#/document/G1675558), [Outlet pipe removal](#/document/G1675695)

steps.title: 3.7L: release the manifold vacuum hose
steps.body: Use the hose clamp remover/installer to disconnect the vacuum hose from the upper intake manifold. Detach the hose retainer at the throttle body, then the retainer at the upper intake manifold, and position the hose clear. [Manifold vacuum hose](#/document/G1681529)

steps.title: 3.7L: disconnect the purge valve connection
steps.body: Disconnect the EVAP purge valve electrical connector and detach the associated wiring harness retainers.
