Before separating its quick-release coupling, use compressed air to clean the retaining-clip area. Release the actual coupling’s hand-operated locks in their proper sequence, then separate it without prying. Fit clean blanking plugs to the open connection. Dirt can damage the connection, and distorted clips can cause leaks. [Purge valve access](#/document/G1681529), [Coupling handling](#/document/G1671536)

steps.title: 3.7L: free the remaining manifold connections
steps.body: Disconnect the PCV tube from the upper intake manifold and position it aside. PCV is the crankcase ventilation connection. Disconnect the throttle body and MAP sensor electrical connectors; MAP means manifold absolute pressure. Detach the wiring harness retainers, then remove the upper intake manifold support bolt. Keep its hardware separate from the manifold mounting bolts. [Remaining manifold connections](#/document/G1681529)

steps.title: 3.7L: lift off the manifold and discard its gaskets
steps.body: Remove the upper intake manifold mounting bolts and lift off the manifold. Remove and discard its gaskets. Clean and inspect the sealing surfaces on both the upper and lower intake manifold. Keep debris out of the exposed openings while working; the new gaskets need clean mating surfaces at reassembly. [Manifold removal and sealing surfaces](#/document/G1681529)

steps.title: 3.7L: remove the coils on both sides
steps.body: Use compressed air to clean the coils and surrounding areas before removal. Disconnect the coil electrical connectors, remove the mounting bolts, and remove the coils with a slight twisting motion to release their seals. Work through both sides so all six plugs are accessible. Keep each coil associated with its original position as an organizing aid. [3.7L coil removal](#/document/G1675558), [Six-plug quantity](#/document/G1675559)

steps.title: 3.7L: replace all six plugs
steps.body: Confirm the engine is warm to hand touch, neither hot nor cold soaked. Blow foreign material out of the plug wells before removing the plugs. Remove the six plugs using hand tools. Discard any plug that is dropped, because internal damage can cause misfire and engine damage. Check the replacements for a gap of 0.049–0.053 in (1.25–1.35 mm). Start each plug by hand without forcing its threads, then tighten to 133 lb.in (15 Nm). Follow the replacement plug’s handling instructions rather than assuming a compound is needed. [3.7L plug handling and torque](#/document/G1675559), [3.7L gap](#/document/G1675554)

steps.title: 3.7L: inspect the boots and install the coils
steps.body: Inspect the coils and replace any rubber boot with cracks, rips or tears. Reinstall the coils and their mounting bolts. Tighten each bolt in two stages: first 62 lb.in (7 Nm), then an additional 50°. The angle is a second tightening movement after reaching the torque value. Reconnect the coil electrical connectors before covering the right-hand side with the manifold. [3.7L coil installation](#/document/G1675558)

steps.title: 3.7L: install new gaskets and tighten the manifold in order
steps.body:
Install new upper intake manifold gaskets, then position the manifold and install its seven mounting bolts. Follow the numbered tightening order for both stages: first 89 lb.in (10 Nm), then an additional 45°.

With the manifold viewed as in Ford’s tightening illustration, throttle body at the left, the order is: 1, lower-edge bolt second from the right; 2, the central upper bolt between the runners; 3, lower-edge middle bolt; 4, lower-edge leftmost bolt; 5, lower-edge rightmost bolt; 6, upper bolt at the right-hand end; 7, left-side bolt beside the throttle-body end. Match those positions to the illustrated sequence before tightening. [Manifold installation and numbered order](#/document/G1681529)

steps.title: 3.7L: restore the support and electrical connections
steps.body: Install the upper intake manifold support bolt and tighten it to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). Reattach the wiring harness retainers, reconnect the throttle body and MAP sensor electrical connectors, and reconnect the PCV tube to the upper intake manifold. [Manifold support and connections](#/document/G1681529)

steps.title: 3.7L: reconnect the purge valve and secure its coupling
steps.body: Remove the temporary blanking plugs and inspect and clean both coupling ends. Push the EVAP purge coupling fully onto its tube and restore its own retaining clip or locking tabs. On the illustrated clip-retained styles, seat the retainer fully; the flush-fitting retainer must have its tabs locked. Pull on the connection to confirm it is retained. Reattach the wiring harness retainers and reconnect the EVAP purge valve electrical connector. [Purge valve reassembly](#/document/G1681529), [Coupling connection and retention](#/document/G1671536)

steps.title: 3.7L: restore the vacuum hose and outlet pipe
steps.body: Reconnect the manifold vacuum hose using the hose clamp remover/installer. Attach its retainer at the throttle body and its retainer at the upper intake manifold. Reinstall the air cleaner outlet pipe and tighten both clamps to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Reconnect the brake booster tube and crankcase ventilation tube that were positioned aside. Continue at step 28. [Vacuum hose reassembly](#/document/G1681529), [Outlet pipe installation](#/document/G1675695)

steps.title: 5.0L: remove the appearance cover and move the ventilation tubes
steps.body: Remove the engine appearance cover. Clean the retaining-clip areas of the PCV valve and crankcase ventilation tube quick-release couplings with compressed air. Using the release sequence for each actual fitting, disconnect both couplings by hand and position the tubes aside. Protect open connections with clean blanking plugs. Do not pry the clips: deformation can cause leaks. [5.0L access](#/document/G1675574), [5.0L coupling precautions and releases](#/document/G1671557)

steps.title: 5.0L: remove the coil covers and coils
steps.body: Remove the ignition coil covers and disconnect the coil electrical connectors. Use compressed air to clear foreign material from the coils and surrounding area. Remove the coil bolts, then give each coil a slight twist to break its seal and remove it. Keep the coils organized by original position as a practical aid. [5.0L coil removal](#/document/G1675574)

steps.title: 5.0L: replace all eight plugs
steps.body: Confirm the engine is warm to hand touch, neither hot nor cold soaked. Blow foreign material out of the wells before loosening the plugs, then remove all eight with hand tools. Discard any dropped plug; hidden damage can cause misfire and engine damage. Check replacement gaps against 0.049–0.053 in (1.25–1.35 mm). Start each replacement by hand without forcing it, then tighten to 133 lb.in (15 Nm). Follow the replacement plug’s handling instructions rather than adding a compound by habit. [5.0L plug handling and torque](#/document/G1675575), [5.0L gap](#/document/G1675570)

steps.title: 5.0L: inspect and reinstall the coils
steps.body: Inspect each coil assembly for cracks, rips or tears and replace any damaged assembly. Install the coils and their bolts. Tighten each bolt first to 62 lb.in (7 Nm), then turn it an additional 45°. Reconnect all coil electrical connectors. This angle differs from the 3.7L specification; keep the branches separate. [5.0L coil installation](#/document/G1675574)

steps.title: 5.0L: restore the coil covers and ventilation connections
steps.body: Install the coil covers. Remove the temporary blanking plugs, inspect and clean the mating coupling ends, and reconnect the PCV valve coupling and crankcase ventilation tube coupling. Fully restore each fitting’s own retaining clip or locking mechanism and pull-check the connection. For a fitting with a secondary lock, push it onto the tube, confirm retention, then lock the secondary tab. [5.0L reassembly](#/document/G1675574), [5.0L coupling connection](#/document/G1671557)

steps.title: 5.0L: reinstall the appearance cover
steps.body: Check whether the cover’s rubber grommets stayed in the cover during removal. If they did, remove them from the cover and install them on the intake manifold first. Then install the engine appearance cover. Continue at step 28. [5.0L appearance cover installation](#/document/G1675574)

steps.title: Reconnect the battery and close up
steps.body: After completing your engine branch, reconnect the negative battery cable and tighten its clamp nut to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Reinstall the battery cover and its retainers. Ford notes that battery disconnection can temporarily change driving behavior while the powertrain control module relearns its adaptive settings. That is not a reason to ignore a persistent misfire. [Battery connection and relearning](#/document/G1692356)

steps.title: Check the finished job and record it
steps.body:
Confirm that all coil connectors, harness retainers and covers disturbed in your engine branch are restored. On the 3.7L, also account for the manifold connections and outlet-pipe tubes; on the 5.0L, check both ventilation couplings and the appearance-cover grommets. [2.3L reassembly](#/document/G1673188), [3.7L coils](#/document/G1675558), [3.7L manifold connections](#/document/G1681529), [3.7L outlet pipe](#/document/G1675695), [5.0L reassembly](#/document/G1675574)

As a practical completion check, make a final visual pass for tools, temporary blanking plugs and any tube left aside before starting. Then start the engine and observe whether it runs normally. If a new rough-running condition appears, switch off and recheck the work before driving. Record the date, mileage, engine and plugs fitted, and retain useful observations from the removed parts. These checks do not replace diagnosis of a continuing misfire.

watchFor.title: Inch-pounds are not foot-pounds
watchFor.body: The plug specifications are 106 lb.in (12 Nm) for the 2.3L and 133 lb.in (15 Nm) for the 3.7L and 5.0L. Read the wrench’s units before tightening. [2.3L torque](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L torque](#/document/G1675559), [5.0L torque](#/document/G1675575)

watchFor.title: A dropped plug goes in the discard pile
watchFor.body: A plug can suffer internal damage without looking broken. Replace a dropped plug rather than installing a possible source of misfire and engine damage. [2.3L handling](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L handling](#/document/G1675559), [5.0L handling](#/document/G1675575)

watchFor.title: Keep the two cleaning stages separate
watchFor.body: Clean around the coils before lifting them out, then clean the plug wells while the plugs still close the holes. The second cleaning is easy to overlook when enthusiasm gets ahead of the air nozzle. [2.3L coils](#/document/G1673188), [2.3L plugs](#/document/G1673189), [3.7L coils](#/document/G1675558), [3.7L plugs](#/document/G1675559), [5.0L coils](#/document/G1675574), [5.0L plugs](#/document/G1675575)

watchFor.title: Do not reuse the 3.7L manifold gaskets
watchFor.body: The removed upper intake manifold gaskets are discard items. Have the replacements available before beginning this branch. [Manifold gasket replacement](#/document/G1681529)

watchFor.title: Preserve unusual evidence
watchFor.body: As a practical diagnostic aid, photograph unusual damage or contamination and label the removed plug by its original position. Do not assign a cause from appearance alone or automatically replace every coil because the plugs were due.

procedures.purpose: Replace the four 2.3L spark plugs with the specified handling and tightening.
Replace the six 3.7L spark plugs with the specified handling and tightening.
Replace the eight 5.0L spark plugs with the specified handling and tightening.
Access, inspect and reinstall the 2.3L coils and appearance cover.
Access, inspect and reinstall the 3.7L coils.
Access, inspect and reinstall the 5.0L coils, covers and ventilation tubes.
Remove and reinstall the 3.7L upper intake manifold for right-hand coil access.
Remove and reinstall the 3.7L outlet pipe during manifold access.
Handle and verify the 3.7L vapor coupling disturbed for manifold access.
Handle and verify the 5.0L ventilation couplings disturbed for coil access.
Disconnect and reconnect the negative battery cable.

stepGroups.title: Prepare and isolate power
stepGroups.summary: Make the engine safe to work around, establish the required temperature and disconnect the negative battery cable.

stepGroups.title: 2.3L EcoBoost
stepGroups.summary: Use this branch only for the 2.3L; finish at step 28.

stepGroups.title: 3.7L V6
stepGroups.summary: Remove and reinstall the upper intake manifold for right-hand coil access; finish at step 28.

stepGroups.title: 5.0L V8
stepGroups.summary: Restore the ventilation couplings, coil covers and appearance cover; finish at step 28.

stepGroups.title: Reconnect and check
stepGroups.summary: Restore battery power, inspect the completed work and check operation.

diagnostics.finding: A replacement plug has the wrong gap or does not match the engine-specific part.
diagnostics.meaning: It has not passed the basic fit-and-specification check for this job.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the part or gap mismatch before installation. Use 0.0295 in (0.75 mm) for the 2.3L, or 0.049–0.053 in (1.25–1.35 mm) for the 3.7L and 5.0L, following the replacement plug’s handling instructions. [2.3L gap](#/document/G1673181), [3.7L gap](#/document/G1675554), [5.0L gap](#/document/G1675570)

diagnostics.finding: A coil or boot has cracks, rips or tears.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford calls for replacement of the damaged component rather than routine reuse.
diagnostics.next: On the 3.7L, replace damaged rubber boots. On the 2.3L and 5.0L, replace damaged coil assemblies. [3.7L inspection](#/document/G1675558), [2.3L inspection](#/document/G1673188), [5.0L inspection](#/document/G1675574)

diagnostics.finding: A plug will not start smoothly by hand.
diagnostics.meaning: Its alignment or the condition of the threads needs attention; more force will not establish correct engagement.
diagnostics.next: Stop installation and inspect before proceeding. Do not use the final tightening torque to pull a reluctant plug into place. This is a handling check, not a thread-repair procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A coupling pulls free after reconnection.
diagnostics.meaning: Its retaining mechanism has not secured the connection.
diagnostics.next: Inspect and clean the ends, reconnect using that fitting’s own locking sequence, fully seat its retainer and repeat the pull check. Do not proceed with an unsecured connection. [3.7L coupling retention](#/document/G1671536), [5.0L coupling retention](#/document/G1671557)

diagnostics.finding: The engine runs roughly after the work, or the original misfire remains.
diagnostics.meaning: The completion check has failed, or plug replacement has not resolved the original concern.
diagnostics.next: Switch off and recheck the connectors, coils and access components disturbed in the relevant branch. If the concern remains, continue diagnosis rather than repeatedly buying ignition parts. Battery relearning can temporarily affect driving behavior, but it does not establish the cause of a persistent misfire. [Battery relearning note](#/document/G1692356)

verification.title: Confirm the engine-specific tightening
verification.body: Check your recorded values: 2.3L plugs 106 lb.in (12 Nm), coil bolts 89 lb.in (10 Nm), appearance-cover fasteners 80 lb.in (9 Nm). 3.7L plugs 133 lb.in (15 Nm), coil bolts 62 lb.in (7 Nm) plus 50°. 5.0L plugs 133 lb.in (15 Nm), coil bolts 62 lb.in (7 Nm) plus 45°. [2.3L plugs](#/document/G1673189), [2.3L coils and cover](#/document/G1673188), [3.7L plugs](#/document/G1675559), [3.7L coils](#/document/G1675558), [5.0L plugs](#/document/G1675575), [5.0L coils](#/document/G1675574)

verification.title: Account for the 3.7L intake work
verification.body: Confirm new gaskets were installed, the seven manifold bolts received 89 lb.in (10 Nm) plus 45° in the numbered order, the support bolt received 89 lb.in (10 Nm), and both outlet-pipe clamps received 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Check the throttle body, MAP sensor, purge valve, PCV tube, vacuum hose, brake booster tube and all disturbed retainers. [Manifold reassembly](#/document/G1681529), [Outlet pipe reassembly](#/document/G1675695)

verification.title: Check retained connections and covers
verification.body: All coil connectors must be connected, the opened couplings retained, and the relevant covers restored. On the 5.0L, confirm the appearance-cover grommets were placed on the intake manifold before the cover was installed. [2.3L reassembly](#/document/G1673188), [3.7L reassembly](#/document/G1675558), [3.7L couplings](#/document/G1671536), [5.0L reassembly](#/document/G1675574), [5.0L couplings](#/document/G1671557)

verification.title: Confirm power and operation
verification.body: The negative battery clamp must be secured at 44 lb.in (5 Nm), with the battery cover retained. Complete the visual check before starting, confirm normal running, and record the service mileage. Persistent rough running needs follow-up rather than a completed-job tick. [Battery connection](#/document/G1692356)

notes: The belt interval does not automatically require new pulleys or tensioners. Use the belt routing for the selected engine.
guides.title: Accessory belts: inspect the belt and the system driving it
guides.summary: Follow the belt inspection and replacement cadence, while keeping pulley and tensioner diagnosis separate.
guides.introduction: An accessory belt transfers crankshaft rotation to its driven accessories. Its routing, the way tension is controlled and any separate A/C belt depend on the engine. Knowing that layout helps you distinguish belt wear from a pulley, tensioner or installation problem.
guides.why: A belt may deteriorate with age or contamination, but noise alone does not identify the failed part. Replacing a tensioner on a mileage schedule intended for the belt can add work without addressing the cause.

when.summary: Inspect at 100,000 mi (160,000 km), then every other oil change until replacement. Replace the belts at 150,000 mi (240,000 km).
notes: Inspect sooner if there is damage, contamination or a new noise.

prepare.title: Identify the belt arrangement
prepare.detail: Use the correct engine diagram, including a separate A/C belt where fitted.

prepare.title: Plan for safe access
prepare.detail: Inspect with the engine off. Read the removal and installation method before releasing tension or removing a belt.

steps.title: Review belt condition and routing
steps.body: Check for contamination, incorrect seating and visible deterioration using the relevant accessory-drive diagnosis.

steps.title: Investigate the cause of abnormal wear
steps.body: A damaged or misaligned pulley can affect a replacement belt too. Check the system when the evidence calls for it.

steps.title: Replace and verify by engine
steps.body: Follow the correct installation sequence and routing, then complete its operation checks.

watchFor.title: A proposed lubricant or belt dressing
watchFor.body: Do not lubricate the accessory belt.

watchFor.title: Cracks versus actual damage
watchFor.body: The 2.3L diagnostic guidance distinguishes small cracks from exposed cord or missing chunks; apply the relevant engine’s inspection criteria.

notes: The normal-use schedule calls for changing both automatic transmission fluid and filter. A drain-only operation, which does not require filter removal, is a different scope. [Ford schedule](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) · [Drain-only distinction](#/document/G1692052)

For a later level-only inspection, use the level-check procedure and correct the measured level as needed. Do not repeat the post-drain initial fill or air-purge routine simply because you opened the fill plug. [Level check](#/document/G1692053) · [Refill scope](#/document/G1692052)
guides.title: 6R80 automatic transmission fluid and filter service
guides.summary: Remove the pan, replace the filter, inspect the magnets, then refill, purge the cooling circuit and set the level at the specified fluid temperature.
guides.introduction: I treat this as one connected job: pan, filter, refill and a properly measured finish. The little level indicator gets the last word—not the number of empty bottles beside the car. This guide covers the 6R80 automatic in the original 2015 Mustang scope: 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. The service requires pan removal and a temperature-controlled refill. [Pan and filter service](#/document/G1692033) · [Drain and refill](#/document/G1692052)
guides.why: The refill procedure circulates fluid through the torque converter and cooling system to clear trapped air. The specified fluid, correct temperature and final level all matter: unsuitable fluid or driving with a low level can cause transmission failure. A guessed capacity is a lousy substitute for the actual reading. [Refill requirements](#/document/G1692052)

when.summary: Change automatic-transmission fluid and filter every 150,000 mi (240,000 km) in normal use.
notes: A leak, contamination concern or diagnosed fault can require service earlier.

prepare.title: Confirm the transmission and plan the whole job
prepare.detail: Verify that the car has the 6R80 automatic. Have the equipment for the hot final check ready before draining anything; this service includes a warm-up drive followed by another hoist access. [Pan service](#/document/G1692033) · [Refill sequence](#/document/G1692052)

prepare.title: Get the specified fluid and matching parts
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft MERCON LV automatic transmission fluid, XT-10-QLVC, specification WSS-M2C938-A. Have the correct vehicle-specific replacement filter and a pan gasket available. For this scheduled fluid-and-filter job, fit a new filter; the repair procedure separately permits filter reuse when excessive contamination is absent. An undamaged pan gasket may be reused. [Fluid, filter and gasket](#/document/G1692033)

prepare.title: Gather dispensing, measuring and hand tools
prepare.detail: Have a universal fluid dispenser, a fluid suction gun for correcting overfill, and a diagnostic scan tool that displays transmission fluid temperature. Ford recommends a pressurized dispenser with 8–12 qt capacity, such as the Mityvac MITMV6412; that is equipment capacity, not the prescribed service fill. Also gather a drain container, clean wiping materials, tools matching the actual fasteners, and torque wrenches capable of 80 lb.in (9 Nm) and 26 lb.ft (35 Nm). [Refill equipment](#/document/G1692052) · [Pan torque](#/document/G1692033)

prepare.title: Arrange suitable lifting access
prepare.detail: The procedure uses a hoist. Confirm its capacity covers the car and any cargo or modifications. Locate the triangle-marked lifting points and position the lift adapters without contacting vulnerable suspension, exhaust, steering or underbody parts. The emergency tire jack is unsuitable for this job; never work beneath a car supported only by a jack. [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) · [Hoist safety](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Prevent unintended starts and protect yourself
prepare.detail: If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around or beneath the car. Keep the key under your control during engine-off work; start the engine deliberately only when the refill instructions require it. Wear eye and ear protection, use protective gloves around sharp edges, and consult the fluid's safety information before handling it. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Raise the car for pan access
steps.body: With the engine off and the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the car on the hoist. Use the triangle-marked lifting locations and check lift-arm clearance before raising it. The supported access route goes directly to the transmission fill assembly and pan. [Pan removal setup](#/document/G1692033) · [Lifting locations](#/document/G1663631)

steps.title: Remove the fill plug and short level indicator
steps.body: Locate the fill-plug assembly on the transmission case just above the pan flange, as shown in the procedure. Remove the assembly and separate the short level indicator from the plug for checking later. Keep both clean and protected from dirt. This is the indicator used for the refill—not an underhood dipstick. [Fill assembly](#/document/G1692033) · [Separate the indicator](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Remove the pan and collect the fluid
steps.body: Place the drain container beneath the pan before releasing it. Support the pan as you remove its bolts, then lower it while allowing the fluid to drain into the container. The illustration identifies 21 pan bolts. Pan removal is the specified draining method; removing the filter is a separate part of the combined service. [Pan removal](#/document/G1692033) · [Draining method](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Remove the gasket and filter
steps.body: Lift the pan gasket away and inspect it for damage. Remove the transmission fluid filter from beneath the transmission, keeping the drain container in place. Set the old filter aside for inspection before discarding it. Although the repair procedure allows an uncontaminated filter to be reused, this guide's scheduled service includes changing it. [Gasket and filter removal](#/document/G1692033) · [Ford maintenance schedule](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1649139&Uid=G1634876&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Clean and inspect the pan and magnets
steps.body: Before moving the magnets, note their locations. Clean and inspect the pan and its magnet or magnets. For the late-build arrangement illustrated in the procedure, keep track of both magnets, labeled 1 and 2, so they return to their corresponding locations. Assess contamination before wiping away the evidence. The procedure supplies no numerical contamination limit. Conspicuous debris warrants diagnosis; fresh fluid does not establish that the cause has been repaired. [Pan and magnet inspection](#/document/G1692033)

steps.title: Check the filter socket for a retained seal
steps.body: Inspect the transmission pump bore—the opening that receives the filter's sealed neck. The old filter seal may remain inside after the filter comes out. If it has, carefully remove it without scratching the bore. Confirm the old seal is out before fitting the replacement filter. [Filter seal inspection](#/document/G1692033)

steps.title: Lubricate the seal and install the new filter
steps.body: Match the replacement filter to the vehicle and removed component. Make sure its seal is on the filter, lubricate that seal with the specified MERCON LV fluid, and install the filter in its proper position. The seal belongs on the filter during installation; leaving the old one in the pump bore is not part of the plan. [Filter installation](#/document/G1692033)

steps.title: Return the magnets and fit the gasket
steps.body: Place the magnet or magnets back in their original pan locations; the late-build illustration shows the two corresponding positions. Refit the pan gasket if it is undamaged, or install the correct replacement gasket if needed. Check that it follows the pan flange and its bolt holes before offering the pan up to the transmission. [Magnets and gasket installation](#/document/G1692033)

steps.title: Install and torque the pan
steps.body: Position the pan against the transmission and install its bolts. Tighten them in a crisscross pattern to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Move between opposing areas around the pan rather than tightening consecutively around the perimeter. Check the torque wrench's units: this specification is inch-pounds. [Pan installation and torque](#/document/G1692033)

steps.title: Add the initial engine-start fill
steps.body: With the engine still off, use the fluid dispenser through the fill opening to add 3.3 L (3.5 qt) of the specified MERCON LV fluid. That is the initial quantity after pan or filter removal, allowing the engine to be started; it is not the finished service level. Additional fluid is determined by the following readings. [Initial service fill](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Establish the cold level before driving
steps.body: Connect the scan tool and monitor transmission fluid temperature. Start the engine, select PARK and let it idle at 600–750 rpm. Use the short level indicator in the fill opening to check the fluid. Add fluid until the reading reaches the indicated area below the crosshatch, shown in the refill procedure's cold-fill illustration. Do not begin the warm-up drive before reaching this level: driving low can damage the transmission. [Cold running check](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Close the fill opening before the warm-up drive
steps.body: Return the level indicator to the fill-plug assembly, install the assembly and tighten the fill plug to 26 lb.ft (35 Nm). Lower the car using the hoist's operating procedure before driving. [Fill plug installation](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Drive to purge the cooling circuit
steps.body: Drive safely for the conditions and obey traffic laws while monitoring transmission fluid temperature with the scan tool. Reach 96.7–102°C (206–215°F). This drive circulates fluid through the torque converter and transmission cooling system to eliminate trapped air. It is a required part of this refill after pan service; it is not an instruction to repeat the initial fill during an ordinary level-only check. [Refill air purge](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Return to the hoist and cycle the selector
steps.body: With the engine idling at 600–750 rpm in PARK, confirm the fluid is within 96.7–102°C (206–215°F), then raise the car on the hoist. For the final level check, with the engine running, move the selector through every gear position, holding each for approximately 5 seconds, then return it to PARK. All drive wheels must be elevated before selecting a drive position on the hoist; otherwise the car can move unexpectedly. [Hot refill setup](#/document/G1692052) · [Selector sequence](#/document/G1692053) · [Hoist running safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Read the hot level in the dotted area
steps.body: Remove the fill plug and separate the indicator from it. With the engine idling in PARK, check the level using the indicator and verify the fluid temperature remains within 96.7–102°C (206–215°F). The final target is the upper level of the dotted area marked B, not the crosshatched area A. If the fluid is hotter than the specified window, allow it to cool into range before judging the reading. [Hot level target](#/document/G1692053) · [Idle speed](#/document/G1692052)

steps.title: Correct the level and close the assembly
steps.body: If the hot reading is below the upper level of dotted area B, add the specified fluid with the dispenser. If it is above that level, withdraw fluid with the suction gun. Recheck the reading and scan-tool temperature until both meet the specification. Return the indicator to the plug assembly, install it and tighten the fill plug to 26 lb.ft (35 Nm). [Level correction and closure](#/document/G1692052) · [Final level check](#/document/G1692053)

steps.title: Inspect the serviced areas and finish
steps.body: As a completion check, look for fresh leakage around the pan flange and fill plug before lowering the car. Confirm that the pan received its crisscross tightening and that the fill assembly is installed. Record the fluid specification, filter replacement, gasket decision, final temperature and level. If slipping, slow shifts or leakage remains, check the level and diagnose the cause; the service alone does not establish that a fault has been repaired. [Pan closure](#/document/G1692033) · [Fluid-related symptoms](#/document/G1692052)

watchFor.title: The initial fill is only the beginning
watchFor.body: The 3.3 L (3.5 qt) quantity follows pan or filter removal. The separate 11.35 L (12 qt) initial quantity in the source applies to an overhauled transmission, not this service. Finish by measured level. [Refill quantities](#/document/G1692052)

watchFor.title: Cold and hot readings use different targets
watchFor.body: Before driving, use the illustrated area below the crosshatch. At 96.7–102°C (206–215°F), use the upper level of dotted area B. Mixing those instructions makes the little indicator a pain in the ass for entirely avoidable reasons. [Cold and hot targets](#/document/G1692052)

watchFor.title: Low level means no driving
watchFor.body: Do not use a road test to see whether a low transmission will sort itself out. Establish the required level first; driving low can cause internal failure. [Low-fluid warning](#/document/G1692053)

watchFor.title: A seal left behind
watchFor.body: Inspect the pump bore after removing the filter. Remove any retained old seal carefully, without scoring the bore, before installing the lubricated filter seal. [Seal handling](#/document/G1692033)

watchFor.title: Fluid specification matters
watchFor.body: Use MERCON LV meeting WSS-M2C938-A. Other fluid can cause abnormal operation or transmission failure. Keep this job to the specified pan, filter and refill service rather than substituting a generic flush or additive routine. [Specified fluid](#/document/G1692052)

procedures.purpose: Remove, inspect and reinstall the transmission pan, gasket, filter and magnets.
Perform the initial refill, cold running check, cooling-system air purge and level correction.
Cycle the selector and verify the temperature-controlled final fluid level.
Identify lifting points and avoid unsafe vehicle support or underbody damage.
Apply relevant remote-start, personal-protection and hoist-running precautions.

stepGroups.title: Access and drain
stepGroups.summary: Raise the car, open the fill assembly and remove the pan and filter.

stepGroups.title: Inspect and reassemble
stepGroups.summary: Check contamination and the filter seal, then reinstall the filter, magnets, gasket and pan.

stepGroups.title: Establish the initial level
stepGroups.summary: Add the engine-start quantity and establish the running cold level before driving.

stepGroups.title: Purge and set the hot level
stepGroups.summary: Warm the cooling circuit, cycle the selector and adjust to the dotted B target.

stepGroups.title: Check the finished service
stepGroups.summary: Inspect for leakage and record the result.

diagnostics.finding: Excessive contamination in the removed filter, pan or magnets
diagnostics.meaning: The repair procedure's condition for filter reuse is not met. It provides no numerical debris threshold or diagnosis from appearance alone. [Inspection criteria](#/document/G1692033)
diagnostics.next: Fit the new filter for this service, retain useful observations of the debris and arrange diagnosis of the contamination rather than assuming the fluid change resolves its cause.

diagnostics.finding: The old filter comes out without its seal
diagnostics.meaning: The seal may still be in the pump bore. [Retained seal check](#/document/G1692033)
diagnostics.next: Inspect the bore and carefully remove the retained seal without scratching it. Confirm the replacement filter carries its lubricated seal before installation.

diagnostics.finding: The final hot reading is below dotted area B's upper level
diagnostics.meaning: The level is low if measured at 96.7–102°C (206–215°F) under the specified running conditions. [Hot reading](#/document/G1692052)
diagnostics.next: Add the specified fluid with the dispenser and recheck temperature and level. Do not drive with a low level.

diagnostics.finding: The final hot reading is above dotted area B's upper level
diagnostics.meaning: The transmission is overfilled under the specified checking conditions. [Overfill correction](#/document/G1692052)
diagnostics.next: Remove fluid with the suction gun, then repeat the temperature and level check.

diagnostics.finding: The temperature is outside the checking window
diagnostics.meaning: The reading does not establish the specified final level. Extended high-speed driving, traffic, hot weather or towing may leave the fluid too hot. [Temperature requirements](#/document/G1692053)
diagnostics.next: Bring the fluid into 96.7–102°C (206–215°F), allowing cooling when needed, and repeat the running level check.

diagnostics.finding: Slipping, slow shifts or leakage continues
diagnostics.meaning: These symptoms call for a fluid-level check; a fluid and filter change does not identify their underlying cause. [Symptom guidance](#/document/G1692052)
diagnostics.next: Verify the level correctly, inspect any leakage and obtain further diagnosis if symptoms remain.

verification.title: Pan and filter assembly is complete
verification.body: Confirm the filter seal was checked and lubricated, the filter installed, magnets returned, gasket assessed and pan bolts tightened crisscross to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). [Assembly requirements](#/document/G1692033)

verification.title: The refill and air purge were completed
verification.body: Confirm the cold running level was established before driving and the warm-up drive reached 96.7–102°C (206–215°F). [Refill sequence](#/document/G1692052)

verification.title: Final level was measured under the right conditions
verification.body: After holding each selector position for approximately 5 seconds, return to PARK. Confirm the final reading reaches the upper level of dotted area B at 96.7–102°C (206–215°F), with the engine idling at 600–750 rpm. [Selector and target](#/document/G1692053) · [Idle requirement](#/document/G1692052)

verification.title: The transmission is closed and checked
verification.body: Confirm the indicator is back in the fill assembly and the plug is tightened to 26 lb.ft (35 Nm). Inspect the pan and plug for fresh leakage and address any continuing symptoms before considering the work complete. [Fill plug torque](#/document/G1692052)

notes: Keep the existing maintenance schedule separate from this procedure. Do not transfer these MT82 fluid instructions or its schedule to the 3160 or an automatic transmission.
guides.title: MT82 manual transmission fluid: drain, refill and set the level
guides.summary: Change the fluid in a 2015 Mustang’s MT82 manual gearbox using the correct lubricant, a level vehicle and the specified fluid depth.
guides.introduction: I start this job by reading the fluid specification, because “transmission fluid” is a category, not a shopping instruction. The MT82 calls for Motorcraft Dual Clutch Transmission Fluid XT-11-QDC, specification WSS-M2C200-D2. Yes, the bottle says dual clutch and your Mustang has a clutch pedal. The specification gets the final damn word. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)
guides.why: This service renews the lubricant used by the manual gearbox. Getting the product and final level right matters more than simply pouring in a stated quantity: Ford supplies both a capacity and a separate level-check illustration. Fresh fluid also does not establish that an existing shifting problem has been repaired. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313) [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

when.summary: Every 150,000 mi (240,000 km) in normal use.
notes: Predominantly towing/car-top-carrier use: 60,000 mi (96,000 km).
Predominantly dusty or sandy driving: 50,000 mi (80,000 km).

prepare.title: Confirm the application
prepare.detail: This guide covers the MT82 in the original 2015 Mustang scope: 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. Confirm that the installed gearbox is an MT82 before choosing fluid or starting work. These instructions do not cover the 3160 or an automatic transmission. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)

prepare.title: Get the correct fluid
prepare.detail: Have Motorcraft Dual Clutch Transmission Fluid XT-11-QDC, meeting WSS-M2C200-D2, available for the listed 2.7 qt (2.6 L) capacity. XL-18 additive is required only after synchronizer replacement; it is not part of this routine fluid change. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)

prepare.title: Gather filling, draining and measuring equipment
prepare.detail: Ford specifies a fluid suction gun—a hand-operated tool for transferring fluid into or out of the gearbox. Also gather a drain container, tools that fit the actual plugs, a torque wrench capable of 26 lb-ft (35 Nm), clean wiping materials and a clean measuring aid for checking fluid depth below the fill opening. Match the tools to the actual fasteners rather than guessing a drive size. [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327) [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

prepare.title: Arrange level underbody access
prepare.detail: Use lifting and support equipment rated for the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications. The car must remain level for filling and checking. Ford identifies lifting locations with triangle stamps in the body or frame; the supplied lifting illustration shows the four locations along the sides. The emergency tire jack is not suitable for this service. [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) [Service safety](#/document/G1693189) [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327)

prepare.title: Protect yourself
prepare.detail: Have eye and ear protection available, use protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts, and read the fluid’s safety information before handling it. Improper chemical handling and sharp components can cause injury. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. If remote start is equipped, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working underneath. An unexpected start during service can cause serious injury or death. Put on the required protection before beginning. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Raise and support the Mustang level
steps.body:
Work on a hard, level surface. Set the parking brake and block any wheels that remain on the ground. Locate the triangle-marked lifting points before raising the car. If using a jack, support the vehicle on stands before going underneath; a jack alone can lower unexpectedly and crush someone beneath it. Do not lift against either bumper. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189) [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631)

If using a hoist, use equipment of adequate capacity and position its arms at the specified lifting locations. Check that adapters and arms do not bear against or interfere with the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, mounting brackets, axle or rear cover. For a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving aboard. Keep the vehicle level for the fluid service. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189) [Lifting points](#/document/G1663631) [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327)

steps.title: Identify both service plugs
steps.body: Locate the drain plug on the underside of the transmission and the separate fill plug on the side of the housing. The close-up of the fill opening shows the cast-in FILL marking. Confirm that you can reach both plugs with the appropriate tools before draining. The documented service accesses these plugs directly; it does not call for wheel removal or transmission disassembly. [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327) [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

steps.title: Drain the old fluid
steps.body: Position the drain container beneath the drain plug, remove the plug and let the transmission fluid drain into the container. Keep the removed plug where it will stay clean and remain identifiable. [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327)

steps.title: Close the drain and open the fill port
steps.body: Reinstall the drain plug after draining and tighten it to 26 lb-ft (35 Nm). Then remove the separate fill plug to open the filling port. [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327)

steps.title: Pump in the specified lubricant
steps.body: Use the fluid suction gun to add XT-11-QDC fluid meeting WSS-M2C200-D2 through the fill opening. Ford lists capacity as 2.7 qt (2.6 L); use that figure to plan the supply, then establish the final amount by checking the level. Do not add XL-18 for an ordinary drain and refill—it is specified only after synchronizer replacement. [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327) [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)

steps.title: Set the fluid surface below the opening
steps.body:
Keep the vehicle level. Check the vertical distance from the lower edge of the fill opening to the fluid surface. Ford’s level illustration specifies 10 ± 3 mm below that edge, giving an acceptable distance of 7–13 mm. The target is below the opening, so fluid spilling from the hole is not the prescribed finished level. [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

If the surface is more than 13 mm below the edge, add fluid with the suction gun. If it is less than 7 mm below the edge, withdraw fluid. Remove the gun from the opening and check again after each adjustment until the surface is within the specified range. [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

steps.title: Install the fill plug
steps.body: Once the level is correct, reinstall the fill plug and tighten it to 26 lb-ft (35 Nm). Confirm that both the drain and fill plugs have been installed and tightened before moving on. [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327) [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

steps.title: Check the closures for leakage
steps.body: As a practical completion check, wipe away spilled fluid around both plugs, then look for fresh wetness. Cleaning first helps distinguish a spill from fluid continuing to escape. If fresh fluid appears, resolve the leak and repeat the level check before calling the service finished. The level check still requires a level vehicle and the same fill-plug torque afterward. [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

steps.title: Clear the work area and finish
steps.body:
Remove the drain container, suction gun and loose tools from beneath the vehicle. Return the car to the ground using the lifting equipment’s operating instructions, keeping everyone clear while the supports are changed. Keep the vehicle secured against movement during this process. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

Record the date, mileage and lubricant used. Record any remaining leak or shifting complaint so it receives diagnosis.

watchFor.title: The product name can mislead
watchFor.body: Motorcraft Dual Clutch Transmission Fluid XT-11-QDC, specification WSS-M2C200-D2, is the listed MT82 lubricant. Shop by that requirement rather than a generic manual-transmission, automatic-transmission or axle-oil label. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)

watchFor.title: Capacity does not replace the level check
watchFor.body: The listed 2.7 qt (2.6 L) capacity and the illustrated 10 ± 3 mm fluid depth serve different purposes. Finish by measuring the level with the vehicle level, rather than stopping solely because a measured quantity has gone in. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313) [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

watchFor.title: A top-up is not a leak repair
watchFor.body: Recurring wetness or a level that repeatedly drops needs investigation. Repeatedly adding fluid can conceal the unresolved problem.

procedures.purpose: Identify the drain plug and perform the MT82 drain, refill and plug-tightening operations.
Identify the fill opening and establish the illustrated fluid depth.
Select the lubricant, plan fluid quantity and distinguish routine service from the additive requirement after synchronizer replacement.
Identify lifting locations and protect the vehicle during underbody access.
Prevent unexpected starting and establish safe lifting, support and personal protection.

stepGroups.title: Prepare and reach the plugs
stepGroups.summary: Prevent starting, support the car level and identify the two service plugs.

stepGroups.title: Drain the gearbox
stepGroups.summary: Collect the old fluid and reinstall the drain plug before filling.

stepGroups.title: Refill and establish the level
stepGroups.summary: Use the specified fluid, adjust its depth and tighten the fill plug.

stepGroups.title: Check and finish
stepGroups.summary: Inspect for leakage, clear the equipment and record the service.

diagnostics.finding: The fluid surface is more than 13 mm below the lower edge of the fill opening.
diagnostics.meaning: The level is below the illustrated acceptable range, provided the vehicle is level.
diagnostics.next: Add the specified fluid with the suction gun, remeasure and stop within 7–13 mm below the opening. [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328) [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)

diagnostics.finding: The fluid surface is less than 7 mm below the lower edge of the fill opening.
diagnostics.meaning: The level is above the illustrated acceptable range, provided the vehicle is level.
diagnostics.next: Withdraw fluid with the suction gun and remeasure. Reinstall the fill plug at 26 lb-ft (35 Nm) once the level is correct. [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

diagnostics.finding: Fresh wetness returns after the plug areas have been wiped clean.
diagnostics.meaning: Residual spillage alone no longer explains the observation; a leak needs investigation.
diagnostics.next: Locate and resolve the source, then repeat the level check before returning the car to use. [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

diagnostics.finding: A shifting complaint remains after the service.
diagnostics.meaning: The fluid change has not established the cause or repaired the complaint.
diagnostics.next: Arrange diagnosis of the shifting problem. Do not treat extra fluid or routine XL-18 dosing as the next repair; XL-18 is specified only after synchronizer replacement. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313)

verification.title: Correct lubricant and measured level
verification.body: Confirm XT-11-QDC / WSS-M2C200-D2 was used and the fluid surface was checked at 10 ± 3 mm below the fill opening’s lower edge while the vehicle was level. [MT82 specifications](#/document/G1687313) [Fluid level check](#/document/G1687328)

verification.title: Both plugs secured
verification.body: Confirm the drain plug and fill plug were each tightened to 26 lb-ft (35 Nm). [Drain and fill](#/document/G1687327)

verification.title: No fresh leakage and equipment cleared
verification.body: Check the wiped plug areas for fresh fluid, account for the tools and fluid-transfer equipment, and record any unresolved observation with the service details.

notes: Confirm the vehicle-specific instruction before booking routine axle-fluid replacement. Suspected leakage or submersion needs attention regardless of the odometer.
guides.title: Rear axle fluid: confirm the schedule and the differential type
guides.summary: Understand Ford’s 150,000-mile normal-schedule entry and the separately stated axle exception before choosing a service deadline.
guides.introduction: Rear axle lubricant protects the gears and bearings inside the differential. Choosing the right service requires two pieces of information: the fitted differential and the maintenance instruction that applies to the car’s use. The drain/fill procedure also has branches for different equipment, including whether a drain plug or cooler is fitted.
guides.why: A gear-oil choice, friction-modifier instruction or filling method from another axle can be wrong for this one. Confirming the assembly first avoids turning a routine fluid job into an experiment.

when.summary: The normal schedule lists rear axle fluid replacement at 150,000 mi (240,000 km); read the axle exception before treating that as an unconditional deadline.
notes: Ford’s special-conditions page separately says axle fluid checks or changes are not required unless leakage is suspected or the assembly has been submerged. These online instructions need to be reconciled for the vehicle’s applicable schedule.
Suspected leakage or submersion needs prompt assessment regardless of mileage.

prepare.title: Identify the axle and equipment
prepare.detail: Confirm the differential type and whether a cooler is fitted.

prepare.title: Confirm the applicable service plan
prepare.detail: Review the normal entry together with the exception and the vehicle’s original maintenance information; obtain a vehicle-specific recommendation if they differ.

steps.title: Resolve the service scope
steps.body: Decide whether this is routine replacement, a leak repair or contamination after water exposure.

steps.title: Use the correct equipment branch
steps.body: Follow the draining/filling procedure for the actual axle, with its specified lubricant and any applicable additive.

steps.title: Finish with the correct level
steps.body: Complete the specified fill, closure and leak checks, and record what fluid and service were used.

watchFor.title: Water exposure or leaking seals
watchFor.body: Do not delay assessment because a mileage milestone is far away.

watchFor.title: Additive used by habit
watchFor.body: A limited-slip label alone is not a substitute for the exact application instructions.

procedures.purpose: Use the axle-equipment branches for draining and filling.
Check differential fluid level.
Confirm the axle lubricant specifications.

notes: Do not bridge the battery terminals with tools. A replacement decision should follow the condition assessment.
guides.title: Battery connections: check the path before replacing the battery
guides.summary: Inspect connections and assess battery condition when starting performance changes.
guides.introduction: Starting demands a strong electrical path as well as a charged battery. Corrosion, a poor connection or a cable problem can interfere with that path. A regular connection check is useful maintenance; replacing the battery on a guessed calendar interval is a different decision.
guides.why: A weak-start symptom can involve the battery, charging system, cables or an electrical drain. Looking at connections first gives diagnosis better evidence.

when.summary: Check battery connections every six months and clean as needed. Battery performance is part of the recommended multi-point inspection.

prepare.title: Review battery precautions
prepare.detail: Keep sparks and ignition sources away and use the appropriate personal protection.

prepare.title: Read the disconnect procedure before cleaning work
prepare.detail: A task that requires disconnection needs the correct sequence and any post-connection considerations.

steps.title: Inspect the connections
steps.body: Look for an obvious connection problem or corrosion and assess what work is actually needed.

steps.title: Clean or correct safely
steps.body: Use the specified battery procedure rather than disturbing terminals with the electrical system in an inappropriate state.

steps.title: Verify starting and charging as needed
steps.body: If the concern remains, test the battery and related system instead of assuming that cleaning proves the battery is healthy.

watchFor.title: A repeat low-charge condition
watchFor.body: Include charging performance and possible drains in diagnosis.

watchFor.title: Changes after disconnection
watchFor.body: The vehicle may need to relearn adaptive behavior; follow the reconnection guidance rather than immediately replacing unrelated parts.

procedures.purpose: Service the battery and its mounting.
Disconnect and reconnect correctly.
Use the battery-charging procedure.
Investigate an abnormal electrical drain.

notes: Applicability remains 2015 Mustang with 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engines. No engine-specific disassembly is needed for this operating inspection.
This article teaches inspection and initial fault sorting. Bulb, assembly, switch and module repairs remain separate procedures.
guides.title: Lighting checks: see, be seen, and catch the dead lamp
guides.summary: Check interior and exterior lights, record exactly what fails, and choose the right diagnostic path before buying parts.
guides.introduction: I work through lighting one function at a time. A Mustang looking damn good under a streetlight does not prove its brake lamps work. This check covers 2015 cars with the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines; check the equipment actually fitted to yours.
guides.why: Headlamps help you see, signaling lamps tell others what you intend to do, and cabin lights make the interior usable. A dark headlamp can involve its bulb, wiring, ballast—the HID lamp’s operating electronics—or body control module. I want a useful fault description before the parts cannon starts firing. [Headlamp diagnosis](#/document/G1694228)

when.summary: Check interior and exterior light operation monthly; include hazard-warning and horn operation in the recommended service inspection.

prepare.title: A safe place and a helper
prepare.detail: Choose a level parking spot away from traffic, secure the car against movement, and arrange a helper to operate controls while you observe. For brake and reversing lamps, keep a driver at the controls and the observer outside the vehicle’s path.

prepare.title: Prevent an unexpected start
prepare.detail: Before walking around the car, disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup in the central display. An unexpected remote start can injure someone working around the vehicle. [Inspection safety](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Simple checking supplies
prepare.detail: Bring a phone or notepad for a lamp checklist and fault notes. The operating check needs no dismantling or electrical test equipment. Use the car’s marked controls; include optional lamps only where fitted.

steps.title: Set up the check
steps.body: Keep the engine off for the walkaround. Set the parking brake and disable remote start before beginning. Have the helper tell you before changing a control or selecting a gear; nobody should be surprised by vehicle movement. Ford requires remote start to be disabled for inspections around the vehicle. [Inspection safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Look before switching anything on
steps.body: Walk around the car and note damaged lamp housings or lenses. Look at the headlamp switch and steering-column lighting stalk for visible damage without removing trim. Record any recent lighting or body repair that might help explain a fault. Ford’s preliminary checks specifically include damage and previous repairs. [Headlamp pre-checks](#/document/G1694228) · [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185)

steps.title: Check the position and rear lighting
steps.body: Select the parking-lamp function using the marked control. Walk around and check the corresponding front position lamps, rear tail lamps, side markers and license-plate lighting where fitted. Record each location as working, faulty or not checked. This is a practical walkaround checklist for Ford’s requirement to check all exterior lights. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Select low beams directly
steps.body: Turn the ignition on and select HEADLAMPS ON rather than relying on an automatic-light setting. Observe both low beams and record whether the left, right or both fail. This is Ford’s starting operating check for an inoperative low beam. Also check any other fitted exterior lighting through its normal control; record the selected mode if operation is uncertain. [Low-beam operating check](#/document/G1694228)

steps.title: Separate high beams from flash-to-pass
steps.body: With the ignition on and HEADLAMPS selected, move the lighting stalk to high beam and then back to low beam, observing both sides in each position. Separately operate the stalk’s flash-to-pass function and release it. Record whether ordinary high beams work when flash-to-pass does not; Ford diagnoses those symptoms through different paths. A dashboard indication alone does not complete the exterior observation. [High-beam and flash-to-pass checks](#/document/G1694228)

steps.title: Check each turn direction, then the hazards
steps.body: Operate the left turn signal and observe the fitted front, rear and side signaling lamps. Cancel it, repeat on the right, then operate the hazard switch and check the signaling lamps around the car. Note a dark lamp, incomplete illuminated area or intermittent behavior without assuming the bulb is responsible. Switch the hazards off afterward. Ford includes all exterior lighting and hazard-system operation in its checks. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Observe the brake lamps
steps.body: With the car secured and the helper in the driver’s seat, have them press and release the brake pedal. Observe the rear stop lamps, including the high-mounted lamp, and confirm that each responds to the pedal. Check the change in illumination rather than merely noticing that the tail lamps are already lit. Record any lamp that fails to illuminate or remains on after release. This observation forms part of the all-exterior-lights check. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Check reversing lamps without standing behind the car
steps.body: Keep the engine off. The driver should remain seated, hold the foot brake, keep the parking brake applied and select reverse using the vehicle’s normal controls with the ignition state needed for lamp operation. Observe from beside the vehicle, outside its travel path. Confirm the reversing lamps illuminate and then go out when reverse is deselected. Return the transmission to its normal secured parking state before anyone leaves the controls. If you cannot establish these conditions safely, mark the reversing lamps untested and arrange that check separately. [All exterior lights](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Work through the interior
steps.body: Operate the fitted cabin and reading lights individually. Check door-operated courtesy lighting and any fitted luggage-compartment, glovebox or vanity lighting by opening the relevant door or cover. Include instrument and control illumination through the normal lighting controls. Record the function and control setting for anything that stays dark or will not switch off. This is a practical checklist for Ford’s all-interior-lights check; safety warning lamps have their own inspection routine. [Ford owner checks](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Include the horn during a service inspection
steps.body: If you are doing the wider service inspection, briefly operate the horn where it will not create a hazard or disturb someone nearby. Record whether it sounds. Ford lists horn operation alongside the hazard-warning system in its recommended multipoint inspection. [Ford service inspection](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Turn a vague complaint into a useful finding
steps.body: Write down the side, exact lamp function, selected control position and whether the failure is constant or intermittent. For example: “Right low beam dark with ignition on and HEADLAMPS selected; left low beam works.” Include which related functions still work. If the problem disappears, record that too: Ford’s diagnostic replacement decisions assume the named fault is present during testing. [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185)

steps.title: Choose diagnosis before choosing parts
steps.body: Use the findings below to select the matching headlamp diagnostic branch. Keep the inspection at the controls and visible lamps: do not apply power or ground to lamp or module circuits as an improvised test, because a direct connection can damage components. Several failures together deserve investigation for a common supply, ground or connection fault. Bulb replacement, assembly removal and aim adjustment are separate jobs; none is a prerequisite for this operating check. [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185) · [Headlamp diagnosis](#/document/G1694228)

steps.title: Repeat the questionable function and close up
steps.body: Repeat any failed or uncertain check under the same control conditions and update the record. After any repair, repeat the affected function and its related modes to confirm normal operation. Return the lighting controls to the intended setting, switch the ignition off, and close the doors, lamp covers and luggage compartment opened for inspection. No component reassembly is required for this walkaround. [Post-repair operating checks](#/document/G1694228)

watchFor.title: Several failures at once
watchFor.body: A shared electrical fault can affect several functions. Check for a common cause before buying several lamps; that particular shopping trip can become a pain in the ass. [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185)

watchFor.title: A working lamp with a misplaced beam
watchFor.body: Illumination does not establish correct aim. Ford’s aim procedure requires level ground, correct tire inflation, normal loading, clean working headlamps and a measured screen setup. Horizontal aim is not adjustable. Treat suspected misalignment as a separate check. [Headlamp aim](#/document/G1694148)

watchFor.title: Intermittent success
watchFor.body: A lamp working today does not explain yesterday’s failure. Preserve the conditions and symptoms in your notes; do not replace a component using a fault-present diagnostic decision while the fault is absent. [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185)

procedures.purpose: Select the diagnostic branch matching the observed headlamp symptom and vehicle market.
Separate bulb-service procedure after diagnosis identifies that repair.
Separate assembly-service procedure when diagnosis requires assembly access or replacement.
Separate measured headlamp-aim check and adjustment.

stepGroups.title: Set up and inspect
stepGroups.summary: Secure the car and look for visible damage.

stepGroups.title: Check the functions
stepGroups.summary: Observe exterior lights, interior lights and the service-inspection horn check.

stepGroups.title: Record, route and finish
stepGroups.summary: Describe faults precisely, choose the next diagnostic action and restore the controls.

diagnostics.finding: One or both low beams fail with HEADLAMPS ON.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include fuses, wiring, connections, bulb, ballast, assembly or body control module; darkness alone does not identify the failed part. [Low-beam diagnosis](#/document/G1694228)
diagnostics.next: Record one-side versus both-side failure. Use Pinpoint Test A for vehicles except China, or Test B for China-market vehicles. Have circuit diagnosis completed before ordering a bulb or ballast. [Low-beam diagnostic branches](#/document/G1694228)

diagnostics.finding: High beams fail.
diagnostics.meaning: The next diagnostic decision depends on whether low beams work and whether one or both high beams fail. [High-beam diagnosis](#/document/G1694228)
diagnostics.next: If low beams also fail, address their diagnostic branch first. If low beams work, use Test C; both-high-beam failure leads first to checking the stalk input with a suitable diagnostic scan tool. [Test C](#/document/G1694228)

diagnostics.finding: Ordinary high beams work, but flash-to-pass does not.
diagnostics.meaning: The flash-to-pass input needs separate investigation; successful ordinary high beams are useful evidence. [Flash-to-pass diagnosis](#/document/G1694228)
diagnostics.next: Use Test G, which checks the steering-column control module’s recorded flash-to-pass switch input before further module diagnosis. [Test G](#/document/G1694228)

diagnostics.finding: A headlamp remains on when the corresponding function is deselected.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford treats continuously illuminated low or high beams as distinct symptoms involving control inputs, wiring or modules. [Continuous-illumination diagnosis](#/document/G1694228)
diagnostics.next: Record the ignition and switch positions and which side remains on. Low beams use Test D except China or Test E for China; high beams use Test F. [Symptom routes](#/document/G1694228)

diagnostics.finding: A diagnostic report shows U1000:00 or U3000:49.
diagnostics.meaning: U1000:00 indicates temporary output protection after excessive current; U3000:49 indicates an output has been permanently disabled. The body control module is the BCM. [BCM fault descriptions](#/document/G1694228)
diagnostics.next: Correct the underlying excessive-current fault and address other related codes first. For U1000:00, clear codes and successfully repeat the self-test after repair to restore the output. U3000:49 requires the VIN-specific guided BCM routine; correct the cause before installing a replacement module. [BCM recovery requirements](#/document/G1694228)

diagnostics.finding: A signaling, stop, reversing or interior lamp fails.
diagnostics.meaning: The operating check identifies the failed function; the supplied headlamp diagnostic chart does not establish the cause for these other lamps.
diagnostics.next: Keep the side, function and control-condition notes and arrange diagnosis for that specific lighting circuit. Avoid treating a headlamp test or replacement procedure as interchangeable with another lamp.

verification.title: Every fitted function has a result
verification.body: Confirm your record covers exterior position lighting, low and high beams, flash-to-pass, turn signals, hazards, stop lamps, reversing lamps, other fitted exterior lights and interior lighting. Mark any untested item explicitly; it is not a pass. [Ford all-lamp check](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1614692&Uid=G1661539&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

verification.title: The original symptom is checked after repair
verification.body: Repeat the original control sequence and confirm the affected lamp now responds correctly. Complete any required BCM code clearing and self-test after correcting an output-protection fault. [Repair verification](#/document/G1694228)

verification.title: Headlamp service includes aim afterward
verification.body: If subsequent work removes a headlamp assembly or replaces its bulb using these Ford procedures, headlamp adjustment is part of completing that repair. A lamp lighting up is only the operating check. [Assembly completion](#/document/G1694118) · [Bulb completion](#/document/G1694119)

notes: The illustrated motor/linkage is background context. Routine blade care does not require removing that assembly.
guides.title: Washers and wipers: keep the complete cleaning system working
guides.summary: Check fluid, spray and blade performance as connected but separate jobs.
guides.introduction: The washers loosen and carry dirt, while the blades clear the glass. Weak spray and poor wiping can happen together, but they do not necessarily have the same cause. Start with the fluid and visible condition before deciding that the motor or linkage needs replacement.
guides.why: Good visibility depends on the system working as a whole. A new wiper motor cannot correct an empty washer reservoir or a worn blade edge.

when.summary: Check washer-fluid level monthly. Check spray and wiper operation every six months; clean or replace blades as needed.

prepare.title: Use the appropriate washer fluid
prepare.detail: Choose a product suitable for the expected temperatures and vehicle requirements.

prepare.title: Inspect the glass and blades
prepare.detail: A dirty windshield or contaminated blade can affect the result of an operation check.

steps.title: Check the supply
steps.body: Confirm washer-fluid level and look for an obvious leak if the level repeatedly falls.

steps.title: Check spray and wiping
steps.body: Verify that fluid reaches the glass and that the blades clear it properly.

steps.title: Address the actual finding
steps.body: Clean or replace blades when needed. Use washer or wiper diagnosis for continuing spray, motor or linkage concerns.

watchFor.title: Continuing streaks or missed areas
watchFor.body: Inspect blade and glass condition before blaming the motor.

watchFor.title: A pump runs but fluid does not arrive
watchFor.body: Investigate the fluid path rather than assuming the motor is the only serviceable part.

procedures.purpose: Understand the wiper and washer system.
Diagnose continuing operating concerns.
Locate and service the washer reservoir if required.
Use the motor procedure only when that repair is needed.

notes: The door-removal link is for structural context or a confirmed repair, not a routine drain-cleaning step. Convertible roof seals have their own procedures.
guides.title: Body drains and weather seals: give water a way out
guides.summary: Check drainage openings and seal condition without disturbing the door or packing drain paths with products.
guides.introduction: Weather seals help manage water and wind around body openings, while designed drain holes let water escape from areas where it can collect. Both deserve attention. A wet interior does not automatically prove that the nearest weatherstrip is the failed part.
guides.why: An obstructed drain and a damaged seal create different problems and need different responses. Regular checks can reveal debris or visible wear before water is left trapped in an enclosed area.

when.summary: Every six months: check body and door drains for obstruction and door weatherstrips for wear; clean or lubricate as appropriate.
notes: Use the correct care product and application instructions for the specific seal.

prepare.title: Locate the intended openings
prepare.detail: Identify actual drainage features; do not create holes or enlarge an opening to guess at a water path.

prepare.title: Inspect before adding products
prepare.detail: Look for debris, wear and displaced seals before deciding that lubrication is the answer.

steps.title: Check the drain paths
steps.body: Look for obstruction in the designed body and door drain openings and clean as needed without damaging surrounding finishes.

steps.title: Inspect seals
steps.body: Review visible weatherstrip condition and seating. Use the approved care instructions if lubrication is needed.

steps.title: Investigate continuing water entry
steps.body: Record where and when water appears and have its path identified before replacing trim or seals.

watchFor.title: Repeated dampness
watchFor.body: The entry point can differ from where water collects. Keep observations for diagnosis.

watchFor.title: A seal displaced by another problem
watchFor.body: Door alignment or damage may need assessment rather than simply forcing the seal back into place.

procedures.purpose: Understand the front-door assembly before any confirmed door repair.
Assess door alignment when fit is part of the concern.
Review corrosion-prevention requirements after body work.

notes: Scope remains the 2015 Mustang with 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. This guide covers operation checks, installed door-latch lubrication and the accessible binding exterior key-cylinder lubrication branch.
A lubrication procedure does not mean the complete latch assembly needs replacement. Replacement follows the applicable diagnostic result. [Latch diagnosis](#/document/G1695898)
guides.title: Hinges, latches and locks: check operation, then lubricate the right place
guides.summary: Check door movement, handle release and locking operation, then use the correct lubrication sequence for a sticky latch or accessible binding key cylinder.
guides.introduction: My first move with a stubborn door is to find out which part is being a pain in the ass. Hinges let the door swing; the latch holds it closed against the striker, its mating catch on the body. Extra opening or closing effort can come from insufficient lubrication, door alignment or striker adjustment. Spraying everything nearby skips the useful part: finding the cause. [Door operation diagnosis](#/document/G1695898)
guides.why: A latch should engage securely and release easily from either handle. Targeted lubrication can restore a dry latch, but excessive grease can damage its internal lock motor. The exterior key cylinder has its own lubrication-and-retest sequence. I want smooth operation without turning a small maintenance job into an expensive one. [Latch and cylinder checks](#/document/G1695898) [Lubrication precautions](#/document/G1695899)

when.summary: Check operation every six months and lubricate where needed using the applicable procedure.
notes: Address failure to latch or release promptly.

prepare.title: Latch tools and materials
prepare.detail: Have a flat-bladed screwdriver suited to the latch opening, Motorcraft Multi-Purpose Grease Spray XL-5-A meeting ESB-M1C93-B, and a clean cloth for removing excess grease. The screwdriver operates the latch while the door remains open. [Door-latch lubrication](#/document/G1695899)

prepare.title: Optional key-cylinder materials
prepare.detail: For an accessible exterior key cylinder that binds, have the correct key and a lock lubricant such as Motorcraft XL-1. If that restores locking and unlocking, the cylinder procedure then calls for multi-purpose grease such as Motorcraft XL-5 for lasting lubrication. Keep these cylinder instructions separate from the latch’s product specification and application time. [Cylinder lubrication, G5](#/document/G1695898)

prepare.title: Access
prepare.detail: Open the door to reach the latch opening on its trailing edge. Lubrication uses the installed latch. Window-glass, trim and handle removal belong to the separate latch-replacement procedure. For the key-cylinder branch, establish the vehicle’s normal key access before starting. [Lubrication access](#/document/G1695899) [Separate latch replacement](#/document/G1695904)

prepare.title: Personal and chemical protection
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp edges. Read each product’s safety information before use. Keep solvents away from flames and other ignition sources; incorrect handling can cause injury or fire. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around the car. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle, keeping it under your control for the lock checks. An unexpected engine start during service can cause serious injury. [Service precautions](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Observe the door as it swings
steps.body:
