Move the door through its normal opening and closing travel, keeping fingers clear of the hinges and latch. Notice where resistance or noise occurs: during the swing, or only as the door meets the body. This is an observation, not an alignment measurement. Ford identifies hinges, door alignment, striker adjustment and the latch as possible causes of extra effort. [Mechanical diagnosis, Test A](#/document/G1695898)

Leave hinge and striker fasteners secured during this check. If the latch later passes its open-door test but the door remains difficult to close, have striker adjustment and door alignment assessed before deciding the hinges need lubrication. That is Ford’s diagnostic order. [Mechanical diagnosis, A2–A5](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Compare both door handles
steps.body:
With the door unlocked, check opening from the exterior handle and then the interior handle. Observe whether each handle releases the door easily and returns after being released. If a handle fails, stop closing the door for repeated trials. [Handle checks, Tests A–E](#/document/G1695898)

A problem affecting only one handle follows a different diagnostic route from a door that is difficult from both handles. Record which handle sticks, needs extra effort or fails to release; that detail helps identify the appropriate next test. [Handle diagnosis, Tests B–E](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Separate locking trouble from opening trouble
steps.body:
Press lock and unlock on the driver’s door control switch, then repeat from the passenger’s switch while observing which locks respond. Record whether the failure affects one door, both doors, only one direction or only one switch. These patterns lead to different electrical tests; they do not establish that the latch needs grease. Finish with the door unlocked. [Power-lock checks, Tests H–K](#/document/G1695898)

For an exterior key cylinder whose normal key access is established, insert the correct key and check both locking and unlocking. If it works normally, skip the cylinder service in step 5. If it rotates freely without operating the lock, arrange the linkage/free-spin diagnostic route in Test G2–G4. A binding cylinder follows the lubrication branch in step 5. [Manual-lock check, G1–G5](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Service an accessible binding key cylinder
steps.body:
Use this branch only for a symptomatic, binding exterior key cylinder with normal key access already established. Spray a lock lubricant, such as Motorcraft XL-1, into the cylinder opening for a couple of seconds. Operate the cylinder with the key and check whether it now locks and unlocks the door. [Cylinder lubrication test, G5](#/document/G1695898)

If locking and unlocking return, apply multi-purpose grease, such as Motorcraft XL-5, into the cylinder opening for a couple of seconds to provide lasting lubrication. Operate the key again and verify both functions. The cylinder application is a couple of seconds, separate from the latch’s approximately five-second application. [Cylinder lubrication and result, G5](#/document/G1695898)

If locking and unlocking do not return, stop this basic cylinder service and arrange removal-based diagnosis of the cylinder and linkage. Do not assume the latch is responsible. Finish with the door unlocked before continuing the latch checks. [Further cylinder diagnosis, G6–G7](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Test the latch with the door open
steps.body:
Open the door and identify the latch opening on its trailing edge. Keep fingers out of the moving mechanism to avoid a pinch injury. Use the flat-bladed screwdriver to move the latch into its fully latched position: two clicks. The door stays open throughout this operation. [Latch positioning](#/document/G1695899)

Remove the screwdriver and pull a door handle to check whether the latch releases easily. Repeat the two-click setup to check release from the other handle. Always return the latch to its released position before moving the door closed. [Open-door latch test, A2](#/document/G1695898)

If both handles release it easily, skip latch lubrication and proceed to step 11; use the diagnostic decisions below for any remaining movement complaint. If both releases are stiff, continue with lubrication. If only one handle fails, stop here and arrange the corresponding handle/cable diagnosis. [Diagnostic branches, A1–A3 and Tests B–C](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Lubricate the latch opening
steps.body:
For a latch needing lubrication, leave the door open and use the screwdriver to set the latch fully closed again, through two clicks. Remove the screwdriver. Spray Motorcraft Multi-Purpose Grease Spray XL-5-A, specification ESB-M1C93-B, into the latch opening for approximately 5 seconds. [Application sequence and material](#/document/G1695899)

Use the specified approximately five-second application. Excessive grease can damage the internal lock motor. [Over-lubrication precaution](#/document/G1695899)

steps.title: Release the latch before closing the door
steps.body:
Operate the exterior door handle to release the latch. Ford notes that exterior handles may operate mechanically or electronically; use the handle’s normal operation. Confirm that the latch has returned to its open position before closing the door. [Exterior-handle release](#/document/G1695899)

If the latch will not release, keep the door open and stop the cycling sequence. Arrange diagnosis rather than trying to close the door against an already closed latch. [Release check, A3](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Distribute the lubricant and clean up
steps.body: Once the latch is released, open and close the door several times to circulate the lubricant inside it. Then open the door and wipe away excess grease from the exposed latch area. Keep fingers clear of the moving mechanism. [Distribution and cleanup](#/document/G1695899)

steps.title: Retest the serviced latch
steps.body:
After lubrication, repeat the open-door test: use the screwdriver to close the latch through two clicks, remove the tool, and check easy release with each handle, resetting the latch between trials. Leave it released when finished. [Post-lubrication test, A3](#/document/G1695898)

Easy release after the original stiffness indicates insufficient latch lubrication caused that concern. If release remains difficult in the both-handles diagnostic branch, Ford directs latch replacement. Arrange that separate repair instead of adding more spray. [Result and repair decision, A3](#/document/G1695898)

steps.title: Confirm complete door operation
steps.body:
With the screwdriver and cloth clear and the latch released, close the door normally. Confirm that it engages securely, then unlock and open it using each handle in separate trials. Persistent extra closing effort calls for striker and door-alignment assessment even if the latch itself releases easily. [Door operation checks, Test A](#/document/G1695898)

Repeat the lock/unlock checks from both door switches and note any remaining fault. If you serviced the accessible key cylinder, confirm that the key still locks and unlocks correctly after its final lubrication. Finish unlocked. [Power-lock checks, Tests H–K](#/document/G1695898) [Cylinder result, G5](#/document/G1695898)

watchFor.title: A door that needs slamming
watchFor.body: Extra force can involve the striker, door alignment, hinges or latch. Have the cause assessed instead of accepting a harder slam as routine operation. [Possible causes, Test A](#/document/G1695898)

watchFor.title: A handle that stays pulled out
watchFor.body: Binding linkage or a failed return spring can cause a sticking handle. Arrange the appropriate handle diagnosis. [Sticking-handle diagnosis, Tests D–E](#/document/G1695898)

watchFor.title: A latch left closed while the door is open
watchFor.body: The screwdriver test deliberately closes the latch without closing the door. Release it with the handle before every actual door-closing attempt. Keep fingers out of its moving parts. [Latch setup and release sequence](#/document/G1695899)

watchFor.title: Persistent rattles
watchFor.body: Ford’s noise diagnosis checks for loose internal components, striker adjustment and door alignment before judging the result of latch lubrication. A rattle alone does not prove the latch needs replacement. [Noise diagnosis, Test F](#/document/G1695898)

procedures.purpose: Installed door-latch positioning, specified grease, application, release, cycling and cleanup.
Operation checks, accessible binding-cylinder lubrication and symptom-based decisions for door movement, handles and locks.
Separate latch-replacement reference when diagnosis requires repair; its removal operations are not lubrication prerequisites.
Task-relevant starting, personal-protection and chemical precautions.
Avoid replacement decisions based on a fault that is not present during testing.

stepGroups.title: Set up, identify the symptom and check locks
stepGroups.summary: Separate door movement, handle release and electrical locking complaints; service an accessible binding key cylinder when appropriate.

stepGroups.title: Check and lubricate the latch
stepGroups.summary: Use the two-click setup, controlled application, exterior-handle release and cleanup sequence.

stepGroups.title: Retest and finish
stepGroups.summary: Verify the latch result and complete door and lock operation.

diagnostics.finding: The latch was stiff from both handles and releases easily after lubrication.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies insufficient latch lubrication as the cause in this diagnostic branch.
diagnostics.next: Complete the normal door and locking checks, then wipe away any remaining excess. [A3 result](#/document/G1695898) [Cleanup](#/document/G1695899)

diagnostics.finding: The latch releases easily with the door open, but closing the door still takes unusual effort.
diagnostics.meaning: The open-door test has not established a latch lubrication fault.
diagnostics.next: Have striker adjustment checked, followed by door alignment. Ford calls for hinge lubrication after those checks pass. [A4–A5 sequence](#/document/G1695898)

diagnostics.finding: Only the interior or exterior handle has trouble releasing the door.
diagnostics.meaning: The affected handle, cable or linkage needs isolation before condemning the latch.
diagnostics.next: Arrange the corresponding interior- or exterior-handle diagnosis. [Tests B–C](#/document/G1695898)

diagnostics.finding: The latch remains difficult to release after the specified lubrication in the both-handles branch.
diagnostics.meaning: The lubrication test has failed.
diagnostics.next: Arrange latch replacement as a separate repair. [A3 replacement decision](#/document/G1695898) [Front-door latch repair](#/document/G1695904)

diagnostics.finding: The exterior key cylinder rotates freely without locking or unlocking.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford routes this symptom through checks of the cylinder-to-latch connections and the cylinder’s free-spin operation.
diagnostics.next: Arrange Test G2–G4 diagnosis. Skip the binding-cylinder lubrication branch. [Free-spin diagnosis](#/document/G1695898)

diagnostics.finding: An accessible binding key cylinder locks and unlocks after the initial lock lubricant.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford identifies insufficient cylinder lubrication as the cause.
diagnostics.next: Complete step 5’s couple-second multi-purpose grease application, then verify key-operated locking and unlocking again. [Cylinder lubrication result, G5](#/document/G1695898)

diagnostics.finding: The binding key cylinder still does not lock and unlock after the initial lubricant.
diagnostics.meaning: The basic lubrication test has not resolved the fault.
diagnostics.next: Stop cylinder service and arrange removal-based cylinder and linkage diagnosis. [Cylinder diagnosis, G6–G7](#/document/G1695898)

diagnostics.finding: Power locking remains intermittent or fails from particular switches or in one direction.
diagnostics.meaning: The symptom needs electrical diagnosis; lubrication alone does not identify its cause.
diagnostics.next: Provide the observed door, switch and direction pattern for Tests H–K. An intermittent fault that is absent during testing is not grounds for guessing at replacement components. [Electrical symptom routes](#/document/G1695898) [Diagnostic assumptions](#/document/G1693185)

verification.title: Latch released and tools clear
verification.body: Before the final closure, confirm that the latch is open and the screwdriver has been removed. [Lubrication release sequence](#/document/G1695899)

verification.title: Engagement and release restored
verification.body: Confirm that the door engages securely and opens easily from both handles when unlocked. Persistent difficulty requires the appropriate diagnostic branch. If it will not latch securely or release reliably, stop using the car until the fault is corrected. [Door operation checks, Test A](#/document/G1695898)

verification.title: Locking checked separately
verification.body: Check both door switches in both directions and record any remaining failure. If the accessible key cylinder was serviced, verify that it locks and unlocks after the final grease application. [Lock checks, Tests G–K](#/document/G1695898)

verification.title: Excess removed
verification.body: Wipe away excess grease from the exposed latch area after cycling the door. [Final lubrication step](#/document/G1695899)

notes: Do not use this inspection as permission to probe, power or dismantle a pretensioner. Restraint repairs have dedicated safety requirements.
guides.title: Seatbelts and seat latches: check the parts you rely on
guides.summary: Inspect wear and function, and keep routine checks separate from the inspection required after a collision.
guides.introduction: The seatbelt’s webbing, buckle, retractor and anchorages work together to restrain an occupant. Seat latches must also hold their intended position. A routine check should look beyond whether the buckle clicks: the complete assembly needs to remain in good condition.
guides.why: Damage to one part can compromise the whole restraint path. A belt that appears to operate normally after a collision has not thereby passed the required post-collision inspection.

when.summary: Check seatbelts and seat latches for wear and proper function every six months.
notes: Collision repair requires the separate inspection of all seatbelt components.

prepare.title: Inspect every seating position
prepare.detail: Do not limit the check to the belt used most often.

prepare.title: Keep cleaning appropriate
prepare.detail: Use the recommended cleaning method; do not bleach or re-dye seatbelt webbing.

steps.title: Review visible condition
steps.body: Inspect accessible webbing and components for damage, and confirm that belt routing is correct.

steps.title: Check operation
steps.body: Check buckle, retractor and seat-latch function using the appropriate inspection procedure.

steps.title: Escalate a defect or collision history
steps.body: Use the dedicated restraint diagnosis or post-collision procedure. Replacement must include the prescribed checks, not simply bolting in a part.

watchFor.title: Frayed, damaged or twisted webbing
watchFor.body: Have the condition assessed; do not conceal it with a cover or chemical treatment.

watchFor.title: A latch that does not engage reliably
watchFor.body: Address it before relying on that seating position.

procedures.purpose: Perform seatbelt maintenance inspection.
Follow the belt-cleaning precautions.
Use the required post-collision procedure.
Understand the front retractor/pretensioner assembly.
Service a confirmed rear seat-backrest latch concern.

notes: The cluster can display warnings from other modules. Replacing the display is not the default response to an active warning.
guides.title: Warning lamps: know a check from an active warning
guides.summary: Check that safety indicators work and respond to the actual message instead of merely clearing it.
guides.introduction: Warning lamps and messages are part of the car’s conversation with you. An indicator’s normal start-up behavior differs from a warning that remains on or appears while driving. Checking operation is useful maintenance; interpreting an active warning requires the meaning of that exact lamp or message.
guides.why: A working warning system can alert you to a developing problem. Clearing a code or turning a reminder off does not repair the system that produced it.

when.summary: Check operation of brake, ABS, airbag and seatbelt warning lamps every six months.
notes: Respond to an active warning when it occurs; do not wait for the routine check.

prepare.title: Know the expected behavior
prepare.detail: Use the information-display and system descriptions for the actual fitted cluster.

prepare.title: Record the exact message
prepare.detail: A photograph taken while safely parked can help preserve wording and conditions for diagnosis.

steps.title: Observe normal start-up indications
steps.body: Compare the lamp behavior with the described operation rather than assuming every illuminated lamp is a fault.

steps.title: Act on a continuing warning
steps.body: Follow the action associated with that exact message. Do not treat a brake-system warning as an oil-service reminder.

steps.title: Diagnose before clearing
steps.body: Use the relevant system’s tests to find the reason, then verify that the warning behaves normally after repair.

watchFor.title: Low engine oil pressure
watchFor.body: Stop safely and turn off the engine; check the level and obtain assistance if the warning persists.

watchFor.title: Check Brake System or low brake fluid
watchFor.body: Stop safely and arrange prompt brake-system assessment.

procedures.purpose: Understand cluster indicators and message operation.
Diagnose instrumentation and message concerns.
Follow brake-system diagnosis.

notes: Scope: 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. The clutch-reservoir discussion applies to manual-transmission vehicles.
Filling after a repair, brake-pressure bleeding, clutch bleeding and master-cylinder replacement are separate jobs.
guides.title: Brake and clutch fluid: check the level without masking the problem
guides.summary: Check the reservoir on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine, recognize the normal range, and know when the reading needs immediate service.
guides.introduction: I approach this as a look, read and decide job. A bottle of fluid is a lousy diagnostic tool, however reassuring the glug sounds. Ford says fluid between MIN and MAX needs no addition; a reading outside that range needs immediate service because system performance could be compromised. There is no prize for making every normal reading touch MAX. [Ford fluid-level guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1605311&Uid=G1642989&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)
guides.why: The reservoir supplies the brake hydraulic system and, on manual-transmission cars, the clutch hydraulic supply also uses this reservoir. That makes identifying the correct reservoir important. A normal level does not explain away a sinking or spongy brake pedal: Ford lists leaks, air and component faults among the possible causes of those symptoms. [Master cylinder](#/document/G1692560) · [Clutch reservoir](#/document/G1704358) · [Brake diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

when.summary: Check fluid level as part of the recommended multi-point inspection at scheduled service, and respond immediately to a low-fluid warning.
notes: This guide does not assign a blanket calendar replacement interval not stated by the reviewed 2015 schedule.

prepare.title: Make the underhood inspection safe
prepare.detail: Switch the ignition off and remove the key to prevent someone starting the engine during the check. If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around the car; an unexpected start can cause serious injury. Wear eye protection. Cooling fans can operate with the ignition off, so keep clear; working nearby requires disabling them first. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Get a clear view
prepare.detail: Open the hood and have enough light to see the reservoir wall, its MIN and MAX markings, and the fluid boundary. An optional inspection light can help. This check reads the reservoir from outside with its cap fitted. Ford’s illustrations show both the reservoir location and the marked viewing area. [Reservoir location](#/document/G1692560) · [Level markings](#/document/G2361881)

steps.title: Find the brake-fluid reservoir
steps.body: Locate the reservoir mounted on the brake master cylinder, in front of the large round brake booster near the rear of the engine compartment. Match the assembly and its MIN/MAX markings rather than identifying it by cap color alone; the illustrations use color to highlight parts. Leave the cap, electrical connector and hydraulic tubes attached. Master-cylinder removal is a separate repair. [Master-cylinder assembly](#/document/G1692560) · [Reservoir markings](#/document/G2361881)

steps.title: Identify the manual-transmission connection
steps.body: On a manual-transmission Mustang, this is also the reservoir used for the clutch hydraulic supply. Read the same reservoir level; do not disconnect the clutch supply tube to check it. On an automatic, proceed with the brake-fluid check. [Manual-transmission connection](#/document/G1692560) · [Brake/clutch reservoir](#/document/G1704358)

steps.title: Read the fluid against both marks
steps.body: Look through the reservoir wall and compare the fluid boundary with MIN and MAX. If it is within that marked range, Ford considers the level normal and says no fluid needs adding. If you cannot clearly distinguish the boundary, improve the lighting or viewing angle; do not record a guessed result. [Level viewing area](#/document/G2361881) · [Ford normal range](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1605311&Uid=G1642989&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

steps.title: Act on the reading and any symptoms
steps.body:
If the level is below MIN or above MAX, arrange immediate service. Do not add or siphon fluid simply to make an unexplained reading look normal: Ford warns that an out-of-range level can compromise system performance. Report the actual reading, any previous additions, warning lamps and pedal changes. [Ford abnormal-level guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1605311&Uid=G1642989&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

A pedal that sinks, travels excessively or feels spongy needs brake-system diagnosis even when the reservoir looks normal. Ford calls for leak inspection, necessary repairs and bleeding where leaks or air are involved; other listed causes require their own tests. Treat that as an active braking concern and arrange assistance before driving. [Brake symptom diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

steps.title: Finish the inspection
steps.body: Confirm the reservoir cap remains fitted, remove your inspection light or other belongings from the engine compartment, and close the hood. Note the level and any symptoms so a later comparison or service visit has something useful to work with. A visual level check does not require disconnecting hydraulic components. If a brake hydraulic component has been disconnected during other work, pressure bleeding becomes a required service operation before the repair is complete. [Component bleeding requirements](#/document/G1694693)

watchFor.title: A level that keeps falling
watchFor.body: Report the repeated drop and any fluid previously added. Repeated filling does not establish the cause; Ford’s brake diagnosis directs leak inspection and repair when hydraulic symptoms point to leaks or air. [Brake diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

watchFor.title: A warning lamp with a normal level
watchFor.body: Do not assume the warning is harmless. Ford lists the fluid-level switch, parking-brake switch, wiring and instrument/control electronics among possible causes of an abnormal red brake-warning indication. [Warning-indicator diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

watchFor.title: Dirt or fluid spills during subsequent service
watchFor.body: If service requires opening the reservoir, clean the area around the cap first and use clean, specified fluid. Brake fluid can damage paint: immediately wash any spill on paintwork with cold water. [Clean handling and paint protection](#/document/G2361881)

procedures.purpose: Identify the reservoir and manual-transmission supply connection; master-cylinder removal remains a separate repair.
Route abnormal pedal behavior and brake-warning indications to the appropriate diagnosis.
Support reservoir viewing and clean handling; pressure bleeding belongs to applicable hydraulic service.
Explain why disconnecting a brake hydraulic component requires pressure bleeding.
Confirm the shared brake/clutch reservoir on manual-transmission vehicles.

stepGroups.title: Identify the reservoir
stepGroups.summary: Find the correct assembly and account for the manual-transmission clutch supply.

stepGroups.title: Read, decide and finish
stepGroups.summary: Compare the level with the marks, recognize problems and complete the check.

diagnostics.finding: Fluid is within MIN–MAX and there are no reported braking symptoms.
diagnostics.meaning: The reservoir level is in Ford’s normal operating range.
diagnostics.next: Leave the level alone; no addition is needed. This result confirms the level, not the condition of every brake component. [Ford fluid-level guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1605311&Uid=G1642989&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

diagnostics.finding: Fluid is below MIN or above MAX.
diagnostics.meaning: The reading is outside the normal range and system performance could be compromised.
diagnostics.next: Seek immediate service and report the reading before altering it. [Ford abnormal-level guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1605311&Uid=G1642989&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259)

diagnostics.finding: The brake pedal sinks, has excessive travel or feels spongy.
diagnostics.meaning: Leaks or air are possible, but the master cylinder and other components are also listed diagnostic paths.
diagnostics.next: Arrange brake-system diagnosis and assistance before driving. Repair the identified cause and complete the applicable bleeding operation; do not assume topping up fixes it. [Brake pedal diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

diagnostics.finding: The red brake warning and yellow ABS warning are illuminated together.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford directs diagnosis toward stored ABS diagnostic trouble codes.
diagnostics.next: Arrange an ABS fault-code check and diagnosis rather than using reservoir level as the sole explanation. [Brake warning diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

verification.title: You have a definite reading
verification.body: You can identify the fluid boundary and both marks, and have recorded whether the level is inside or outside the normal range. An unreadable boundary is an unfinished check. [Reservoir viewing area](#/document/G2361881)

verification.title: The next action matches the result
verification.body: A normal level needs no addition. An out-of-range level has an immediate service plan, and abnormal pedal behavior or warning indications have not been dismissed because the level looks acceptable. [Ford level guidance](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/vdirsnet/OwnerManual/Home/Content?ProcUid=G1605311&Uid=G1642989&buildtype=web&countryCode=USA&div=f&languageCode=en&userMarket=usa&vFilteringEnabled=False&variantid=3259) · [Brake diagnosis](#/document/G1721936)

verification.title: The car is closed up
verification.body: The reservoir cap is fitted, inspection equipment is accounted for and the hood is closed. No hydraulic connection was disturbed during this visual check.

guides.title: Pressure-bleed the brake hydraulic system
guides.summary: Remove air after hydraulic repairs, with the correct fluid, pressure equipment and wheel sequence. Includes the extra steps for a new ABS hydraulic unit.
guides.introduction: The brake pedal sends force through fluid to the calipers. Air compresses much more readily than brake fluid, so trapped air can use up pedal travel before the pads clamp firmly. Pressure bleeding feeds clean fluid into the reservoir and carries air out through the caliper bleeders. It belongs after the reason for air entry has been repaired.
guides.why: A low or spongy pedal can come from a leak or trapped air, but it can also have other causes. Bleeding cannot repair a leaking connection, a faulty master cylinder or a damaged hose. The brake diagnostic chart separates these faults; starting there avoids treating a temporarily improved pedal as proof that the car is repaired.

when.summary: After a brake hydraulic component is disconnected, or when diagnosis identifies air after the leak or fault is repaired.
notes: Pressure bleeding is required after disconnecting a caliper, hose, tube or other brake hydraulic component. A newly installed master cylinder also needs the priming operation in Component Bleeding.
This is condition-based repair work. These procedures do not establish a calendar or mileage interval for flushing brake fluid.

prepare.title: Confirm the repair and brake configuration
prepare.detail: Identify the installed front caliper type, the rear parking-brake arrangement, and whether the car is left- or right-hand drive. Have the pressure-bleeding illustrations and the correct bleeder torque information available before opening a bleeder.

prepare.title: Use the specified fluid and clean equipment
prepare.detail: Use clean Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance brake fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. Prepare a brake/clutch pressure bleeder with a correctly fitting reservoir adapter, a clear bleed hose and a clean fluid container. Follow the equipment maker’s setup instructions.

prepare.title: Plan access and any ABS service operation
prepare.detail: Use the proper lifting and wheel-removal procedure. If a new hydraulic control unit has been installed, arrange a diagnostic scan tool capable of the ABS Service Bleed function before starting.

prepare.title: Protect nearby surfaces
prepare.detail: Clean around the reservoir cap before removal. If fluid spills, wash the affected component immediately with cold water; keep dirt and foreign material out of the fluid supply.

steps.title: Repair the cause and prime a new master cylinder
steps.body: Inspect for leaks and complete the hydraulic repair first. When the master cylinder is new, follow Component Bleeding to prime it with a master-cylinder bleeding set before bleeding the rest of the system. Do not use repeated bleeding to work around an unresolved leak.

steps.title: Set up a clean, pressurized fluid supply
steps.body: Fill the reservoir with the specified fluid and attach the correct pressure-bleeder adapter. Make sure the tank holds enough clean fluid for the operation, then connect it as its manufacturer directs. The pressure-bleeding procedure specifies 207–345 kPa (30–50 psi).

steps.title: Use the wheel sequence for the car’s steering layout
steps.body: Remove the wheels as directed and use the left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive sequence illustration in Brake System Pressure Bleeding. The two sequences differ. Keep that diagram open rather than substituting a remembered “furthest wheel first” order.

steps.title: Clear each caliper, including its additional bleeders
steps.body: Remove a bleeder cap if fitted. Partly fill a clean container with specified fluid, connect the hose and keep its outlet submerged. Open the bleeder 180 degrees and allow fluid to flow until it is clear and bubble-free, then close it to the confirmed specification. Four- and six-piston front calipers require the inner bleeder before the outer one. At rear calipers with an integral parking brake, apply and release the parking brake five times, then reopen the bleeder 180 degrees until clear fluid flows; repeat as necessary. Complete the remaining wheel ends in the prescribed order.

steps.title: Complete the extra cycle when the hydraulic unit is new
steps.body: For a newly installed ABS hydraulic control unit, perform the diagnostic tool’s ABS Service Bleed operation and then repeat the complete pressure-bleeding procedure. The first pressure bleed alone does not finish this repair.

steps.title: Release pressure, restore the level and verify operation
steps.body: Reinstall bleeder caps where fitted, lower the vehicle as directed, close the pressure-tank valve and release its pressure before removing the equipment. Fill the reservoir to the correct level and install its cap. Refit the wheels using their full installation instructions, inspect for leaks and confirm normal brake operation before the controlled road test required by the procedure.

watchFor.title: The pedal still sinks or feels spongy
watchFor.body: Return to the brake diagnostic chart. It distinguishes leaks and air from master-cylinder, hose, caliper and hydraulic-control-unit faults; an unresolved pedal concern is not a completed bleed.

watchFor.title: A six-piston torque discrepancy
watchFor.body: The available six-piston front-bleeder torque entry contains an inconsistent unit pair. Confirm the correct specification for the fitted caliper before tightening; do not choose one of the conflicting values by assumption.

watchFor.title: Air introduced during setup
watchFor.body: An unprimed replacement master cylinder, a dirty connection or an inadequate fluid supply can undermine the work. Finish the required preparation before moving through the wheel sequence.

notes: The rear parking-brake cycling instruction applies to calipers with the integral parking-brake arrangement described in the procedure.

procedures.purpose: Complete pressure-bleeding sequence, illustrated wheel order and new-HCU finishing steps.
Prime a new master cylinder and identify when disconnected hydraulic components require pressure bleeding.
Diagnose low, spongy or sinking brake-pedal symptoms before choosing bleeding as the repair.
Check the required fluid and fitted-brake specifications; note the six-piston torque discrepancy explained above.
Remove and reinstall wheels with the correct seating, tightening and recheck instructions.

guides.title: Cooling-system pressure testing: follow the leak, skip the parts lottery
guides.summary: Check the cap separately, pressure-test the cold cooling system, and follow the results on a 2015 Mustang with the factory 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L cooling system.

applicability.equipment: Factory cooling system; select the engine-specific diagnostic article.

guides.introduction: When coolant disappears, I want evidence before buying a damn thing. The cooling system contains coolant while accommodating expansion, contraction and changing pressure. Its hoses, seals, joints and expansion bottle all have to seal. These engines have their pressure cap on the expansion bottle—Ford calls it the degas bottle—and have no radiator cap. The cap test and system test below check different parts of that sealing job. [2.3L cooling](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L cooling](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L cooling](#/document/G1694609)
guides.why: A pressure drop gives you a reason to investigate; escaping coolant gives you a place to investigate. Neither automatically condemns a head gasket. A successful pressure test also leaves fan, pump and thermostat performance as separate questions: Ford provides distinct diagnostic paths for coolant loss, overheating and slow warm-up. [2.3L diagnosis](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L diagnosis](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L diagnosis](#/document/G1694609)

when.summary: When coolant loss or an engine-specific diagnostic path calls for a cooling-system pressure test.
notes: This is a diagnostic check, with no mileage-based pressure-testing interval in these procedures.
Start with the relevant 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L article below. Their pressure-test values agree, but their component layouts and diagnostic branches must stay with the fitted engine.

prepare.title: Make the engine safe to work around
prepare.detail: Let the engine and cooling system become cold. Never loosen the cap with the engine running or the system hot: pressurized steam and coolant can escape forcefully and cause serious injury. [Cooling-system safety](#/document/G1693187) Keep the ignition off and the key out of the vehicle. If equipped, disable remote start through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup so another person cannot start the engine during the inspection. Wear eye and ear protection and consult the safety information for the materials you use. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189)

prepare.title: Gather the pressure tester and both adapters
prepare.detail: Use a cooling-system pressure tester, such as Ford-listed radiator tester 014-R1072 or equivalent. Cap testing requires Snap-On TA53 or equivalent; bottle testing requires Snap-On TA52, AST ASSFZ-47, Redline RDL95-0750 or equivalent. Have the equipment instructions available for attachment, testing and pressure release. A way to time approximately two minutes and record readings is useful. [2.3L equipment](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L equipment](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L equipment](#/document/G1694609)

prepare.title: Have the correct coolant and inspection equipment
prepare.detail: For any necessary level correction, the specified products are Motorcraft Orange prediluted VC-3DIL-B meeting WSS-M97B44-D2, or concentrated VC-3-B meeting WSS-M97B44-D mixed appropriately with distilled water. Have a coolant/battery refractometer, 300-ROB75240 or equivalent, to check concentration. A thick cloth is required when releasing pressure at the bottle cap. [2.3L coolant handling](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L coolant handling](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L coolant handling](#/document/G1694583)

prepare.title: Plan for the internal-leak branch
prepare.detail: If coolant loss has no external explanation, the diagnostic sequence includes a combustion-gas check using UView UVU560000-R or equivalent and its supplied instructions. Have that equipment available or arrange that test as the next diagnostic action. This is separate from the hand-pump pressure test. [2.3L loss-of-coolant test](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L loss-of-coolant test](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L loss-of-coolant test](#/document/G1694609)

prepare.title: Work at the bottle without adding a teardown
prepare.detail: Open the hood and identify the degas bottle and its pressure cap. The pressure-test procedures connect the equipment there without requiring draining, lifting, shield removal or bottle removal. Keep hands and equipment clear of cooling fans, which may operate with the ignition off. Inspect fans for visible damage before underhood work; a damaged fan requires replacement before continuing. If an inspection requires working near a fan, it must first be disabled. [2.3L test access](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L test access](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L test access](#/document/G1694609), [Fan safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Record the complaint and cold starting condition
steps.body: With the engine cold and ignition off, note the coolant level in the bottle, when the loss occurs, any coolant odor or previously observed steam, and any retrieved cooling-related diagnostic trouble codes. Check whether the cap was installed correctly. Include recent cooling-system repairs in your notes; a connection disturbed during earlier work deserves attention. Correct an obvious identified fault and verify the result before extending the diagnosis. [2.3L inspection](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L inspection](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L inspection](#/document/G1694609), [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185)

steps.title: Look for external leak evidence
steps.body:
Inspect accessible hoses, tubes, clamps, gasket and O-ring joints, thermostat housing, radiator, pressure cap, degas bottle and coolant pump. Look for both escaping coolant and cracked or damaged parts. Include the pump's weep hole, cylinder-block and cylinder-head core plugs, and block heater if fitted. A wet cabin floor or coolant odor inside can point toward the heater core, the coolant-fed heat exchanger for the cabin. Record the location rather than naming a failed part by proximity. [2.3L leak checks](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L leak checks](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L leak checks](#/document/G1694609)

Keep these additional inspection points with the fitted engine:

- **3.7L:** include the lower intake manifold and transmission fluid cooler where fitted. [3.7L inspection](#/document/G1694576)
- **5.0L:** include the lower intake manifold and oil cooler. Ford lists the oil cooler as a possible internal or external leak source. [5.0L inspection](#/document/G1694609)

steps.title: Remove the cold cap and inspect its seal
steps.body:
Once the system is cold, cover the cap with a thick cloth when releasing pressure, then remove it. The cloth does not make opening a hot system safe. [Cooling-system safety](#/document/G1693187), [2.3L cap handling](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L cap handling](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L cap handling](#/document/G1694583)

Inspect the cap and bottle sealing area for damaged O-rings, crossed threads, burrs or other defects that prevent sealing. Replace the defective cap and/or bottle rather than testing through a known sealing fault. [2.3L cap inspection](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L cap inspection](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L cap inspection](#/document/G1694609)

**2.3L and 5.0L:** Ford also directs replacement of the cap and/or bottle when coolant expelled through the cap may have contaminated the gasket. That additional replacement instruction appears in these two engine procedures. [2.3L instruction](#/document/G1673122), [5.0L instruction](#/document/G1694609)

steps.title: Check coolant condition and correct the level
steps.body:
Inspect the coolant before topping up. Clear, uncontaminated Orange coolant may normally become pink or light red. Sediment, rust coloration, an oily sheen or milky-brown fluid needs the follow-up described below. Incorrect coolant requires corrective flushing and refilling as a separate service; adding more of the correct product does not undo contamination. [2.3L coolant inspection](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L coolant inspection](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L coolant inspection](#/document/G1694609)

If appearance is acceptable, measure concentration with the refractometer. The normal recommendation is **48–50% coolant**, expressed as **48/52 to 50/50 coolant to distilled water**, giving freeze protection of **−34 to −37°C (−30 to −34°F)**. Extreme climates may require adjustment, but do not go below **40%** or above **60%** coolant. Too little reduces freeze/corrosion protection; too much reduces overheat protection. [2.3L concentration](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L concentration](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L concentration](#/document/G1694583)

For an existing concentration within the normal range, use the specified prediluted coolant for topping up. Otherwise, adjust with the specified concentrate and/or distilled water according to the measured concentration. For this cold setup, the filling procedures identify the top of the **MIN FILL LEVEL** marking as the cold level. Do not mix coolant types or add alcohol, methanol or brine; these can compromise protection and damage the engine. [2.3L level correction](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L level correction](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L level correction](#/document/G1694583)

steps.title: Test the cap separately
steps.body: Attach the pressure tester to the removed cap using **Snap-On TA53 or equivalent**, following the equipment instructions. The cap must hold **145 kPa ± 21 kPa (21 psi ± 3 psi)**. Replace a cap that fails this check. Release the tester pressure as its instructions direct before disconnecting the cap. Keep this result separate from the bottle-connected system test: the cap's specification is not a system pumping target. [2.3L cap test](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L cap test](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L cap test](#/document/G1694609)

steps.title: Connect to the bottle and build pressure slowly
steps.body: Fit the bottle adapter—**Snap-On TA52, AST ASSFZ-47, Redline RDL95-0750 or equivalent**—and connect the pressure tester according to its instructions. Keep the engine off. Slowly operate the pump until the gauge reads **124–138 kPa (18–20 psi)**. Fast pumping can produce a misleading reading. Stay within this test band; excess pressure can damage cooling-system components. Do not pump toward the separate cap-test value. [2.3L system test](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L system test](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L system test](#/document/G1694609)

steps.title: Watch the gauge and locate escaping coolant
steps.body: Observe the gauge for approximately **two minutes**. Ford expects **no pressure drop** during that period. Record the starting and ending readings. If pressure falls, inspect the accessible leak points from step 2 for escaping coolant, keeping clear of the fan. Record the pressure loss and exactly where leakage appears before selecting a repair. [2.3L observation criteria](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L observation criteria](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L observation criteria](#/document/G1694609), [Fan safety](#/document/G1693189)

steps.title: Release test pressure before disconnecting anything
steps.body: Use the tester's pressure-release instructions before removing the tester and bottle adapter. Do this whether the test held pressure or revealed a leak; do not start loosening components to repair a pressurized system. The Ford procedure calls for tester removal after a successful hold, followed by cap installation. If coolant loss remains unexplained, complete the checks below before final closure. [2.3L test completion](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L test completion](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L test completion](#/document/G1694609), [Pressure hazard](#/document/G1693187)

steps.title: Check for fluid mixing when no external leak explains the loss
steps.body:
If pressure fell without a visible external leak, an internal leak is possible. Also continue this branch when investigating coolant loss that has no external explanation, even if the pressure test held. [2.3L loss-of-coolant path](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L loss-of-coolant path](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L loss-of-coolant path](#/document/G1694609)

Inspect coolant in the bottle for engine oil. Then remove the engine-oil dipstick—the oil level indicator—and inspect the oil on it for coolant; refit the dipstick after inspection. Oil in coolant or coolant in engine oil calls for engine diagnosis rather than guessing which gasket failed. [2.3L internal checks](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L internal checks](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L internal checks](#/document/G1694609)

**3.7L and 5.0L:** their loss-of-coolant procedures also ask you to inspect the coolant for transmission fluid. If you suspect it, record the finding and arrange fluid identification and further diagnosis before choosing a repair. The observation alone does not identify the failed component. [3.7L fluid inspection](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L fluid inspection](#/document/G1694609)

steps.title: Complete the combustion-gas check if the fluid checks are negative
steps.body: If neither fluid-mixing check identifies a concern, use **UView combustion leak tester UVU560000-R or equivalent** to check for combustion gases, following that tester's supplied setup, operating and interpretation instructions. Do not improvise engine temperature, test duration or reagent criteria from the hand-pump test. A positive result leads to engine diagnosis. With no external leak, no fluid mixing and a negative combustion-gas test, Ford's loss-of-coolant path ends with the cooling system judged operational. That conclusion does not erase an observed, unresolved pressure drop. [2.3L combustion-gas branch](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L combustion-gas branch](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L combustion-gas branch](#/document/G1694609)

steps.title: Refit the cap and document the outcome
steps.body:
After removing all test equipment and completing any level correction with the system cold, install the serviceable or replacement degas-bottle cap until it reaches its **hard stop**. Record the cap result, system readings, visible leak location, fluid observations and any combustion-gas result. [2.3L closure](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L closure](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L closure](#/document/G1694609)

An identified leak requires repair before calling the concern resolved. After correction, repeat the applicable checks and verify normal operation. If the repair drains or opens the coolant circuit, complete the fitted engine's filling and bleeding procedure before operational verification; those are separate repair steps, not automatic prerequisites for this pressure test. [2.3L verification](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L verification](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L verification](#/document/G1694609), [2.3L filling and bleeding](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L filling and bleeding](#/document/G1694549), [5.0L filling and bleeding](#/document/G1694583)

watchFor.title: Normal color change versus contamination
watchFor.body: Clear Orange coolant turning pink or light red does not by itself justify replacement or flushing. Rust-colored fluid, sediment or foreign material does require corrective attention. Dark orange coolant containing debris may indicate stop-leak material, which can restrict coolant flow. [2.3L coolant condition](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L coolant condition](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L coolant condition](#/document/G1694609)

watchFor.title: Oil-like appearance
watchFor.body: An iridescent surface sheen may indicate traces of oil; milky-brown coolant may indicate more substantial oil contamination. These observations warrant diagnosis, not a head-gasket verdict by color alone. Ford also calls for corrective flushing and refilling when oil contamination is present. [2.3L contamination](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L contamination](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L contamination](#/document/G1694609)

watchFor.title: Incorrect coolant can hide in an ordinary-looking mixture
watchFor.body: Suspected Motorcraft Gold contamination requires the nitrite check supplied with the 3-Way HD Antifreeze Coolant Test Kit, 328-2050-62291 or equivalent; appearance alone may not reveal it. A positive nitrite finding calls for flushing and refilling with the specified mixture as a separate service. [2.3L contamination check](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L contamination check](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L contamination check](#/document/G1694609)

notes: I keep the cap result, system pressure result and combustion-gas result on separate lines. Three different questions deserve three actual answers.
Replacement, flushing and filling/bleeding procedures belong to the repair that the findings justify; they are not extra disassembly for this inspection.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L inspection, cap test, system pressure test and loss-of-coolant diagnostic decisions.
3.7L inspection, cap test, system pressure test and loss-of-coolant diagnostic decisions.
5.0L inspection, cap test, system pressure test and loss-of-coolant diagnostic decisions.
Cold-system opening and pressurized-coolant precautions.
Prevent unintended starts and retain relevant fan, personal-protection and material-handling precautions.
Use observed faults and previous-repair information to guide diagnosis.
2.3L cap handling, cold level and coolant top-up requirements; separate filling/bleeding after repair.
3.7L cap handling, cold level and coolant top-up requirements; separate filling/bleeding after repair.
5.0L cap handling, cold level and coolant top-up requirements; separate filling/bleeding after repair.

stepGroups.title: Establish the cold baseline
stepGroups.summary: Record the concern, inspect leak points and prepare the coolant and sealing surfaces.

stepGroups.title: Test the cap and system
stepGroups.summary: Use the separate adapters and pressure specifications, then release test pressure.

stepGroups.title: Investigate unexplained coolant loss
stepGroups.summary: Check fluid mixing and combustion gases when the external inspection does not explain the loss.

stepGroups.title: Close the system and confirm the result
stepGroups.summary: Seat the cap, retain the findings and verify any subsequent repair.

diagnostics.finding: Cap fails its separate pressure check.
diagnostics.meaning: The cap does not meet the specified holding requirement.
diagnostics.next: Replace the cap, address any bottle sealing defect, and complete the system test independently. [2.3L cap decision](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L cap decision](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L cap decision](#/document/G1694609)

diagnostics.finding: System pressure falls and coolant escapes externally.
diagnostics.meaning: An external leak has been demonstrated.
diagnostics.next: Release pressure, repair the identified source with the appropriate component procedure, then repeat the test and verify normal operation. [2.3L leak decision](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L leak decision](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L leak decision](#/document/G1694609)

diagnostics.finding: System pressure falls without visible external leakage.
diagnostics.meaning: An internal engine leak is possible; the pressure reading does not identify a particular failed part.
diagnostics.next: Complete the coolant and engine-oil inspections. If those are negative, continue to combustion-gas testing. Retain the pressure loss as unresolved until explained. [2.3L internal-leak path](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L internal-leak path](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L internal-leak path](#/document/G1694609)

diagnostics.finding: Engine oil is found in coolant, coolant in engine oil, or combustion gases in coolant.
diagnostics.meaning: The loss-of-coolant path requires engine diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Arrange that diagnosis before selecting a repair; this guide does not establish a gasket or component replacement from these findings alone. [2.3L diagnostic routing](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L diagnostic routing](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L diagnostic routing](#/document/G1694609)

diagnostics.finding: Pressure holds, but the original complaint is overheating or slow warm-up.
diagnostics.meaning: The system passed this static pressure check; temperature-control performance still needs its own diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Use Pinpoint Test B for overheating or C for failure to reach normal temperature in the article for the fitted engine. [2.3L symptom paths](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L symptom paths](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L symptom paths](#/document/G1694609)

verification.title: Separate passing results are recorded
verification.body: The cap meets 145 kPa ± 21 kPa (21 psi ± 3 psi), and the system shows no drop over approximately two minutes after slow pressurization to 124–138 kPa (18–20 psi). Record failures explicitly rather than combining both checks into one pass. [2.3L criteria](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L criteria](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L criteria](#/document/G1694609)

verification.title: The system is closed correctly
verification.body: All testing equipment is removed after pressure release, the dipstick is refitted if inspected, and the degas-bottle cap is seated at its hard stop. Confirm the cold level after any correction. [2.3L completion](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L completion](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L completion](#/document/G1694609)

verification.title: The original concern has a documented disposition
verification.body: Record whether the leak was located, repaired and successfully rechecked, or remains under diagnosis. Verify normal operation after an identified cause is corrected. A test with no reproduced fault is not grounds for replacing parts by assumption. [2.3L verification](#/document/G1673122), [3.7L verification](#/document/G1694576), [5.0L verification](#/document/G1694609), [Diagnostic methods](#/document/G1693185)

guides.title: Battery testing, charging and replacement: diagnose before you buy
guides.summary: Inspect the connections, test with the right equipment, recharge when required, and replace a confirmed faulty battery—including the cable torques and new-battery reset.
guides.introduction: A flat battery tells me what happened, not what caused it. Loose connections, a discharged battery and a faulty battery all belong on the suspect list; buying parts by frustration gets expensive damn quickly. This guide covers testing, charging and justified replacement on the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. [Battery diagnosis](#/document/G1931208)
guides.why: The battery-condition test measures terminal voltage under a controlled discharge current for a specified time. A casual voltage reading does not reproduce that test, and an incompletely charged battery can give a misleading retest result. The vehicle’s charging system maintains charge during normal use; fifteen minutes of idling is not a recovery plan for a deeply discharged battery. Use an external charger, then let the final test result determine the next move. [Battery diagnosis](#/document/G1931208) [Battery charging](#/document/G1692355)

when.summary: When starting becomes weak, a battery is discharged, or a test result calls for charging or replacement.
notes: Use the battery’s condition and diagnostic result; there is no fixed replacement interval in this guide.
Extended storage and repeated short moves with heavy electrical loads can discharge a battery. Fifteen minutes of idling is not an adequate recovery plan for a deeply discharged battery.

prepare.title: Arrange the tester and its instructions
prepare.detail: Use Ford-approved battery test equipment. The charging procedure specifies the GR-1-190 Diagnostic Charger, special tool 162-00036. Have its operating instructions available: they govern the charging operation and equipment settings. [Battery diagnosis](#/document/G1931208) [Battery charging](#/document/G1692355)

prepare.title: Gather tools for access and tightening
prepare.detail: Use tools that match the actual cover retainers, terminal nuts and hold-down bolt, plus a torque wrench capable of accurately applying 44 lb.in (5 Nm) and 71 lb.in (8 Nm). These are inch-pound values. For replacement, arrange a battery carrier or a safe grip at opposite corners and obtain the correct battery for your specific vehicle. [Cable procedure](#/document/G1692356) [Battery replacement](#/document/G1692362) [Battery handling](#/document/G1693181)

prepare.title: Plan the new-battery reset
prepare.detail: If replacement is required, have access to a scan tool with the Battery Monitoring System (BMS) reset function. The reset is performed after the new battery is connected. A scan tool also establishes whether a connected-vehicle battery health report is available; that feature must not be assumed present. [Battery replacement](#/document/G1692362) [Battery diagnosis](#/document/G1931208)

prepare.title: Protect against acid and explosive gas
prepare.detail: Wear eye protection, ventilate the work area, and keep flames, sparks and burning materials away. Battery acid can seriously injure skin and eyes; avoid contact with clothing as well. If acid reaches skin or eyes, flush immediately with water for at least 15 minutes and obtain prompt medical attention. If swallowed, call a physician immediately. Wash your hands after handling posts, terminals or related parts because they contain lead compounds. [Battery precautions](#/document/G1693181)

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start and expose the battery
steps.body: Turn the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. If remote start is fitted, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around the car; an unexpected start can cause serious injury. Remove the three battery-cover retainers shown in the access illustration, then remove the cover. Keep the retainers for reassembly. [Service safety](#/document/G1693189) [Battery access](#/document/G1692356)

steps.title: Inspect the battery and its electrical connections
steps.body: Check the case for damage or leakage, the mounting for looseness, and the wiring, terminals and connectors for visible damage. Inspect the high-current connections at the battery junction box (BJB), together with the battery and chassis ground connections. The battery terminals and grounds must be clean and securely attached. Correct dirty or loose connections and retest before condemning the battery; damaged wiring or connections need their own repair. Do not proceed with routine charging of a visibly damaged or leaking battery. [Inspection and retest](#/document/G1931208) [Acid precautions](#/document/G1693181)

steps.title: Check whether a battery health report is available
steps.body: Use the diagnostic scan tool to establish whether connected-vehicle battery data exists for this car. If it does, review the battery health report. A report calling for replacement of the 12-volt battery directs you to the replacement steps, followed by the excessive-drain check. If the report does not call for replacement and the terminals and grounds pass inspection, Ford’s report-equipped branch proceeds to the drain check. If no report is available, continue with the disconnected battery-condition test below. [Health-report branches](#/document/G1931208)

steps.title: Disconnect negative first, then positive
steps.body: With the ignition off, loosen the negative terminal nut, lift the negative cable connection from its post and position it aside so it cannot reconnect accidentally. Then move the positive terminal cover, loosen the positive terminal nut and position that cable aside too. Removing only the negative cable is sufficient when merely interrupting vehicle power; the battery-condition test specifically requires both battery cables removed. This guide also uses that full disconnection for charging and replacement. If auxiliary batteries are actually fitted, they must also be disconnected to remove vehicle power; leaving them connected can damage the vehicle. [Cable disconnection](#/document/G1692356) [Test isolation](#/document/G1931208) [Charging preparation](#/document/G1692355)

steps.title: Run the battery-condition test
steps.body: With both vehicle cables removed from the battery, use the approved diagnostic battery charger to test its condition according to the equipment instructions. Record the result and any charging direction. The equipment supplies the controlled test conditions; do not substitute an unloaded voltage reading or invent a discharge load and duration. If the analyzer directs charging, continue below. A REPLACE BATTERY or REPLACE-BAD CELL result directs replacement. An OK result proceeds to reconnection and the drain-check branch. [Battery-condition test](#/document/G1931208)

steps.title: Let a cold battery warm before charging
steps.body: For the charging branch, allow a cold battery to reach approximately 5°C (41°F). Warming at room temperature may take four to eight hours. Cold batteries do not readily accept charge, so give this step the time it needs. The charging procedure does not require removing the battery hold-down or lifting the battery out. [Charging preparation](#/document/G1692355)

steps.title: Connect the charger and complete its charging cycle
steps.body: With the vehicle battery cables disconnected, attach the charger’s positive red clamp to the positive battery post first. Attach its negative black clamp to the negative battery post next. Charge using the GR-1-190 Diagnostic Charger and its manufacturer’s operating instructions. Maintain ventilation and keep ignition sources away throughout charging because the battery produces explosive gas. [Charger connections](#/document/G1692355) [Charging hazards](#/document/G1693181)

steps.title: Retest after the battery is fully charged
steps.body: Finish charging before the required retest; an incomplete charge can produce false readings. End the charging operation and handle charger disconnection as directed by its manufacturer. Retest with both vehicle cables still removed and retain the final result. If it passes, keep the battery and proceed to reconnection. If the analyzer reports REPLACE BATTERY or REPLACE-BAD CELL, continue with replacement. [Charging instructions](#/document/G1692355) [Retest and replacement decisions](#/document/G1931208)

steps.title: Remove the battery only on the replacement branch
steps.body: Confirm both battery cables are disconnected. Remove the battery hold-down bolt and clamp, then lift the battery out. Use a battery carrier or support it with your hands at opposite corners. Do not squeeze the plastic case’s end walls: that pressure can force acid through the vents and injure you or damage nearby parts. If a vent tube is attached, disconnect it before lifting and retain it for reconnection. [Battery removal](#/document/G1692362) [Handling and vent precautions](#/document/G1693181)

steps.title: Seat and secure the replacement battery
steps.body: Match the replacement to the actual vehicle application and its component markings or instructions. Lower it into the mounting position using the same carrier or opposite-corner grip. Reinstall the hold-down clamp and bolt, then tighten the bolt to 71 lb.in (8 Nm). Reconnect any vent tube that was disconnected; leaving it detached can allow harmful battery gas into the cabin, with potentially fatal consequences. [Battery installation](#/document/G1692362) [Handling and vent precautions](#/document/G1693181)

steps.title: Reconnect the positive cable first
steps.body: After charging, testing or replacement is finished and the charger is disconnected, refit the positive battery cable connection. Tighten its nut to 44 lb.in (5 Nm), then restore the positive terminal cover. This is the first cable connection when reversing the full disconnection sequence. [Cable reconnection](#/document/G1692356)

steps.title: Reconnect negative and refit the battery cover
steps.body: Refit the negative battery cable connection and tighten its nut to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Reinstall the battery cover and its three retainers. Check that the cables and covers are back in their proper positions and that the battery remains securely mounted. [Cable and cover installation](#/document/G1692356) [Battery mounting](#/document/G1692362)

steps.title: Perform the BMS reset if the battery is new
steps.body: Once the replacement battery is connected, use the scan tool to carry out the Battery Monitoring System reset and confirm that the function completes. This requirement belongs to installing a new battery; recharging and retaining the existing battery does not make it a replacement. Clearing a dashboard message is not the specified scan-tool reset. [New-battery reset](#/document/G1692362)

steps.title: Follow through on the drain-check branch
steps.body: Ford’s diagnostic sequence includes checking for excessive battery drain after an OK condition test or the applicable health-report branch; a health-report-directed replacement also requires that check afterward. With ignition off and the battery cables connected, arrange the separate Battery Drain Check and a review of applicable technical service bulletins or service messages. That check requires a fully charged battery and must not begin while low-battery messages such as deep sleep mode or battery saver active are present. Parasitic drain means electrical current still being consumed while the parked vehicle should be resting. If excessive drain is found, the responsible circuit needs repair; another battery will not resolve that cause. Circuit isolation is a separate diagnostic job. [Diagnostic completion](#/document/G1931208) [Drain-check preparation](#/document/G1692357)

steps.title: Check starting and account for adaptive relearning
steps.body: After confirming that tools and charging equipment are clear, check whether the original weak-starting concern has been resolved. Battery disconnection can temporarily change driving behavior while the powertrain control module relearns its adaptive values, and driving may be needed for that relearning. Do not use that note to dismiss a continuing starting fault; return to the recorded test and connection findings if the original problem remains. [Adaptive relearning](#/document/G1692356) [Diagnostic findings](#/document/G1931208)

steps.title: Prepare window initialization only when needed
steps.body: Check window operation after power is restored. If one-touch initialization is required, use this branch; convertible models do not have one-touch up or bounce-back features. For an existing window motor, Ford first requires de-initializing it by disconnecting the battery cable or window-motor fuse while the window is operating, then reconnecting that cable or fuse before initialization. If using the battery-cable method, interrupt power at the negative cable only and reconnect it to 44 lb.in (5 Nm) afterward. Keep hands, body parts and objects out of the glass path throughout this work: during initialization the window closes with high force and cannot detect an obstruction. [Window preparation and warning](#/document/G1957566) [Negative-cable procedure](#/document/G1692356)

steps.title: Initialize the applicable one-touch window
steps.body: Close the door and start with the window fully open. Hold the window switch UP at its second detent—the second switch position—until the glass reaches the top run, then continue holding for at least two seconds after it stalls there. Release the switch. Hold DOWN at the second detent until the glass reaches the bottom, continuing for at least two seconds after it stalls. Cycle the glass up and down once more to establish the lower soft stop, then test one-touch up and one-touch down. Keep the glass path completely clear; obstruction detection is unavailable during initialization. [Window initialization](#/document/G1957566)

steps.title: Close out the job with results
steps.body: Confirm the battery is secure, both cable connections and the positive terminal cover are restored, the outer cover and retainers are fitted, and any battery vent tube is connected. Record the final analyzer result, whether the battery was charged or replaced, the BMS reset completion if applicable, and the outcome or outstanding status of the drain check. Recheck the original starting concern and any applicable one-touch window operation before calling the diagnosis finished. [Mounting and reset](#/document/G1692362) [Cable assembly](#/document/G1692356) [Vent connection](#/document/G1693181) [Diagnostic completion](#/document/G1931208) [Window check](#/document/G1957566)

watchFor.title: The battery goes flat again
watchFor.body: Repeated discharge after a completed charge or replacement warrants the drain-check branch. Do not keep buying batteries without checking what is consuming power. [Drain diagnosis](#/document/G1931208)

watchFor.title: A damaged or leaking case
watchFor.body: Stop routine charging and handling. Avoid acid contact and arrange safe handling of the damaged battery; eye or skin exposure requires immediate flushing for at least 15 minutes and prompt medical attention. [Battery precautions](#/document/G1693181)

watchFor.title: A low-charge result changes after charging
watchFor.body: Use the completed, fully charged retest to make the condition decision. The preliminary reading and final result are not interchangeable. [Retest requirement](#/document/G1931208)

watchFor.title: A window needs initialization
watchFor.body: Keep every obstruction clear. Initialization uses high closing force without obstruction detection, so testing bounce-back with a hand or object is dangerous. [Window safety](#/document/G1957566)

notes: Scope remains the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine; connected-vehicle reports and auxiliary batteries are conditional equipment, not assumed features.

Extended parking and repeated short moves with heavy electrical loads can discharge a battery. Use an external charger for recovery rather than relying on a brief idle. [Charging guidance](#/document/G1692355)

The charging and test equipment’s instructions govern its operation. No substitute charging rate, test load, test duration or voltage cutoff is invented here. [Charging procedure](#/document/G1692355) [Battery test](#/document/G1931208)
I would keep the before-and-after results together—parts-guessing is a pain in the ass, and a useful record beats another guess.

procedures.purpose: Inspect connections, select the available diagnostic branch and interpret battery-condition results.
Prepare a cold battery, connect the specified diagnostic charger and complete charging.
Remove and refit the battery cover and disconnect and reconnect cables with the correct sequence and torques.
Remove and install the battery, tighten the hold-down and perform the new-battery BMS reset.
Apply acid, explosive-gas, lifting, lead and vent-tube precautions.
Prevent an unexpected start during battery service.
Establish readiness for the separate excessive-drain diagnostic job.
Restore applicable one-touch window operation when initialization is required.

stepGroups.title: Expose the battery and choose the diagnostic branch
stepGroups.summary: Prevent an unexpected start, inspect the connections and check for available battery health data.

stepGroups.title: Disconnect and test
stepGroups.summary: Remove both vehicle cables and obtain a controlled battery-condition result.

stepGroups.title: Charge when directed
stepGroups.summary: Warm a cold battery, complete charging and obtain the final condition result.

stepGroups.title: Replace only when justified
stepGroups.summary: Lift safely, secure the replacement and restore any vent connection.

stepGroups.title: Restore power and reset a new battery
stepGroups.summary: Reconnect positive before negative, refit the cover and perform the applicable BMS reset.

stepGroups.title: Check the cause and the original symptom
stepGroups.summary: Follow the drain-check branch and account for adaptive relearning.

stepGroups.title: Restore applicable window functions and finish
stepGroups.summary: Initialize one-touch windows when needed and document the completed checks.

diagnostics.finding: Battery terminals or chassis grounds are dirty or loose.
diagnostics.meaning: The electrical connections have not passed the preliminary inspection.
diagnostics.next: Correct the connection condition and retest the battery before making a replacement decision. [Connection diagnosis](#/document/G1931208)

diagnostics.finding: The connected-vehicle health report explicitly requests replacement.
diagnostics.meaning: Ford’s available-report branch directs installation of a new 12-volt battery.
diagnostics.next: Replace it, perform the BMS reset after connection, and complete the excessive-drain check. [Health-report decision](#/document/G1931208) [BMS reset](#/document/G1692362)

diagnostics.finding: The analyzer directs charging or a charged retest.
diagnostics.meaning: A final condition decision requires completing the charging instruction.
diagnostics.next: Charge fully and retest with the vehicle cables removed. Incomplete charging can produce false readings. [Retest requirement](#/document/G1931208)

diagnostics.finding: The analyzer reports REPLACE BATTERY or REPLACE-BAD CELL.
diagnostics.meaning: The diagnostic procedure directs battery replacement.
diagnostics.next: Use the replacement steps, reconnect at the specified torques and complete the new-battery BMS reset. [Replacement decision](#/document/G1931208) [Replacement procedure](#/document/G1692362)

diagnostics.finding: The battery passes its condition test.
diagnostics.meaning: The diagnostic sequence proceeds to checking for excessive drain; an OK battery result does not complete that branch.
diagnostics.next: Reconnect the battery and arrange the separate drain check with the battery fully charged. Repair an excessive draw if found. [Diagnostic sequence](#/document/G1931208) [Drain-check readiness](#/document/G1692357)

verification.title: Mechanical and electrical assembly is restored
verification.body: For replacement, confirm the hold-down bolt was tightened to 71 lb.in (8 Nm). Confirm both terminal nuts were tightened to 44 lb.in (5 Nm), positive was connected before negative, and the terminal cover, battery cover and retainers are fitted. Reconnect any disturbed vent tube. [Battery mounting](#/document/G1692362) [Cable torques and sequence](#/document/G1692356) [Vent safety](#/document/G1693181)

verification.title: The test result supports the action taken
verification.body: Keep the final condition result, charging outcome and replacement decision together. Do not treat an incompletely charged retest as conclusive. [Battery diagnosis](#/document/G1931208)

verification.title: Replacement includes the reset
verification.body: Confirm successful completion of the scan-tool BMS reset after connecting a new battery. [Reset requirement](#/document/G1692362)

verification.title: The original concern and follow-up are checked
verification.body: Confirm whether starting has improved and record the drain-check outcome or remaining diagnostic work. Where window initialization was needed, verify one-touch up and down afterward. [Diagnostic completion](#/document/G1931208) [Window verification](#/document/G1957566)

guides.title: Wheel alignment: turn tire wear into a useful measurement
guides.summary: Understand toe and camber, check what can upset the readings, and plan an alignment that fixes the cause of uneven wear.

applicability.equipment: Factory suspension geometry; modified suspension needs its own applicable specifications.

guides.introduction: Alignment describes where the wheels point and how they lean. Toe is the direction a wheel points when viewed from above; camber is its inward or outward lean when viewed from the front or rear. A small error can make a tire scrub across the road instead of rolling cleanly. Getting the angles right starts with healthy tires and suspension, not immediately turning an adjustment bolt.
guides.why: An alignment check can help explain a crooked steering wheel, uneven tire wear or a pull. Those symptoms can also come from tire pressure, tire forces, brake drag or loose suspension parts. Measuring after those basic checks prevents an adjustment from hiding another problem.

when.summary: Check when tire wear, pulling or an off-center steering wheel points to an alignment concern.
notes: This is a condition-based check, with no fixed alignment mileage added here.
Use the final alignment checks required by the relevant suspension or steering repair. Lowered or otherwise modified cars need specifications appropriate to that configuration.

prepare.title: Collect the clues
