| Cooling vacuum filler, suitable coolant collection equipment and refractometer | Refill without leaving air pockets; verify concentration. |
| Capable diagnostic scan tool | Record faults, monitor temperature and perform the required Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction. |
| Plastic scraper, lint-free towels, labeled trays, bags and a clean protected bench | Keep debris out and each tappet/cap in its original position. |

These are planning requirements, not a claim that every generic tool kit fits. Check the full linked subprocedures for conditional seal tools before ordering.

Also prepare the **303-1419 stretchy-belt tool**, a hose-clamp tool, a fluid suction gun, suitable hose-isolation tools and clean compressed air for the coil wells. If valve-cover tube/VCT seals are damaged, their replacement tools are **303-1247, 205-142 and 205-153**. Keep a minimum **3 mm** wide cable tie available for the specified A/C-belt installation method. See the belt, valve-cover and degas-bottle references in the steps below.

prepare.title: Build the replacement-parts pile before disassembly
prepare.detail:
| Part or material | Replacement rule |
| --- | --- |
| Correct bank-specific head gasket and cylinder-head bolts | New gasket and new main bolts; Ford prohibits reusing the head bolts. |
| Small M6 cylinder-head bolt | Discard and replace. It is separate from the eight main bolts. |
| VCT-unit bolts and crankshaft-pulley bolt | New where removed by the required timing/front-seal work. |
| Catalytic-converter flange nuts on the disturbed bank | Discard the old nuts; install new ones. |
| Upper-intake, lower-intake and both valve-cover gaskets | Replace the gaskets removed by those procedures; none of these is the head gasket. |
| Crankshaft front seal; coolant-pump gasket and O-ring; thermostat-housing O-ring; front-cover coolant-pipe seal | Include the seals disturbed by the access route. Follow each component’s replacement instructions. |
| Secondary timing-chain tensioner | New if the cylinder head is replaced; also do not reuse a secondary tensioner that has itself been removed. |
| Oil filter, specified engine oil and coolant | Renew the oil/filter after the repair; refill and bleed the cooling system correctly. |
| Motorcraft TA-357 RTV, WSE-M4G323-A6, or a currently approved exact replacement | For the front-cover joint specified by Ford, not an extra coating for the head gasket. |

Match parts to VIN and bank. Check the other seals and the A/C belt against their own removal instructions. A gasket set’s contents are a packing list, not permission to reuse something missing from the box.

Inspect coil boots and valve-cover spark-plug-tube/VCT seals. Replace damaged boots/seals; the source does not require replacing every undamaged tube seal. Have enough clean, specified coolant for the refill, without treating the published dry system capacity as a forced refill amount.

prepare.title: Set up a cold, clean, organized workspace
prepare.detail: Let the engine cool fully before opening the cooling system. Use eye protection, keep ignition sources away from fuel, collect fluids safely and follow the hoist instructions. Photograph connections; label fasteners by component and length. Make a tappet/cam-cap tray for the original positions. I like paperwork here: “this bolt probably went somewhere important” is not a filing system.

steps.title: Confirm the leak and identify the bank
steps.body: Record the symptoms, trouble codes, temperature history and fluid condition. Inspect for external coolant leaks and cooling-system faults. Use the [cooling pressure-test guide](#/maintenance/cooling-pressure-leak-test) and the [cylinder leak-down guide](#/maintenance/engine-cylinder-leakdown) as applicable. Ford’s [engine diagnosis](#/document/G1804267) distinguishes leakage past valves/rings, between cylinders and into the cooling circuit. Bubbles during a correctly set up leak-down test can also indicate a casting crack. Confirm the path rather than declaring the gasket guilty from a single symptom. The catalog’s separate cranking-compression guide does not cover a 3.7L test branch, so do not borrow its other-engine setup.

steps.title: Cool the engine, release fuel pressure and disconnect the battery
steps.body:
Let the engine cool fully. Record faults and symptoms first. If it is safe to run, release fuel pressure by disconnecting the fuel-pump driver module beneath the left rear seat cushion, letting the engine idle until it stops, then switching the ignition off. Disconnect the battery ground through the battery procedure. Put the vehicle in Neutral and support it on a suitable hoist at the approved lifting points.

**If coolant may be inside a cylinder, or running would cause overheating or damage, do not run or crank it to carry out the normal pressure-release routine. Obtain the approved non-running method instead.** Do not improvise by cracking a pressurized fuel line. References: [fuel pressure release](#/document/G1702143), [battery isolation](#/document/G1692356), [lifting](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Drain coolant and disconnect the affected exhaust flange
steps.body:
1. With the engine cold, cover the expansion-tank cap with a thick cloth and remove it carefully. Never open a hot pressurized cooling system.
2. Remove the fitted underbody shield, or the subframe-bracket/shield assembly. Keep the different bolts identified. Ford shows two equipment branches; remove the one your car actually has.
3. Put a suitable container under the radiator drain, attach a drain hose and open the valve. Keep contaminated coolant separate for proper disposal. A partly drained engine still holds coolant.
4. On the bank being repaired, unplug the heated oxygen-sensor and catalyst-monitor-sensor connectors. Support the exhaust connection as needed. Remove and discard that catalytic-converter flange’s nuts; clean the mating surfaces without straining sensor wiring.

References: [coolant draining](#/document/G1694549), [front-cover access/shield branches](#/document/G1681517), [LH head](#/document/G1681515), [RH head](#/document/G1681516).

steps.title: Remove the air-cleaner outlet pipe
steps.body:
This is the large air duct between the air-cleaner assembly and throttle body—not a cylinder-head component.

1. Disconnect and move aside the brake-booster tube and crankcase-ventilation tube attached to this area.
2. Loosen the duct’s two clamps and lift the outlet pipe away.
3. Label the disconnected tubes and protect open air passages from debris.

The two clamp screws use **5.4 Nm / 48 lb-in** when the duct goes back. Reference: [air-cleaner outlet pipe](#/document/G1675695).

steps.title: Remove the upper intake manifold
steps.body:
The upper manifold sits above the engine and distributes intake air. It must come off to reach the RH ignition coils as well as to complete the lower-manifold work.

1. Release the vacuum hose from the upper manifold with the appropriate clamp tool. Detach its retainers from the throttle body and manifold.
2. Unplug the EVAP purge valve, free the harness retainers, and disconnect the purge quick-release coupling using its correct release method.
3. Disconnect the PCV tube and move it aside. Unplug the throttle-body and MAP-sensor connectors and release their wiring retainers.
4. Remove the upper-manifold support bolt, then its mounting bolts. Lift the manifold off without trapping a hose or wiring underneath it.
5. Remove and discard the upper-manifold gaskets. Protect the now-open lower-manifold passages. If the failure involved valve/piston damage, inspect for metal debris; Ford requires a replacement manifold if that debris is found.

**What is exposed now:** the lower intake assembly and access to the RH coils. You have not exposed the head gasket. References: [upper manifold](#/document/G1681529), [fuel/EVAP coupling method](#/document/G1671536), [coil access](#/document/G1675558).

steps.title: Remove the ignition coils on both banks
steps.body:
Before pulling a coil, clear loose dirt from the coil and surrounding well with compressed air, using eye protection and controlling where debris goes. Unplug each coil connector, remove its mounting bolt, and gently twist the coil to release the boot before lifting it out. Label the coils and inspect their boots for cracks, tears or rips.

Both sets come out because both valve covers must come off for front-cover access. The RH coils are accessible after the upper manifold has been removed. This step removes the coils; it is not an instruction to remove the spark plugs. Reference: [3.7L ignition coils](#/document/G1675558).

steps.title: Remove the left valve cover and its gasket
steps.body:
1. Remove the crankcase vent tube and oil-level indicator/dipstick. Detach the fuel-supply/EVAP tube retainer from the cover.
2. With the coils already out, unplug the oil-pressure switch and free the associated harness retainers.
3. Unplug the VCT oil-control solenoids and release the harness retainers attached to the cover.
4. Loosen the cover bolts and lift the cover carefully. If a VCT seal grips a solenoid, wiggle the cover gently until it releases. Do not lever or pull hard against a solenoid.
5. Remove and discard the **valve-cover gasket** from the cover. Inspect the VCT seals and spark-plug-tube seals; remove them with the specified tools only if damaged and being replaced.

**What you see now:** camshafts and valve gear inside the cylinder head. The head gasket is still below the whole head, not around this opening. Reference: [LH valve cover](#/document/G1681530).

steps.title: Remove the right valve cover and its gasket
steps.body:
1. With the RH coils already out, disconnect the PCV tube from this side.
2. Unplug the VCT oil-control solenoids and release the wiring-harness retainers.
3. Remove the heater-tube bolt and release the heater-tube retainer from the valve-cover stud bolt.
4. Loosen the valve-cover bolts and lift the cover without loading the VCT solenoids. Gently free any sticking seal rather than forcing it.
5. Discard the RH valve-cover gasket. Inspect its VCT and spark-plug-tube seals; replace damaged seals using the specified tools.

The RH and LH cover gaskets are separate from the head gaskets. Keep the covers, bolts and bank-specific attachments identified. Reference: [RH valve cover](#/document/G1681531).

steps.title: Clear the coolant bottle and drive belts
steps.body:
The front cover cannot simply be lifted off while the pulley and front accessories are in its way.

1. Remove the degas/expansion bottle for crank-pulley access. With it cold and depressurized, isolate its lower hose as specified, use a suction gun to remove remaining coolant, release the upper hose clamps, remove the mounting bolts, and move it enough to disconnect the lower hose. Collect spills.
2. Before taking off the accessory belt, loosen the coolant-pump pulley bolts while the belt can restrain the pulley. They are removed later with the pump.
3. Rotate the accessory-belt tensioner **counterclockwise**, slip the belt off, and release the tensioner under control. Record the routing; keep all belts, pulleys and tensioner surfaces free of lubricant or belt dressing.
4. For the separate stretchy A/C belt, use **303-1419**. Ford’s removal sequence rotates the crank pulley clockwise to feed the tool approximately **180°** onto the compressor pulley, folds the tool underneath the inside of the belt as illustrated, then pulls the tool firmly to remove the belt. Follow that tool-placement drawing; do not substitute a screwdriver or an assumed tensioner.

References: [accessory belt](#/document/G1688121), [A/C belt and tool placement](#/document/G1688123), [degas bottle](#/document/G1694561), [pump pulley preparation](#/document/G1694559).

steps.title: Remove the crankshaft pulley and front seal
steps.body:
Remove the crankshaft-pulley bolt and washer; discard the bolt. Use the specified three-leg puller to remove the pulley. Use **303-409** to remove the crankshaft front seal, and discard the seal. Keep the sealing surfaces and exposed crankshaft area protected and clean.

This removes a front-of-engine oil seal. It is another seal being disturbed for access, not the head gasket. The new seal and pulley will be installed after the front cover is back in place. Reference: [crankshaft front seal/pulley](#/document/G1681513).

steps.title: Remove the thermostat housing and coolant pump
steps.body:
1. Keep remaining belts protected with waterproof plastic against coolant spills. Release the thermostat-housing hose clamps and disconnect the hoses.
2. Remove the housing bolts and the housing. Remove its O-ring. The source has an inconsistent inspection note, but its installation branch explicitly calls for a **new O-ring**; plan on replacing it.
3. Remove the previously loosened coolant-pump pulley bolts and pulley.
4. Remove the pump bolts and lift the pump out. Discard its gasket and O-ring. Keep residual coolant out of other exposed openings.

You only drain the system once for this combined job; repeated drain instructions in the linked standalone procedures do not mean refilling between parts. References: [thermostat housing](#/document/G1694563), [coolant pump](#/document/G1694559).

steps.title: Move the belt tensioner, generator and support bracket
steps.body:
Remove the accessory-drive-belt tensioner mounting bolts and tensioner. Remove the specified generator nut and bolt, then position the generator aside. Avoid loading its wiring; the front-cover procedure calls for positioning it aside, not inventing extra electrical disconnections. Remove the stud bolt and the upper-intake-manifold support-bracket bolt, then remove the bracket.

Bag these fasteners separately from the head bolts. **The front cover is now accessible after both valve covers, the pulley, pump and these obstructions are cleared.** Reference: [front cover removal, accessory/bracket steps](#/document/G1681517).

steps.title: Remove the engine front cover
steps.body:
Remove the front-cover bolts, recording their positions and lengths. Use only the designated pry pads in Ford’s illustration to release the cover; do not drive a tool between sealing faces. Lift the cover away and remove its coolant-pipe seal with **205-150 and 205-153**.

Clean the cover’s RTV joints using the specified preparation method and wash away all remaining contamination. Keep debris out of the open engine. This RTV-joint preparation does not authorize abrasive cleaning of the head-gasket faces later.

**What you see now:** the timing-chain drive at the front of the engine. The head is still attached to that drive and to the block. References: [front cover, pry pads and coolant-pipe seal](#/document/G1681517), [RTV preparation](#/document/G1692003).

steps.title: Set the timing reference and remove the primary timing chain
steps.body:
1. Rotate the crankshaft **clockwise only at this alignment step** until the intake-VCT timing marks match Ford’s diagram. Do not spin the crank freely after the chain is removed.
2. Remove the LH oil tube and install **303-1248** to hold the LH camshafts at TDC. Remove the RH oil tube and install its holding tools too.
3. If the chain’s colored links are no longer visible, mark the links at the LH and RH intake-VCT marks, and the two links bracketing the crankshaft-sprocket mark. Use the diagram’s exact locations.
4. Remove the primary tensioner, then the tensioner arm, then the lower LH chain guide.
5. Remove the VCT oil-control-solenoid bolts and solenoids as directed to provide chain clearance. A slight twist can free a solenoid; keep it completely clean.
6. Remove the primary chain. Keep its identity and marks intact.

**Checkpoint:** both banks are held in the specified timing position; the primary chain is off. The affected head’s smaller secondary-chain/VCT assembly still has to come off. Reference: [primary timing chain](#/document/G1681528).

steps.title: Remove the affected bank’s VCT units and secondary-chain assembly
steps.body:
VCT means variable camshaft timing; these units sit on the ends of the camshafts. Work on the bank being repaired.

Compress that bank’s secondary-chain tensioner and insert **303-1530** into the hole at the rear of its guide so it bears against the mega cap and holds the tensioner collapsed. Remove and discard that bank’s VCT-unit bolts, then remove the VCT units/secondary-chain assembly as illustrated.

**If the secondary tensioner itself must be removed:** remove the hold-down tool, remove the exhaust VCT solenoid and its bolt, lift out the tensioner shoe, then push the tensioner upward from below to remove it. A removed secondary tensioner cannot be reused. A replacement cylinder head also requires a new secondary tensioner. Replacing only the gasket does not automatically mean replacing a tensioner that remained installed and serviceable.

Reference: [VCT removal, matching LH/RH branch](#/document/G1681532).

steps.title: Remove the camshafts from the head being lifted
steps.body:
Remove the **303-1530** hold-down and **303-1248** cam-holding tools at the point specified in the camshaft removal branch. Identify the intake and exhaust camshafts and retain every numbered bearing cap in its original location and orientation. Remove the cap bolts, caps and camshafts using that bank’s illustrated layout. Keep each cap with its own head; they are not interchangeable spare brackets.

**What you see now:** the tappets/valve gear in the head with the camshafts removed. The head remains bolted to the block; you still have the lower intake and bank-specific attachments to release. Reference: [camshafts, LH/RH removal](#/document/G1681512).

steps.title: Remove the lower intake manifold
steps.body:
The upper manifold is already off and the fuel system is already depressurized.

1. Disconnect the fuel supply quick-release coupling using its correct method. Cap/protect the open connections.
2. Remove the fuel-rail sound insulators. The thermostat housing has already been removed for front-cover/pump access.
3. Unplug the fuel injectors and disconnect the coolant tube at the rear of the lower manifold.
4. Remove the lower-manifold bolts and lift the assembly off. Ford specifically says the fuel rail does **not** have to be removed from this assembly.
5. Discard the lower-intake gaskets. Protect the open intake ports and inspect/clean the sealing faces. If metal debris from upper-engine damage is found in the manifold, replace the manifold as Ford requires.

**Checkpoint:** the upper and lower intake assemblies are clear. Neither of their gaskets was the head gasket. References: [lower intake](#/document/G1681524), [fuel coupling](#/document/G1671536).

steps.title: Release the last head attachments and remove the tappets
steps.body:
| LH head | RH head |
| --- | --- |
| Remove the ground-strap nut/strap. Disconnect CMP sensor connectors and release the head’s harness retainer. | Disconnect the RH CMP connectors; disconnect the CHT temperature-sensor connector at the specified point. |
| Remove the CMP sensors and upper LH chain guide. | Remove the CMP sensors and upper RH chain guide. |

Use **hand tools** on the upper-chain-guide bolt; power tools can damage the guide. Label every valve tappet by its exact original valve position, remove it and inspect it. Remove and discard the small **M6 head bolt**, keeping it distinct from the eight main head bolts.

Check the head against its illustration before lifting: no attached hose, wire, intake assembly, chain or exhaust connection should be asked to hold its weight. References: [LH head removal](#/document/G1681515), [RH head removal](#/document/G1681516).

steps.title: Unbolt and lift the cylinder head: this exposes the head gasket
steps.body:
**This is the point where you physically get to the head gasket.** Everything above and in front was access work.

1. Protect the exposed engine cavities with clean lint-free towels, without trapping a towel under the head or leaving material where a fastener must be accessed.
2. Remove and discard the **eight main cylinder-head bolts** using the selected bank’s removal illustration. The colored order explorer later in this section is for installation, not an invented loosening sequence.
3. Lift the cylinder head with controlled assistance. Do not pry against the gasket face, hang the head on a remaining attachment or set the bare gasket face down on an unprotected bench.
4. With the head off, the thin old gasket is exposed at the head-to-block joint. Note the failed area and fluid tracks, then lift off and discard the gasket. If material adheres, remove it with the permitted plastic-scraper method in the next step.
5. Keep the block’s cylinder bores and oil/coolant openings protected. Store the head with its gasket side upward for inspection.

References: [LH head removal](#/document/G1681515), [RH head removal](#/document/G1681516).

steps.title: Clean the head and block gasket faces
steps.body:
For the **head-gasket faces**, Ford explicitly prohibits metal scrapers, wire brushes, powered abrasive discs and other abrasive cleaning. Use a plastic scraper and controlled cleanup; keep debris away from oil passages, coolant passages and cylinders. Remove the protective towels without dropping their contents into the engine. The separate [RTV cleaning article](#/document/G1692003) concerns RTV joints: do not use it to override these head-face restrictions. Flat does not mean shiny, and shiny does not mean flat.

Before assembly, account for every towel and cleaning tool. Confirm no old gasket material remains on either mating face or locating dowel, and no debris has fallen into a passage. Do not scrape across the face with a razor or metal blade.

steps.title: Inspect both castings and decide whether they can be reused
steps.body: Support the head with the gasket face upward. Check it with the calibrated straightedge and feeler-gauge pattern in [head distortion](#/document/G1661748); check the block using [block distortion](#/document/G1661746). The [3.7L specification table](#/document/G1681493) gives head-face flatness as 0.08 mm (0.003 in) end to end, with a 150 × 150 mm area—or full width—less than 0.05 mm (0.002 in). A machine shop should assess cracks, surface finish and repairability after an overheating failure; do not assume milling is automatically permissible. **The catalog’s block-flatness row contains inconsistent metric/imperial pairs. I have not turned those into an acceptance limit here. Verify the current Ford block specification before approving the deck.** Fel-Pro’s [surface-finish explanation](https://www.felpro.com/technical/tecblogs/surface-finish.html) is useful background; its generic examples are not substitute Mustang tolerances.

steps.title: Place the new head gasket and lower the head onto it
steps.body:
1. Identify the correct **bank-specific head gasket** using the VIN/part information. Compare its locating holes and oil/coolant passages with the correct Ford installation illustration. Do not assume that flipping a gasket makes it fit the opposite bank.
2. Ensure the locating dowels and mating faces are clean and sound. Position the **new gasket on the head-to-block joint**, correctly located on the dowels as illustrated.
3. Do not add RTV or copper spray to the head gasket. The source specifies RTV at other joints; that does not make it a head-gasket coating.
4. Lower the cylinder head squarely onto the located gasket without dragging it across the sealing faces. Stop and correct any misalignment before clamping it down.
5. Fit the correct **new main head bolts**. The supplied head instructions do not specify an extra thread-lubricant rule; do not invent one or mix a stud-kit method with the Ford bolt procedure.

**What changed:** the old head gasket has been removed and a new one is now sandwiched between the head and block. It is not fully clamped until the next step is completed. References: [LH installation steps 1–2](#/document/G1681515), [RH installation steps 1–2](#/document/G1681516).

steps.title: Clamp the new gasket with the five head-bolt passes
steps.body:
Use the bank-specific bolt map in the visual guide. Work through **bolts 1 → 8 for each stage**, then return to bolt 1 for the next stage. Do not finish all five stages on one bolt before moving to the next.

| Pass | Specification | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 20 Nm / 177 lb-in | Seat all eight in the illustrated order. |
| 2 | 35 Nm / 26 lb-ft | Complete the second torque pass on all eight. |
| 3 | Additional 90° | Measure a quarter-turn on each bolt in order. |
| 4 | Additional 90° | Make another separate quarter-turn pass. |
| 5 | Additional 45° | Finish with a separate eighth-turn pass. |

Use a proper angle gauge. **lb-in and lb-ft are different units.** The angle stages are not substitute torque values and the 90° passes must not be merged. These values are for the original-style new bolts in [LH](#/document/G1681515)/[RH](#/document/G1681516) installation step 2; an aftermarket stud kit needs its own approved installation method. Do not loosen or retorque the completed head just to double-check it.

steps.title: Refit the small head bolt, tappets, guide and sensors
steps.body: Install the **new M6 bolt at 10 Nm / 89 lb-in** after the main bolts. Return oil-lubricated tappets to their original locations. Reconnect the RH CHT sensor where applicable. Refit the upper timing-chain guide with hand tools and tighten its bolt to **10 Nm / 89 lb-in**. Lubricate CMP sensor O-rings with clean specified engine oil; install the sensors at **10 Nm / 89 lb-in** and reconnect them. Restore the LH harness retainer and ground strap; the LH strap nut is **9 Nm / 80 lb-in**. References: the installation branches in [LH](#/document/G1681515) and [RH](#/document/G1681516).

steps.title: Refit the lower intake manifold and its connections
steps.body:
Install new lower-intake gaskets, set the manifold in position and tighten its bolts to **10 Nm / 89 lb-in** using the installation illustration. Reconnect the rear coolant tube and injector connectors. Restore the fuel-rail sound insulators and fuel quick-release coupling, checking that the connection is secure.

The standalone lower-manifold procedure also reinstalls the thermostat housing, upper manifold, battery and fluids. In this combined repair, finish the thermostat with the pump/front-cover work, and leave the upper manifold off until the RH valve cover and coils are back. Keep the battery disconnected and the engine unstarted until timing, covers and fluids are complete. This avoids closing off your own access or starting a partly assembled engine. Reference: [lower-intake installation](#/document/G1681524).

steps.title: Install the camshafts and bearing caps
steps.body:
1. Before positioning the cams, follow Ford’s instructed **counterclockwise** crankshaft movement to the freewheeling position: crankshaft dowel at **9 o’clock**. Keep the crank there through camshaft installation and clearance checks. This controlled movement is a different step from the earlier clockwise-only chain-alignment operation.
2. Lubricate the camshafts with clean specified engine oil. Install the correct intake and exhaust cams in the **neutral position shown for that bank**.
3. Position each camshaft-seal gap at **12 o’clock**. Install the original-position bearing caps and oil tube.
4. Follow the bank-specific cap-bolt diagram: first **8 Nm / 71 lb-in, then 45°**; loosen the cap bolts as directed; then perform the final **8 Nm / 71 lb-in, then 45°** sequence. Do not omit the deliberate loosen-and-retighten cycle or guess the order from a different bank.

Keep the crank at the 9 o’clock freewheeling position until the next clearance check is finished. Reference: [camshafts, LH/RH installation and cap maps](#/document/G1681512).

steps.title: Check valve clearances before restoring timing
steps.body:
With the engine at room temperature, measure each valve’s clearance with the cam on its base circle—the round heel of the cam lobe, where it is not pressing the valve open. Record the valve location and reading.

| Valve | Ford cold-clearance range |
| --- | --- |
| Intake | 0.15–0.25 mm / 0.0059–0.0098 in |
| Exhaust | 0.36–0.46 mm / 0.0142–0.0181 in |

For this **untimed reassembly**, obey the camshaft procedure: the crank stays in the 9 o’clock freewheeling position and a cam sprocket bolt is used to turn the camshafts for the check. Do not import the standalone clearance page’s crankshaft-rotation instruction into an engine whose timing is disconnected.

If a reading is outside specification, select the appropriate replacement tappet and repeat the camshaft removal/refit and measurement. In consistent units, the selection calculation is **new tappet thickness = measured clearance + existing tappet thickness − desired clearance**. Ford prefers a midrange clearance; the tappet’s marking identifies its thickness (for example, 3.310 means 3.31 mm). Preserve every valve’s location. New components make this check/adjustment mandatory.

After the clearances are correct, remove the oil tube again, rotate the bank’s cams to the illustrated TDC position and install **303-1248** and **303-1530** as specified. Only then perform the instructed **60° clockwise** crank move to the dowel-at-**11 o’clock** TDC position. References: [camshaft reassembly](#/document/G1681512), [valve clearance](#/document/G1681500).

steps.title: Refit the secondary-chain/VCT assembly
steps.body:
**If the existing secondary tensioner remained installed:** align the secondary-chain colored links with the matching VCT marks. Fit the units onto the camshafts with their holes aligned to the cam dowels. Use **new VCT bolts** and tighten in four stages: **40 Nm / 30 lb-ft → loosen one full turn → 25 Nm / 18 lb-ft → 180°**. Ensure the secondary chain is centered on its tensioner guides, then remove the 303-1530 hold-down at the instructed point.

**If installing a replacement secondary tensioner:** follow this additional branch before completing the normal assembly:

1. Oil the new tensioner’s O-rings and the mega-cap bore with clean specified engine oil. Leave the shipping clip fitted initially.
2. Push the tensioner fully down into its bore until it snaps into its seated position. Fit the tensioner shoe; only then remove and discard the shipping clip.
3. Align the secondary chain and VCT marks, fit the units to the cam dowels, and install their new bolts using the four stages above.
4. Press down on the chain and top shoe until the tensioner bottoms; release it so the tensioner springs up and applies chain tension.
5. Refit the removed exhaust VCT solenoid cleanly without forcing it into the mega cap; inspect for burrs/contamination if it will not seat. The RH replacement branch states **8 Nm / 71 lb-in + 20°**; the general timing-chain solenoid installation gives the same stages. The LH replacement paragraph omits a torque entry, so verify that solenoid against the general installation instruction rather than treating the omission as a different value.
6. Follow the manual’s transition through its hold-down and VCT-installation checks; do not remove and reinstall a newly seated tensioner as a rehearsal.

Use the **LH or RH illustrations for your bank** and finish with the secondary chain centered and hold-down released as directed. References: [VCT installation and new-tensioner branches](#/document/G1681532), [general solenoid installation](#/document/G1681528).

steps.title: Install the primary chain and verify all timing references
steps.body:
1. Align the colored links with both intake-VCT marks and the crankshaft-sprocket mark. The crank mark sits **between the two marked crank links**. Use the source illustration for the counting convention and positions.
2. Refit the lower LH guide at **10 Nm / 89 lb-in**, then the tensioner arm.
3. Reset the primary tensioner by releasing its ratchet detent, compressing the plunger in a soft-jawed vise, aligning the plunger/housing holes and installing a lockpin.
4. Install the tensioner at **10 Nm / 89 lb-in** and remove its lockpin. Use only the slight cam movement the procedure permits to remove slack.
5. Check the installed marks. Ford specifies **48 links between the RH and LH intake marked links**, and **35 links between the LH intake marked link and the pair at the crank**. Resolve a mismatch before closing the engine.
6. Refit the clean VCT oil-control solenoids with a slight twist if needed, never by force: **8 Nm / 71 lb-in + 20°**. Forcing them can damage the mega cap and render the head unusable.
7. Remove the holding tools and reinstall the RH/LH oil tubes at the specified points: **8 Nm / 71 lb-in + 45°**.

**Checkpoint:** timing marks, marked links, tensioners and tool removal all agree. Do not use the starter motor to “see whether it is close enough.” Reference: [timing-chain installation](#/document/G1681528).

steps.title: Reseal and install the front cover
steps.body:
1. Fit a new coolant-pipe seal using **205-150/205-153**. Install **307-399** alignment pins. Check the two block locating dowels are seated correctly.
2. With the faces prepared, apply the specified **TA-357 / WSE-M4G323-A6 RTV**: a **3.0 mm** bead on the cover sealing faces including inner bolt bosses; **5.5 mm** beads at the illustrated head/block and oil-pan/block junctions. Do not replace the mapped bead path with a coating over the whole cover.
3. Position the cover and install the initial bolts at **3 Nm / 27 lb-in**. Remove the alignment pins and install the remaining bolts. The cover and initial bolts must be in place within **4 minutes** of initial RTV application; finish the remaining bolts within **35 minutes**. If either limit is exceeded, remove the sealant, clean and start again.
4. Use the numbered **22-position front-cover map** for these stages:

| Stage | Fasteners | Tightening |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Bolts 1–21 | 10 Nm / 89 lb-in |
| 2 | Bolts 1–20 | 24 Nm / 18 lb-ft |
| 3 | Bolt 21 | 20 Nm / 177 lb-in |
| 4 | Bolt 21 | Additional 90° |
| 5 | Bolt 22 | 10 Nm / 89 lb-in |
| 6 | Bolt 22 | Additional 45° |

5. Fit the upper-intake support bracket and its bolt finger-tight. Install its stud bolt at **8 Nm / 71 lb-in**. Reposition the generator and tighten its bolt/nut to **47 Nm / 35 lb-ft**. Refit the accessory tensioner at **11 Nm / 97 lb-in**.

Reference: [front cover, RTV path, alignment pins and bolt map](#/document/G1681517). These front-cover stages are not the cylinder-head bolt sequence.

steps.title: Refit the coolant pump and thermostat housing
steps.body:
Fit a **new pump gasket and O-ring**, lubricating the O-ring with clean specified coolant. Install the pump and its seven bolts in the illustrated order: **10 Nm / 89 lb-in, then 45°**. Fit the pump pulley with its bolts finger-tight for now.

Install a **new thermostat-housing O-ring**, lubricated with clean specified coolant. Refit the housing and tighten its four bolts in the illustrated sequence: **8 Nm / 71 lb-in, then 45°**. Reconnect the coolant hoses and clamps. Remove any belt-protection plastic after the spill risk is over. The pump-pulley bolts are tightened later, after the accessory belt is back on.

References: [pump, seven-bolt order](#/document/G1694559), [thermostat housing, four-bolt order](#/document/G1694563).

steps.title: Install the front seal, crank pulley and both belts
steps.body:
1. Lubricate the front-seal bore with clean specified engine oil. Install the **new front seal** using **303-102 and 303-1251**.
2. Lubricate the seal and pulley as specified, then install the pulley using **303-335 and 303-102**. Use a strap wrench to hold it while installing the washer and **new crank-pulley bolt**.
3. Tighten that new bolt in four stages: **120 Nm / 89 lb-ft → loosen one full turn → 50 Nm / 37 lb-ft → 90°**.
4. Refit the stretchy A/C belt using its specific routing illustration. Slide it between the crank pulley and accessory tensioner, position it behind the crank pulley, then onto the compressor pulley as shown. The source uses “accessory drive belt ribs” in two lines of this A/C-belt procedure; treat the illustration and A/C-belt context as the routing reference, not as a new instruction to fit the other belt there.
5. Position the A/C belt over the top of the crank pulley and secure it through the pulley spokes with a cable tie at least **3 mm / 0.12 in** wide. Keep the belt **above the oil-pan flange**. Rotate the crank **by hand clockwise 180°**, remove the tie, then turn it **by hand clockwise 360°** and verify it is seated on both pulleys. Do this only after timing is completely rebuilt.
6. Route the accessory belt correctly, rotate its tensioner counterclockwise to fit it, then release the tensioner under control. Check every groove on every pulley. Tighten the coolant-pump pulley bolts to **24 Nm / 18 lb-ft**.
7. Reconnect the degas bottle’s lower and upper hoses, remove the temporary hose clamp/isolation tool, and secure the bottle at **9 Nm / 80 lb-in**. Do not fill/start yet.

References: [front seal/pulley](#/document/G1681513), [A/C belt routing](#/document/G1688123), [accessory belt](#/document/G1688121), [pump pulley](#/document/G1694559), [bottle](#/document/G1694561).

steps.title: Fit new valve-cover gaskets and reinstall both covers
steps.body:
The head gasket is now clamped below the head. These are the **separate oil-sealing gaskets at the top**.

1. Clean the cover mating faces and the specified RTV junctions. Replace damaged spark-plug-tube/VCT seals with the tools listed in the cover procedures; undamaged seals do not automatically require replacement.
2. For each cover, apply an **8 mm / 0.31 in bead of TA-357 RTV only at the front-cover-to-cylinder-head junctions shown**. Fit a **new valve-cover gasket**, then place the cover without dislodging it or stressing the VCT solenoids.
3. Tighten the valve-cover bolts to **10 Nm / 89 lb-in** using that cover’s illustration. Install the cover and finish tightening within **4 minutes** of its sealant application. If you miss that window, remove the sealant, clean and reapply.
4. Confirm the VCT seals sit below the top of the solenoid electrical connectors; an incorrectly seated seal can leak oil.
5. **LH:** restore its harness retainers, VCT connectors and oil-pressure-switch connector. Reattach the fuel/EVAP tube retainer, dipstick and crankcase vent tube.
6. **RH:** refit the heater-tube retainer to the cover stud and tighten its bolt to **23 Nm / 17 lb-ft**. Restore its harness retainers, VCT connectors and PCV tube.

Finish tightening the upper-intake support-bracket bolt to **10 Nm / 89 lb-in** at the point specified by the front-cover procedure. References: [LH cover](#/document/G1681530), [RH cover](#/document/G1681531), [front-cover final bracket fastening](#/document/G1681517).

steps.title: Refit the coils, upper intake and air duct
steps.body:
1. Replace damaged coil boots, then seat the coils in their correct locations. Install each coil bolt at **7 Nm / 62 lb-in, then 50°**, and reconnect the coil plugs.
2. With the RH coils now installed, fit **new upper-intake gaskets**. Refit the upper manifold and tighten its bolts using its illustrated sequence: **10 Nm / 89 lb-in, then 45°**. Tighten the upper-manifold support bolt to **10 Nm / 89 lb-in**.
3. Reconnect the throttle-body and MAP plugs, harness retainers, PCV tube, EVAP quick coupling and purge-valve plug. Restore the vacuum hose and both retainers. Confirm every connection from the removal checklist is restored.
4. Fit the air-cleaner outlet pipe, reconnect the brake-booster and crankcase-ventilation tubes and tighten its two clamps to **5.4 Nm / 48 lb-in**.

References: [coils](#/document/G1675558), [upper manifold](#/document/G1681529), [air duct](#/document/G1675695).

steps.title: Reconnect the exhaust and replace the oil/filter
steps.body: Install new catalytic-converter flange nuts on the disturbed bank at **40 Nm / 30 lb-ft** and reconnect the exhaust-sensor connectors. Drain the engine oil and tighten the drain plug to **27 Nm / 20 lb-ft**. Install a new oil filter. The supplied head procedure explicitly says **do not lubricate its seal**, and specifies **5 Nm / 44 lb-in, then 180°** for that filter installation; do not silently substitute a general oil-change habit. If your replacement filter has conflicting fitting instructions, verify the correct part and current procedure before proceeding. Refill with specified SAE 5W-20 oil; the 3.7L service-fill reference is **6.0 U.S. qt / 5.7 L including filter**, with final level confirmed correctly on the dipstick. References: [head procedure](#/document/G1681515), [3.7L specifications](#/document/G1681493).

steps.title: Refill coolant; keep the engine off for now
steps.body:
Close the radiator drain and confirm every disturbed coolant hose, pump, housing and bottle connection is restored. Use coolant approved for the vehicle’s current Ford requirement, checking concentration with a refractometer. The supplied procedure’s normal-climate range is **48/52 to 50/50 coolant/distilled water**. Its historical materials are Motorcraft Orange specifications WSS-M97B44-D/D2; do not choose or mix coolant by color alone. The **12.4 U.S. qt / 11.7 L** historical total capacity is not a command to force that much into a partly drained system.

**Preferred planning route here: vacuum filling.** Install the suitable vacuum filler and follow that tool manufacturer’s complete fill/bleed procedure, as Ford directs. Confirm the tool’s vacuum/leak checks and fill steps are completed. Do not splice in half of the non-vacuum sequence.

**For non-vacuum filling at this stage:** fill the degas bottle to MAX FILL, fit the cap fully, and leave the engine off. Complete the next step’s fuel and battery checks before the running bleed sequence. Reference: [cooling fill/bleed](#/document/G1694549).

steps.title: Restore fuel and battery power; perform the pre-start checklist
steps.body:
Reconnect the fuel-pump driver module and battery using their procedures. For repressurization, turn the ignition on, wait the specified **3 seconds**, then check for fuel leaks before starting. If any fuel connection leaks, stop and correct it before proceeding.

Before any bleed run or first start, confirm:

- Every main head-bolt pass and the separate M6 fastening are complete.
- Valve clearances and the primary/secondary timing checks are complete; holding tools and lockpins are removed.
- All towels, caps and temporary hose clamps are accounted for; no intake or fluid passage remains plugged.
- Coils, sensors, ground strap, wiring retainers, vacuum/PCV/EVAP connections and fuel connections are restored.
- Correct oil/filter are installed, the oil level is checked, and coolant is filled to the starting level for the chosen method.
- Both belts are correctly seated, the A/C-belt installation tie is removed, and the front accessories are secure.

Refit the correct underbody equipment with its illustrated fastener groups: shield **A 11 Nm / 97 lb-in, B 2 Nm / 18 lb-in**; bracket/shield assembly **C 63 Nm / 46 lb-ft, D 2 Nm / 18 lb-in**. Identify A–D from the drawing, not by bolt size guesses. References: [fuel repressurization](#/document/G1702143), [battery restoration](#/document/G1692356), [shield fasteners](#/document/G1681517).

steps.title: Complete the chosen coolant-bleeding method
steps.body:
For a vacuum refill, finish the selected tool manufacturer’s checks and the Ford procedure. If using the non-vacuum branch, now—with the engine assembled and the pre-start checklist complete—carry out the following source sequence. Never open a hot pressurized coolant cap.

1. Fill the degas bottle to MAX FILL; install the cap fully to its hard stop and turn climate control off.
2. Start and hold **3,500 rpm for 30 seconds**, then switch off and wait **1 minute** for large air pockets to purge. This one-minute pause is **not permission to open a hot cap**. Let the engine cool before opening the system; check and correct the level using Ford’s warm/cold level guidance.
3. Restart and idle to normal operating temperature, with thermostat opening confirmed in the source by at least one cooling-fan cycle.
4. Follow the source cycle: **3,500 rpm for 30 seconds → idle 30 seconds → engine off 1 minute**. The source then says to repeat that cycle a total of **5 times**. Use the complete linked branch if its cycle numbering needs clarification; never continue a bleed run through overheating or other abnormal behavior.
5. Let it cool safely before opening the cap for the final level check; top up as required and reinstall the cap.

The vacuum tool’s operating instructions and Ford’s bleed precautions are required parts of these methods, not optional reading. Reference: [complete cooling fill/bleed branches](#/document/G1694549).

steps.title: Verify the repair with leak checks, scan-tool correction and a road test
steps.body:
After completing the chosen coolant-fill/bleed method, verify stable temperature, no oil-pressure warning, no unusual mechanical noise, and no fuel, oil, coolant or exhaust leakage. Stop and investigate an abnormal condition rather than continuing the test.

Perform the **Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction** with a capable diagnostic scan tool, as required after front-cover/front-seal work. Once stationary checks are satisfactory, carry out a controlled road test. After a full cool-down, recheck oil/coolant levels and every disturbed joint, and review diagnostic codes.

Finally revisit the original fault. Was the failed gasket actually responsible, and has the overheating or mechanical cause been addressed? Record the diagnosis, bank repaired, parts, measurements and tightening/checklist completion. The repair is finished when the engine passes those checks—not merely when the last cover looks tidy. References: [head completion](#/document/G1681515), [front-cover completion](#/document/G1681517), [cooling bleed](#/document/G1694549).

diagnostics.finding: Coolant loss or overheating, but no confirmed head-to-block leak
diagnostics.meaning: External leaks, cooling-control faults or other causes may explain the symptom.
diagnostics.next: Complete cooling diagnosis before removing the head. Avoid running an engine that is overheating.

diagnostics.finding: Leak-down air reaches a neighboring cylinder or produces bubbles in the cooling circuit
diagnostics.meaning: A gasket leak is possible; a damaged casting can also create a leak path.
diagnostics.next: Use the Ford leakage interpretation and inspect the head/block before deciding which components to replace.

diagnostics.finding: Surface measurement fails, cracks are suspected, or the block limit is unresolved
diagnostics.meaning: A new gasket alone cannot establish a sound joint.
diagnostics.next: Have the casting assessed and verify the current Ford acceptance/repair specification before assembly.

diagnostics.finding: Timing marks, chain links or holding tools do not agree
diagnostics.meaning: Valve timing has not been established reliably.
diagnostics.next: Stop before cover installation or cranking. Recheck the exact 3.7L chain, VCT and camshaft branches.

verification.title: Before the first start
verification.body: Correct bank/gasket and new fasteners recorded; all five head-bolt passes completed in order; M6 tightened separately; timing marks and link counts checked; all holding tools/towels removed; cam clearances addressed; oil and coolant filled; fuel system pressurized and leak-free.

verification.title: During the stationary check
verification.body: No fuel, coolant, oil or exhaust leaks. Normal temperature behavior, no unexpected mechanical noise and no unresolved oil-pressure warning. Complete the required cooling bleed and diagnostic correction using their full procedures.

verification.title: After the road test and full cool-down
verification.body: Recheck fluid levels and joints. Confirm the original symptom has gone and the original cooling or mechanical cause has been addressed. Document the parts, measurements and diagnosis for the next service.

watchFor.title: One number applied to every fastener
watchFor.body: The eight main head bolts, small M6 bolt, VCT bolts, cam caps, front cover and crank pulley have different instructions. Keep the component name attached to every value.

watchFor.title: A generic coolant or filter instruction replacing the vehicle-specific one
watchFor.body: The supplied workshop and owner publications have different oil-specification revisions, and the head procedure’s filter-seal instruction is explicit. Use the current correct part/instructions; verify discrepancies instead of guessing.

watchFor.title: A “helpful” extra gasket coating
watchFor.body: The front cover requires precisely placed RTV. That does not mean the head gasket does. Follow the gasket instructions and the Ford joint-specific procedure.

notes: Reference hierarchy: the VIN-correct current Ford workshop procedure controls repair order, bank details and fastener values. Owner guidance covers fluids and capacities. Supplier articles explain concepts; they do not provide an alternative Mustang bolt pattern, machining allowance or torque specification.

Numerical values above were checked against the supplied 303-01B collection. The independent bolt diagrams simplify layout; verify the bank and orientation against Ford’s installation-step-2 illustration before using them. They are not to scale.

The owner reference lists oil specification WSS-M2C945-A; the later-revised head procedure lists WSS-M2C945-B1. Confirm the currently approved oil for the VIN. The block-flatness row’s inconsistent unit pairs are deliberately not republished as an acceptance limit.

This is a combined written walkthrough of the supplied procedures, with original Atlas explanations. The linked Ford location/sequence drawings remain required for physical identification; this page does not claim to replace every tooling illustration or establish applicability beyond the stated vehicle. Online references were checked October 25, 2026.

references.title: Ford · 2015 Mustang 3.7L capacities and specifications
references.description: Primary owner guidance for the 6.0-qt oil service fill, historical coolant capacity and original fluid specifications. Does not supply head-bolt or valve-timing instructions.

references.title: Fel-Pro · Torque-to-yield head bolts
references.description: Explains why new torque-to-yield bolts and the correct torque/angle process matter. General background; Ford’s 3.7L values govern this guide.

references.title: Fel-Pro · Preparing a head-gasket surface
references.description: Explains surface finish, flatness and why the gasket and casting requirements must match. Do not substitute its generic examples for the Mustang specifications.

references.title: Fel-Pro · Use and misuse of sealers
references.description: Supplier video page explaining that sealant belongs only where the particular gasket/joint requires it. Applies as background, not as a new RTV instruction for this head gasket.

303-01B · Right cylinder head. The RH sensor branch, gasket, fasteners and tightening. Installation step 2 contains the RH bolt-order illustration.
303-01B · Camshafts. Bearing-cap sequences, crankshaft freewheeling position, oil tubes, camshaft seals and clearance checks.
303-01B · Variable camshaft timing units. Secondary-chain alignment, new VCT bolts and the separate replacement-tensioner branch.
303-01B · Primary timing chain. Initial alignment, holding tools, tensioner resetting, colored links and final link-count check.

303-01B · Crankshaft front seal and pulley. Puller/installer tools, new seal and bolt, staged pulley tightening.

303-01B · Valve clearance adjustment. Measure and select the correct tappet when required.
